papers.abstract: In this paper, building on the work of Dai--Sasahira--Stoffregen, we derive constraints on the intersection forms of smooth, compact, indefinite, spin $4$-manifolds bounded by almost-rational plumbed homology spheres (AR homology spheres) using two methods. First, we use the constraints on the existence of $\operatorname{Pin}(2)$-equivariant maps between representation spheres, established by Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu in their proof of the $10/8 + 4$-inequality. Second, we compute Lin's $κo$-invariant for AR homology spheres. Combined with Lin's version of the relative $10/8$-inequality, this computation yields constraints different from those based on Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu. As applications, we give an alternative proof of the non-sliceness of the $(2n, 1)$-cables of the figure-eight knot for even $n$---a result originally proved by Kang, Park, and Taniguchi via real Seiberg--Witten theory---by showing within ordinary Seiberg--Witten theory that certain cyclic branched covers of them are nontrivial in the homology cobordism group. We also obtain new lower bounds on the minimal genus of surfaces in various $4$-manifolds bounded by knots whose double branched covers are AR homology spheres. Moreover, we provide an obstruction to smooth $4$-manifold decompositions related to the $11/8$-conjecture.

papers.title: On Talagrand Type
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $1<s<2$ and every $0<δ<1$, Rademacher type $s$ coincides with Talagrand type $(s,ψ_{s,δ})$. Together with the result of Cordero-Erausquin and Eskenazis for $s=2$, this yields the equivalence for every $1<s\le2$ and every $0<δ<1$.

papers.title: The Dynamical Radius of Comparison for C*-Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce a dynamical version $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ of the radius of comparison $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ of a unital C*-algebra, based on the dynamical Cuntz semigroup. We also give an intrinsic ordered semigroup definition, which agrees with $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ when $A$ is residually stably finite, and is lower semicontinuous for equivariant direct limits with injective unital maps. We construct actions $α$ of $G = \mathbb{Z} / 2 \mathbb{Z}$ on simple unital AH~algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and actions $α$ of a finite group $G$ on unital C*-algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (C^* (G, A, α))$. For a minimal action of a countable discrete group $G$ on a zero dimensional compact metrizable space $X$, and with $α$ being the corresponding action on $C (X)$, we prove that $\operatorname{rc} (C (X), α) = 0$ if and only if the action on~$X$ has dynamical comparison as defined by Kerr. For finite group actions on simple unital stably finite C*-algebras, assuming the weak tracial Rokhlin property, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, α) \leq \operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and assuming weak tracial strict approximate innerness, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, α) = \operatorname{rc} (A)$.

papers.title: A finitely generated Linear group without property (T) that is neither inner amenable nor properly proximal
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit finitely generated ICC subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb{F}_2(t))$ that is neither inner amenable nor properly proximal and does not have Kazhdan's property (T). The group is obtained by adjoining a scalar dilation to Caprace's example. In particular, this has resolved a question due to Boutonnet, Ioana, and Peterson in negative.

papers.title: Modular integrals for individual modular knots
papers.abstract: To each modular knot, we attach a weight $2$ modular integral for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ whose homogenized cycle integrals recover its linking numbers with other modular knots in $S^3$. This construction answers Choie-Zagier's question of explicitly constructing modular integrals with given rational period functions in weight $2$. Our formula applies to individual modular knots without symmetrization, thereby realizing an approach discussed but not pursued by Duke-Imamoglu-Tóth. This gives an answer to Ghys' question on pairwise linking numbers in terms of modular integrals, as sought by Simon.

papers.title: A new conformal gauge on the visual boundary of a hyperbolic group
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic re-gauging of the visual boundary, arising from the logarithmic metric on the sublinear Morse boundary introduced by Garg-Jana-Qing. For every proper geodesic hyperbolic space $X$, we prove that $d_{\mathrm{log}}(ξ,η)\asymp (1+(ξ\midη)_o)^{-θ}$. As a consequence, under the natural identification of boundaries, $d_{\mathrm{log}}$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the polynomial Floyd boundary metric associated with the radial density $g_θ(t)=(1+t)^{-1-θ}$. Every quasi-isometry between proper geodesic hyperbolic spaces induces a bi-Lipschitz map between their logarithmic boundaries with a fixed admissible exponent. For every non-elementary hyperbolic group, the logarithmic boundary is nondoubling and has infinite Hausdorff and Assouad dimensions. Nevertheless, the logarithmic re-gauging preserves Nagata (capacity) dimension and continues to recover the asymptotic dimension of the group. It also detects one-endedness through linear connectedness (bounded turning) and preserves uniform perfectness. Thus the logarithmic and visual metrics are not quasisymmetrically equivalent, although several coarse-geometric features remain visible in the logarithmic boundary.

papers.title: On an inverse boundary problem in elastodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the simultaneous identification of the Lamé parameters $λ$ and $μ$ in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity. For smooth coefficients, we establish uniqueness from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map when $μ$ is axisymmetric, admits a multiplicative or additive separation on a product domain, or is quasianalytic in one fixed direction. These results require neither smallness of $\nablaμ$ nor real analyticity of the coefficients, and impose no corresponding structural condition on $λ$. In the axisymmetric and separated cases, partial boundary data suffice to determine $μ$.

papers.title: Semiparametric Efficient Inference under Non-Informative Complex Survey Designs
papers.abstract: Under non-informative complex survey designs, dependence among sampling indicators prevents the direct application of standard i.i.d. semiparametric efficiency theory. We introduce a \emph{reference Poisson experiment}, a hypothetical i.i.d.\ experiment constructed from the limiting inclusion probabilities of the original dependent design. Under suitable conditions, the actual observed-data experiment is in fact locally asymptotically normal, with the same tangent-space geometry as the reference Poisson experiment. Consequently, the efficient influence function derived by orthogonal projection in this hypothetical i.i.d.\ setting characterizes efficient estimators under the original dependent design. This yields a systematic approach to efficiency analysis for general semiparametric full-data models and pathwise-differentiable targets under complex survey designs. Under the joint superpopulation--design law, the efficiency bounds depend on the design only through its limiting inclusion probabilities. For finite-population targets whose first-order expansions are governed by the full-data efficient influence function, the same estimators are efficient under both superpopulation and finite-population centering, with bounds linked by a Pythagorean identity yielding a generalized finite-population correction. We establish efficiency of cross-fitted mean and conditional-mean regression estimators under explicit design-specific sufficient conditions. Simulations and California Academic Performance Index data illustrate the theory.

papers.title: The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
papers.abstract: Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

papers.title: A General Inequality for Walks in Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and $w_k(G)$ denote the number of walks in $G$ of length $k$. For sequences $a_1, \cdots, a_n$ and $b_1, \cdots, b_n$ of non-negative integers such that $a_1 + \cdots + a_n = b_1 + \cdots + b_n$, we determine a simple necessary and sufficient condition on $a_1, \cdots, a_n, b_1, \cdots, b_n$ for the inequality \[ w_{a_1}(G) \cdots w_{a_n}(G) \geq w_{b_1}(G) \cdots w_{b_n}(G) \] to hold for any graph $G$.

papers.title: Control and Identification in Least-Squares Self-Tuning Regulation with Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: We study stability, minimum variance tracking and parameter identification for the Åstr{ö}m--Wittenmark self-tuning regulator with unknown input gain. Ordinary least squares (LS) estimates are used directly in certainty-equivalent control. Under the stated plant and martingale noise assumptions, we establish almost sure stability and optimal tracking for every bounded reference, provided that the gain estimates remain nonzero. When at least two parameters are estimated, all coefficient estimates are strongly consistent. The proof obtains a logarithmic information lower bound from an LS energy identity and uses it to establish gain consistency without assuming closed-loop stability. For at least two estimated parameters and every bounded reference, the squared error is almost surely $O(\log\log n/n)$ for the estimated ratios of the plant coefficients to the input gain and $O(\log\log\log n/\log n)$ for the full parameter estimate. A law of the iterated logarithm shows that the latter rate is sharp under zero reference. The bound for the full parameter estimate improves with reference energy, which also appears explicitly in the logarithm law for cumulative squared tracking residuals. These results show that optimal tracking can coexist with substantially slower estimation of the full parameter vector than of the coefficient ratios used in feedback. For at least two estimated parameters, a chi-square limit yields asymptotically exact confidence ellipsoids for every bounded reference.

papers.title: Liouville regular Jordan curves
papers.abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.

papers.title: pqSEDMD: Subspace Methods for Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition Identification
papers.abstract: The dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), along with its variant for nonlinear systems, the extended DMD (EDMD), are powerful tools for the extraction of meaningful spatio-temporal characteristics of (non)linear dynamical systems from measurement data. Despite some efforts to handle the identification task when dealing with real-world data, the decomposition based methods face a critical challenge: real-world data has two inherent sources of uncertainty, the process and measurement noise. Subspace identification methods, are robust tools able to provide accurate state-space models for multi-variable linear systems directly from input-output data. Combining these two methods, we introduce the p-q quasi-norm Subspace Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (pqSEDMD). An algorithm that uses our previous improvements to the EDMD by the use of a p-q-quasi-norm reduction on an orthogonal polynomial basis, the pqEDMD algorithm, along with subspace identification methods. The result is a robust approximation of nonlinear systems in a linear function space, combining the strengths of the two methodologies. Throughout the paper we will use the Duffing oscillator as a benchmark problem to show the effectiveness of the algorithm and illustrate many important aspects related to the development.

papers.title: Inverse theorems and non-arithmetic critical pairs for restricted sumsets in $\mathbb{Z}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $A,B\subset\mathbb{Z}_p$ be nonempty with $|A|\neq|B|$, and let $A\rplus B$ be the set of sums $a+b$ with $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and $a\neq b$. Alon, Nathanson and Ruzsa proved $|A\rplus B|\ge\min\{p,|A|+|B|-2\}$. Liu and Qian conjectured that when $|A|+|B|\le p$ equality forces $A$ and $B$ to be arithmetic progressions with a common difference, with $B$ the first or the last $|B|$ terms of $A$. We refute the conjecture. For every prime $p\ge11$ there is a critical pair with $|A|+|B|=p$, $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ and neither set an arithmetic progression, and for $p=13$ one with $|A|+|B|=p-2$. These pairs satisfy $|A|+2|B|\ge p+2$, and the inequality $|A+B|\le|A\rplus B|+|A\cap B|$ shows that no counterexample can do better. We conjecture that every critical pair with $|A|+2|B|\le p+1$ is arithmetic, and prove this when $|A+B|=|A|+|B|-1$. In the conjectured range the statement is equivalent to the minimality of the ordinary sumset, to a defect of one element, and to the emptiness of the band $|A|+|B|\le|A+B|\le p-1$. We also describe all critical pairs with $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ at $p=|A|+2|B|-2$, and prove that every critical pair satisfies $|A\cap(A+t)|\ge|A|-|B|$ for $t\in B-B$ and that one with a uniquely represented restricted sum is arithmetic whenever all critical pairs with a smaller second set are.

papers.title: Reduction Modulo Binary Polynomials with Logarithmic Feedback Depth
papers.abstract: Polynomial modular reduction is central to binary finite-field arithmetic and repeated Frobenius powering. Top-down shift/XOR folding can use few operations when the nonleading support is sparse, but a tap near the leading term creates a long feedback chain. We formulate this recurrence as inversion of a nilpotent shift operator and factor its inverse by characteristic-two Frobenius powers. The resulting Frobenius-factorized reduction (FFR) applies to every monic binary modulus without materializing a reciprocal or dense reduction matrix, and its shifts can be generated online without a persistent modulus-specific schedule. For degree $m$ and nonempty nonleading support of size $s$, with nearest-tap distance $Δ_{\min}$, FFR uses exactly $\lceil\log_2(m/Δ_{\min})\rceil$ sequential feedback stages and has scheduled work $O(ms(1+\log(m/s)))$. A portable-C evaluation on 1,096 supports through degree $131072$ identifies distinct FFR, López--Dahab, and gf2x-backed Barrett regions. On four certified irreducible moduli, FFR makes complete Rabin irreducibility testing $1.35$--$8.04$ times faster than NTL and $1.60$--$6.81$ times faster than the matched Barrett implementation.

papers.title: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

papers.title: The Constant in Thomae-Type Formulas for Eight Points on the Complex Projective Line
papers.abstract: We consider the family of cyclic fourfold covers $C(x)$ of the complex projective line branched at eight points $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_8)$. It is known that the period map identifies the configuration space $X(2,8)$ of the branch points with a Zariski open subset of a quotient of the five-dimensional complex ball, and that the inverse of the period map is expressed projectively by $105$ automorphic forms $f_J$, which are proportional to the signed branch-point polynomials $\hat x_J$ with a common scalar factor. We normalize an element $ω$ of the one-dimensional eigenspace of the deck transformation group acting on the holomorphic differentials on $C(x)$. For the period $η$ of $ω$, we determine the common scalar factor: it is the product of a constant expressed in terms of the gamma function and the square of a quadratic form in $η$.

papers.title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Thermoacoustically Unstable Flames Via Non-Drifting Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: In this work, Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS) of thermoacoustically unstable free flames in closed-open tubes are presented. Simulations demonstrate nonlinear saturation of the primary instability as the flame flattens, resulting in a quasiperiodic acoustic limit cycle. Acoustic forcing is used to trigger secondary parametric instability, causing an oscillatory flame fingering characteristic of the unsteady Rayleigh-Taylor effect. To reduce computational cost, we perform DNS only on the region surrounding the flame. Acoustics at in- and outflows are described using the Navier-Stokes Characteristic Boundary Condition (NSCBC) method to model their delayed reentry into the domain in a formulation referred to as the Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Condition (ADCBC) method. A new Averaged Proportional and Integral Linear Relaxation (APILR) method is also introduced, which modifies the Classic Linear Relaxation (CLR) method to maintain time-averaged values of inflow velocity and outflow pressure. Many moving averages may be used consecutively to increase the damping rate of boundary reflection coefficients. An integral control term is used to remove non-zero equilibrium time-averaged inflow velocities which adversely affect control over flame position in the DNS region. Both new boundary methods demonstrate their capability in inert and counterflow flames test cases. In the case of a 100 cm long tube, these methods enable the numerical simulation of combustion instabilities at 98% reduced computational expense.

papers.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function is $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$
papers.abstract: We prove a weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal function with respect to Euclidean balls with dimensional dependence $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$. This improves the order of growth in the classical $O(n)$ estimate of Stein and Strömberg. The proof goes through a pointwise bound of the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator by the heat maximal operator with $\sqrt{n}$ loss. The key technical aspect of our result is an improvement of the weak-type bound for the heat maximal operator from $O(\sqrt{n})$ to $O(\log n)$.

papers.title: Homology of non-matching complexes under edge additions and applications to their Stanley-Reisner ideals
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph $G$ and an integer $t\geq 2$, we study the $t$-non-matching complex $\NM_t(G)$ and its Stanley-Reisner ideal. We prove that, if adding an edge $e$ to $G$ preserves bipartiteness, the inclusion $\NM_t(G)\hookrightarrow\NM_t(G+e)$ induces an injection on reduced homology in degree $2t-3$. If $G$ contains a cycle of length at least $2t$, then $\NM_t(G)$ has Leray number $2t-2$, and its Stanley-Reisner ideal has regularity $2t-1$. We also obtain explicit lower bounds for certain graded Betti numbers and the projective dimension of this ideal. If $G$ contains a $2t$-cycle, we determine the maximal shifts of this ideal through homological degree $|E(G)|-2t+1$. For the complete bipartite graph $G=K_{r, s}$ with $2\leq t\leq r\leq s$, we determine the depth, projective dimension, all maximal shifts, and the unique extremal Betti number of the associated ideal, thereby settling a conjecture on facet ideals of chessboard complexes.

papers.title: Two problems about bases and independent sets in free groups
papers.abstract: We will answer a problem of Dotsenko that asks for a tight upper bound on the rank of subgroups given a maximum length for its generators. Then, we will use the same tools to answer a longstanding problem of Grigorchuk in the 10th edition of the Kourovka notebook. We accomplish this using Stallings foldings and simple graph theory.

papers.title: Spectral Geroch conjecture and noncompact area enlargeable summands
papers.abstract: We study complete metrics on area enlargeable manifolds through the spectral constant $Λ_γ(g)$, the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient of $-Δ+γ\mathrm{scal}_g$ over compactly supported functions. We prove that every complete metric on an area enlargeable $m$-manifold, $m\ge2$, satisfies $Λ_γ(g)\le0$ for all $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. For an area enlargeable manifold $M_1$ and an oriented manifold $M_2$ of the same dimension, we prove that $M_1\#M_2$ is area enlargeable if and only if $M_2$ admits a spin covering. Both summands may be noncompact. Consequently, if the universal covering of $M_2$ is spin, then $M_1\#M_2$ carries neither a complete metric of positive scalar curvature nor a complete metric with positive $γ$-spectral constant for $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. The threshold $(m-1)/(4m)$ is optimal. At the endpoint, the obstruction holds for metrics whose scalar curvature is bounded from below, but explicit complete warped metrics on $\mathbf{T}^{m-1}\times\mathbf{R}$ show that it fails in general. We also prove that the locally constant and the classical formulations of area enlargeability coincide in dimensions at least two.

papers.title: Asymptotics for Model Selection in Probabilistic Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: The probabilistic formulation of principal component analysis promises statistically grounded solutions to the problem of selecting the number of principal components. However, developing tractable model selection methods is complicated by the fact that the probabilistic principal component analysis (PPCA) model exhibits non-standard large sample asymptotics at model singularities, where the Fisher information matrix does not have full rank. In this work, tools from singular learning theory are used to provide a complete description of the marginal likelihood asymptotics for PPCA. The singular Bayesian information criterion (sBIC) along with our asymptotic results provides an effective procedure for selecting the number of principal components. In particular, the sBIC corrects for the overpenalization of the standard dimension-based BIC, which leads to too few principal components being selected, while also selecting the smallest true model with probability converging to one. Our framework extends beyond PPCA, where we also provide expressions for the sBIC that can be used to select between PPCA and factor analysis models. In both simulations and on real data the effectiveness of the proposed sBIC methodology is demonstrated.

papers.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.

papers.title: Characterization of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule and lattice points in flagged hive polytopes
papers.abstract: We have previously, for a given positive integer $n$, explicitly characterized by certain linear inequalities the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux of shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ produced by $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson (LR) rule. We now extend that characterization for lower shape lengths. Then using the composition of promotion operators defining the Naito-Suzuki-Watanabe bijection between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux, we also explicitly characterize by certain linear inequalities the corresponding $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux when the shape length is $2n$ or $2n-1$. In addition, when the given $n$ is $3$ or $ 4$ the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and the $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux are characterized by linear inequalities for lower shape lengths. Since recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule are in natural bijection with Littlewood-Richardson-Sundaram (LRS) tableaux, we relate our results on the inverse quantum LR rule with other two bijections for the Naito-Sagaki conjecture and establish bijections between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux, $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux and the lattice points in a (disjoint) union of flagged hive polytopes.

papers.title: Self-injective dimensions and Iyama grade dualities over Noether algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an algebra module-finite over a commutative Noetherian ring. We first establish a local criterion for the $n$-Gorenstein condition in terms of the grades and flat dimensions of injective envelopes of simple modules over central localizations. As a main application, we give an affirmative answer, in this module-finite setting, to a question of Huang on the symmetry of finite self-injective dimension under the Auslander condition. We also show that $A$ is Auslander--Gorenstein if and only if it is Iwanaga--Gorenstein and has the fiberwise Iyama grade duality. For Cohen--Macaulay algebras, central regular reductions to Artin algebras allow both the Auslander condition and the grade duality to be tested on simple modules over $A$ itself.

papers.title: Sampling Luck Masquerades as Allocation Gain: Auditing Test-Time Budget Allocation for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) solvers report the best of many sampled solutions per instance, and the sample count is, by convention, identical for every instance. Whether a non-uniform allocation of a fixed total budget would buy anything has not been measured. We measure it, and we audit the measurement itself. First, on in-distribution workloads the allocation headroom is not detectable. Across three pretrained solvers (POMO, AM, SymNCO) on uniform TSP-100, an oracle allocation computed and evaluated on the same stored samples reports a 2.2-2.6% gain with intervals excluding zero; measured out of sample the same gain is indistinguishable from zero (0.457, 0.015, -0.512 percent). Following the customary in-sample procedure, all three solvers would have supported a published 2%-level gain that does not exist. We calibrate this bias against an instance-wise null in which the true gain is zero by construction; over the ranges we test it does not shrink with more samples or more instances. Second, the same correction that removes the phantom gains preserves a real one. Under distribution shift (a workload mixing uniform and clustered instances), a pre-registered confirmatory experiment finds that allocation guided by held-out sample statistics improves best-of-k by 11.5% (AM, primary endpoint; 95% CI [7.4, 19.7]) and 12.0% (SymNCO, replication) at equal evaluation budget, with the signal-acquisition cost not charged; a pre-registered negative control (POMO, an order of magnitude more robust to shift) shows -0.3% [-0.7, 0.24]. The gain exceeds a frozen distribution-label baseline by 4.2 points [1.9, 7.7]. An exploratory policy charging a 20-sample probe against the same budget retains 3.4% (AM) and 4.6% (SymNCO). We give a correction procedure and a reporting checklist, and release all data, code, and the pre-registration record.

papers.title: CS-PIKAN: Curvilinear Separable Physics-Informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Autograd-Based Metric Evaluation and Certified Error Bounds for PDEs on Complex Domains
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (PIKANs) offer effective neural solvers for partial differential equations (PDEs), but their conventional formulations rely on Cartesian domains and scattered collocation points, often resulting in high computational costs, approximate boundary enforcement, and no rigorous error guarantees. We introduce CT-PIKAN, which maps curvilinear domains to the unit square and computes all geometric quantities, including those required by the Laplace-Beltrami operator, through automatic differentiation. Building on this transformation, Curvilinear Separable PIKAN (CS-PIKAN) represents solutions as rank-R sums of products of one-dimensional KANs with topology-adapted bases (Fourier for periodic and Chebyshev for bounded coordinates and time). A separable envelope and transfinite lift enforce boundary and initial conditions exactly, while a single sqrt{g}-weighted residual is minimized on a stratified tensor grid, reducing network cost from the product to the sum of grid sizes. We derive a metric-explicit Poincar'e constant, establish computable a-posteriori error bounds for elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic problems, and prove that the loss provides an unbiased estimator of the squared residual norm underlying these bounds. Nine benchmarks cover advection, Poisson, and heat conduction on Cartesian, polar, wavy, annular, star-shaped, and sampled-boundary domains. Across three seeds, CS-PIKAN reduces the relative L2 error of CT-PIKAN by factors of 7-126 at equal or lower training cost (up to 10 times faster), with all certified bounds satisfied. Ablations highlight the importance of exact periodicity and boundary constraints; KAN factors outperform MLPs for transport-dominated problems but not smooth elliptic ones. Nevertheless, classical body-fitted solvers remain substantially cheaper at comparable accuracy for these two-dimensional linear problems.

papers.title: On the absence of point defects in biaxial Landau--de Gennes models
papers.abstract: We study local minimizers of a sextic-potential Landau--de Gennes energy for nematic liquid crystals in the small-elastic-constant limit. Under the uniform energy and $L^\infty$ bounds, these minimizers converge to a locally energy-minimizing harmonic map $\mathbf{Q}_0$ into a biaxial vacuum manifold. The main result of this paper is that such a limiting map $\mathbf{Q}_0$ has no interior point singularities. The proof relies on a geometric identification of the lifted Frobenius metric on the universal cover $\mathbb{S}^3$ with a rescaled Berger metric. For a hypothetical tangent cone at a point singularity, its link is a nonconstant harmonic two-sphere into the Berger sphere. We construct a smooth variation field adapted to the Hopf direction and show that it induces a quantitative instability estimate, in contradiction with the shifted stability inequality inherited from local minimality. This replaces the usual round-sphere test fields by a target-specific construction and rules out interior point defects in the biaxial setting. The result is sharp in view of the well-known existence of point defects in the uniaxial theory.

papers.title: Extremely proximal actions and primitivity of group rings
papers.abstract: We present a purely dynamical criterion for the primitivity of group rings. To be precise, we show that if $G$ is a countable group that admits a topologically free, extremely proximal action, then the group ring $KG$ is primitive for any field $K$. Our criterion recovers several of the existing results on primitivity and applies to new examples, such as the commensurator groups of torsion-free non-elementary hyperbolic groups, some Kac-Moody groups, and other weakly hyperbolic groups.

papers.title: Precise cover times for branching random walks on Hamming graphs: (iterated) logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract: We prove tight asymptotics of the cover time $τ_{\mathrm{cov}}(d)$ of a continuous-time branching random walk on the Hamming graph $\{0,1,\dots,b-1\}^d$, as $d\to\infty$. We focus on the slow-branching regime, where particles move at rate one and branch at rate $λ\in(0,1)$. For $b>2$, we show that $τ_{\mathrm{cov}}(d)=x_\star d+λ^{-1}\log d+O_{\mathbb P}(1)$. For $b=2$, we show that $τ_{\mathrm{cov}}(d)=x_\star d+χ^{-1}\log\log d+O_{\mathbb P}(1)$. Here, $x_\star$ and $χ$ are explicit positive constants depending only on $b$ and $λ$. Our results sharpen previously known linear-order estimates. The dichotomy reflects the geometry of the last uncovered region: for $b>2$, there are exponentially many antipodes, whereas the binary hypercube has a unique antipode and its neighbors govern the final coverage. Our proofs combine classic spine change of measure techniques and many-to-few estimates with a multiscale decomposition of the genealogy and a weighted martingale analysis of the early population.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Probability Measure of a Multi-group Curie-Weiss Model with Interacting Groups
papers.abstract: We study the problem of reconstructing the probability measure of a multi-group version of the Curie-Weiss or mean-field model of ferromagnetism from a sample of the voting behaviour of the population. While originally used to study phase transitions in statistical mechanics, the Curie-Weiss model has been applied to study phenomena where many agents interact with each other, in particular in case of a heterogeneous population with identifiable subpopulations. The degree of social cohesion within social groups manifests in the way the members of the group influence each others' decisions as well as how they behave under outside influence from voters belonging to another group. While the maximum likelihood estimator of the coupling parameters has desirable statistical properties in theory, computational challenges make applications to larger populations impractical. Therefore, we analyse an estimator based on asymptotic approximations to the behaviour of the Curie-Weiss model valid for large populations. Due to the wide application of models such as Curie-Weiss, the estimator is potentially useful in disciplines such as political science, sociology, automated voting, and preference aggregation.

papers.title: Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\R^4$
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the algebraic and differential geometric properties of smooth mappings between domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$, classifying them according to the constant ranks of their holomorphic and antiholomorphic derivative components. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$, where both block matrices $A$ and $B$ have rank 1. We characterise the set of SPCR linear automorphisms as a 12-dimensional submanifold of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{C})^2$ and analyse its underlying CR structure, demonstrating its geometric and structural rigidity.

papers.title: A sharp inverse theorem for the quadratic large sieve
papers.abstract: We prove that if $A\subseteq[N]$, $|A|\gg\sqrt N$, and $|A_p|\le p/2+O(1)$ for every prime $p\ll\log N$, then $A$ contains at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log N}/\log\log N)$ elements in the image of a single integral quadratic $m\pm x^2$. A matching construction shows that this is optimal even when the quadratic may be chosen arbitrarily in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

papers.title: The curvature of left-invariant magnetic systems
papers.abstract: We compute the magnetic curvatures (in the sense of Assenza) of left-invariant magnetic systems on Lie groups and explore relations between curvature properties and algebraic properties, extending to the magnetic setting a number of results from Milnor's classic 1976 paper on the geometry of left-invariant metrics. We also discuss the existence of non-trivial bi-invariant magnetic systems and exhibit the resulting curvature formulas in some concrete examples, including the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Annealed Gibbs Measures with Data-Driven Interaction Potentials on Hierarchical Structures
papers.abstract: We construct annealed Gibbs measures on continuous interaction parameters and binary spins on Cayley trees of order $k\geq 1$, with coupling functions determined by an empirical loss. The interaction parameters and spins are distinct random variables: the former determine edge couplings, while the latter represent binary labels. The training data specify the coupling function and the joint Gibbs specification, rather than automatically selecting a unique Gibbs measure on interaction parameters. We derive necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for the finite-volume joint densities. These conditions take the form of nonlinear integral equations for boundary laws and characterize the splitting annealed Gibbs measures constructed here. For $k=1$, the translation-invariant equations reduce to positive compact integral operators. Under the stated hypotheses, they have a unique normalized positive solution. For $k=2$, an explicit empirical-loss kernel reduces the translation-invariant equations to polynomial equations. In this case, we show that hierarchical learning systems may exhibit phase-transition phenomena: for certain empirical kernels on Cayley trees order two, multiple Gibbs measures on spins emerge beyond a critical inverse temperature, corresponding to distinct equilibrium prediction regimes. For a selected annealed Gibbs measure, we distinguish its marginal on interaction parameters from its conditional Gibbs measures on spins at fixed interaction parameters. Our results provide a new perspective on energy-based learning, where data do not merely determine an optimal model through minimization but define an entire probabilistic landscape of possible inference states.

papers.title: On the Benign Optimization Landscape and Geometry of Heteroscedastic Probabilistic PCA
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the global optimization landscape and local geometry of heteroscedastic probabilistic principal component analysis (HePPCA). Since the signal strengths and noise variances are often unknown in practice, we analyze a formulation that uses fixed plug-in estimates of these parameters. We first show that the population HePPCA problem is an instance of a homogeneous quadratic program with orthogonality constraints (QPOC). For QPOC, we first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for a critical point to be a global maximizer and explicitly construct a positive-curvature direction at every nonglobal critical point. This establishes a benign optimization landscape of QPOC in which every critical point is either a global maximizer or a strict saddle point. Building on this analysis, we establish quantitative curvature bounds for population HePPCA, yielding local geodesic strong concavity near every global maximizer and uniformly positive curvature in suitable tangent directions at all nonglobal critical points. Combining these results with a deterministic perturbation argument and sample covariance concentration bounds, we derive a sufficient sample-size condition under which empirical HePPCA inherits the benign landscape and local geodesic strong concavity with high probability. Finally, we present numerical experiments to corroborate our theoretical results.

papers.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For a central division $F$-algebras $L$ of a fixed degree $n$ we identify the double quotients of the homogeneous spaces $L_E^\times/L^\times$ with a topological space $Ξ_E$ which does not depend on a choice of $L$ , define a convolution products $\ast _L$ on the space ${\mathcal M} _E$ compactly supported measures on $Ξ_E$ and conjecture that the product $\ast _L$ on $Ξ_E$ does not depend on a choice of $L$.

papers.title: Consecutive integers free of certain prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $n_k$ denote the least integer $n>2k$ such that $(n-k)(n-k+1)\cdots(n-1)$ is not divisible by any prime in the interval $(k,2k)$. Confirming a conjecture of Erdős, we prove that, for all sufficiently large $k$, $$ n_k > e^{\frac{\log^2 k}{20 \log \log k}}. $$

papers.title: Learning Locally Stable Neural ODEs and Their Regions of Attraction
papers.abstract: We propose a class of neural ODEs that are hard-constrained to have a locally exponentially stable equilibrium point at the origin, with an exactly characterized region of attraction. The model obtains its dynamics by passing an arbitrary neural vector field through a projection layer defined by a jointly learned Lyapunov function. By design, this function satisfies a variant of the Zubov equation for the projected dynamics and is therefore a maximal Lyapunov function for the projected system. As a result, the projected dynamics are locally exponentially stable at the origin, and the region of attraction is exactly given by the 1-sublevel set of the Lyapunov function. We prove that this model class universally approximates any sufficiently smooth dynamics that are locally exponentially stable at the origin on their region of attraction, and propose an implementation that is consistent with the theory. The approach is validated experimentally on nonlinear systems with nonconvex regions of attraction.

papers.title: Subhypergraph counts and proofs of two conjectures of Alon
papers.abstract: For a fixed integer $r\ge2$ and a finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ without isolated vertices, let $N_r(m,H)$ be the maximum number of unlabelled copies of $H$ among all finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $m$ edges. Friedgut and Kahn [Isr. J. Math., 1998] proved that $N_r(m,H)=Θ_H(m^{ρ^*(H)})$, where $ρ^*(H)$ is the fractional edge-cover number of $H$. We sharpen this to $N_r(m,H)=(λ_r(H)+o(1))m^{ρ^*(H)}$ as $m\to\infty$, with $λ_r(H)>0$, and characterize the limiting $λ_r(H)$ by a variational problem over finite hypergraphs. We develop a globally rainbow compression argument combining color-coding with successive vertex cloning. In particular, when $r=2$, the asymptotic formula confirms a conjecture of Alon [Isr. J. Math., Conjecture 1, 1986]. Moreover, for graphs we express the limiting constant $λ_2(H)$ as a supremum over finite cores. We also prove that, for every prescribed number of edges, an extremal graph for a star forest can be chosen to be a star forest, confirming another conjecture of Alon [Isr. J. Math., Conjecture 2, 1986].

papers.title: The Loss of Tension in an Infinite Membrane with Holes of Decaying Spatial Density
papers.abstract: What is the effect of randomly removing material from an infinite stretched membrane? Under what conditions can the membrane still sustain tension? This problem was introduced by Robert Connelly in connection with applications of rigidity theory in the natural sciences, and was later studied in M. V. Menshikov, K. A. Rybnikov, and S. E. Volkov, "The loss of tension in an infinite membrane with holes distributed according to a Poisson law" (2002); a discrete version was also considered in Robert Connelly, Konstantin Rybnikov, and Stanislav Volkov, "Percolation and the Loss of Tension in an Infinite Triangular Lattice" (2001). We study a mathematical framework based on a non-homogeneous Poisson point process whose intensity $λ$ tends to zero at infinity. The hole shapes are i.i.d.\ and independent of their locations. We show that if the intensity does not decay too quickly, then tension is still lost throughout the whole plane, as in the homogeneous model studied in 2002. Conversely, we give sufficient conditions under which complete loss of tension does not occur. Thus, both destruction and non-destruction regimes are possible even when the intensity tends to zero, indicating a phase transition in the model. The processes studied here are closely related to bootstrap percolation.

papers.title: Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension
papers.abstract: Consider the following plaquette model from statistical physics: a lamp lies at every vertex of the triangular lattice and a switch lies at every even vertex of the (bipartite) dual hexagonal lattice. Each switch toggles the three lamps on its face. The energy of a configuration is the number of ON lamps. For the Glauber dynamics associated with the Gibbs measure defined by this Hamiltonian at any inverse temperature $β>0$, we show that, in any dimension $d\ge 2$, the infinite volume relaxation time satisfies \[e^{β^2/C}/C \le T_{\mathrm{rel}}\le Ce^{e^{Cβ}}\] for some $C>0$. Our result entails that the Gibbs measure is unique. The $e^{β^2}$ scaling was conjectured by Garrahan and Newman in 2000 and matches the behaviour of supercritical rooted kinetically constrained models such as the East model, thus recovering fragile glass phenomenology in the absence of kinetic constraints. More precisely, we show that, on a torus of side length $2^k$, when $β\to\infty$ and $k/β\to0$, we have $T_{\mathrm{rel}}=e^{2βk(1+o(1))}$, confirming a prediction of Newman and Moore. Quite surprisingly, however, we also prove that, on non-periodic finite domains of size $n\le e^{β/C}$ for large $C>0$, we have the much larger asymptotics $\ln T_{\mathrm{rel}}=βn^{Θ(1)}$. The main ingredients of the proofs are new results in extremal and enumerative combinatorics and rely on renormalisation ideas for the dynamics and its groundstates also known as the Ledrappier subshift. Our combinatorial results also have consequences in geometric group theory (more precisely to the complexity of the word problem for the Baumslag finitely presented group), ergodic theory and linear coding theory.

papers.title: On concatenation of matrices for reversible linear codes over a finite commutative ring and applications to DNA codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a generalized framework for constructing reversible linear, reversible self dual and reversible DNA codes using a matrix-theoretic approach based on involutory matrices. The proposed concatenation scheme gives a large class of generator matrices and yields codes with good parameters. The construction is carried out at the level of linear codes and then extended to DNA codes. Using a matrix product approach, we provide a unified method for analysis and proof. Further, we resolve an open problem raised by Oztas et.al. and also we correct and improve some results of them.

papers.title: Bidirectional Random Projections
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes bidirectional random projections for ordinary least squares (OLS) regression under the fixed design setting. Let $(X, Y) \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a sample and $W \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n}$, $R \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p_1}$ be two random projections. We develop an expected excess loss bound for the OLS estimator built on $(WXR, WY)$, extending an established bound for the OLS estimator built on $(XR, Y)$. Our analysis shows that our bound is larger and the gap between the two bounds decays at a rate of approximately $O(1/n_1)$. These findings are confirmed by numerical results.

papers.title: On automorphic measures, Lyapunov exponents and instability of rational maps
papers.abstract: To construct obstructions to the stability of rational maps with non-summable critical points in their Julia sets, we introduce automorphic measures with complex eigenvalues for rational maps on the Riemann sphere. In particular, these measures extend the classical notions of quasi-invariant and conformal measures by allowing the respective Radon--Nikodym derivative to be complex-valued and proportional to a multiplicative cocycle. \[ j_{(s,t)}(R) = |R'|^{s} \left(\frac{|R'|}{R'}\right)^{t}, \] which plays the role of a generalized automorphy factor in the sense of group actions. The existence of such measures reveals a close connection between geometric and dynamical properties of rational maps. We show that the existence of certain automorphic measures, particularly unimodular measures and their associated vector fields, implies instability of the corresponding rational map. Specifically, for a weakly dissipative rational map admitting a $( -1, 1)$-unimodular measure, there exists an integer $q \ge 1$ such that the map is $q$-unstable. This result generalizes earlier instability criteria involving pseudoconformal measures and connects the presence of such measures to the failure of structural stability. Furthermore, we establish ergodic and combinatorial conditions ensuring the existence of unimodular measures or vector fields -- most notably, through bounded recurrence, bounded velocity of arguments, and relations with the Milnor--Thurston kneading theory. These criteria provide a unified framework linking automorphic measures, Lyapunov spectra, and the geometric deformation spaces of rational maps.

papers.title: On the sharp linear convergence rate of the circumcentered--reflection method on subspaces
papers.abstract: For two subspaces $U,V\subseteq\RR^n$, the circumcentered--reflection method (CRM) of Behling, Bello-Cruz, and Santos~\citeyearpar{BBS2018} computes the projection onto $U\cap V$ using only the reflections across $U$ and $V$, with known linear-convergence rate equal to the cosine of the Friedrichs angle. We prove that, when CRM is initialized in $V$, it contracts at the strictly smaller rate $ρ_V=(\sin^2θ_p-\sin^2θ_F)/(\sin^2θ_p+\sin^2θ_F)$, where $θ_F\in(0,π/2]$ is the Friedrichs angle, whose cosine we denote by $c_F\coloneqq\cosθ_F$, and $θ_p\in[θ_F,π/2]$ is the largest principal angle between $U$ and $V$. The bound is sharp, attained on an explicit ray in $V$, and optimal among parameter-free single-step iterations. The constant itself is not new: Bauschke, Bello-Cruz, Nghia, Phan, and Wang~\citeyearpar{BBNPW2016} identified it as the optimal rate of the relaxed alternating-projection family and of their adaptive linesearch map $B_T$. Our contribution is that the parameter-free geometric circumcenter attains it as well, via Kantorovich's inequality applied to a single self-adjoint operator on $V$. Restricted to $V$, CRM coincides pointwise with the linesearch maps $A_T$ and $B_T$ from the Gubin--Polyak--Raik framework~\citep{GPR1967}. We further prove $ρ_V<c_F^2$ whenever $θ_F<π/2$, with one-step convergence exactly when $θ_F=θ_p$. Over-reflecting either or both of $R_U$, $R_V$ inside the circumcenter does not help. Going faster than $ρ_V$ universally requires memory: Chebyshev semi-iteration applied to $P_VP_U$ attains a strictly smaller rate, beating $ρ_V$ by a factor at most $2$, attained in the limit $θ_F\toθ_p$.

papers.title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers for Generalized Newtonian Models
papers.abstract: We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic $λ$-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the $p$-Laplacian and $p$-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for $4/3\le p\le 4$, $p\ne2$, with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.

papers.title: Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development
papers.abstract: Neurons receive information through their dendrites. During development, when synaptic connections are forming, dendrites grow, retract, and branch. The resulting dendritic tree shapes the structure of the broader neural network. Crucially, retraction and branching make it necessary to track whole dendritic paths rather than only their endpoints. While this is handled implicitly in some existing simulations, here we construct an explicitly path-valued stochastic process for dendrite growth. Combining this with a branching process, using ideas from measure-valued branching particle systems, we show that the model produces the typical tree structures of real dendrites. To complement this analytical work, we also outline several methods for numerical simulation, including time discretisations at different temporal scales and an approximation using a dynamic graph. This provides both a more rigorous mathematical framework and more structured simulation methods for modelling dendrite development.

papers.title: Jordan types for pairs of commuting nilpotent matrices: A survey
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to survey results on Jordan types for pairs of nilpotent commuting matrices. We also review recent proof of the Box Conjecture on Jordan types that have equal dense orbit in the nilpotent commutator.

papers.title: Algorithms for experimenting with Zariski dense matrix groups over number fields
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be an algebraic number field. We provide a computational analog of the strong approximation theorem for finitely generated Zariski dense groups $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{P})$, $n$ prime. That is, we present algorithms to find the set of congruence quotients of $H$ modulo all maximal ideals of a finitely generated subring $R$ of $\mathbb{P}$ such that $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,R)$. The algorithms have been implemented in GAP. Potential applications are illustrated by a range of experiments in degree $2$, with a special focus on Bianchi groups.

papers.title: Stability of Anomalous Dissipation for the Forced Three-Dimensional Navier--Stokes Equations under Geometric Perturbations
papers.abstract: The energy dissipation in the inviscid limit is a central problem in turbulence theory. Kolmogorov's 1941 (K41) theory predicts nonvanishing energy dissipation as viscosity tends to zero, a phenomenon known as anomalous dissipation. Bruè and De Lellis constructed solutions exhibiting this phenomenon, but their construction relies on precise geometric conditions. Based on quasi-self-similar mixing, we prove that anomalous dissipation persists under small pure normal perturbations of the central curves satisfying area-preserving and equal-length conditions. The perturbations vanish near the spatial endpoints and at the initial and terminal times, and smallness is measured in a mixed norm with at most two time derivatives and total order at most six. We establish stability of the area-preserving maps and full local fields, including the mixed derivatives needed for Hölder estimates of the forcing, and obtain high-frequency energy concentration. A comparison estimate and a contradiction argument give a positive dissipation lower bound uniform over the admissible perturbations. Using the $(2+\frac12)$-dimensional framework, we construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional (3D) Navier--Stokes equations with anomalous dissipation for a sequence of viscosities tending to zero.

papers.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
papers.abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(β+1)}/β}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $β^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logβ$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $β$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.

papers.title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
papers.abstract: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.

papers.title: On Minimal Observation Time for Recovering Latent Hawkes Networks
papers.abstract: Dynamics of interacting systems in engineering, society, and nature often evolve over latent networks that govern which entities can interact. We study the problem of inferring these networks from event-based observations, which arise naturally in finance, seismology, and neuroscience. While there is substantial algorithmic work addressing this important problem, theoretical results are scarce. In this paper we ask the following fundamental question: what is the minimum time that one must observe the dynamics in order to exactly recover the underlying network, as a function of the number $d$ of interacting entities? For a class of stationary Hawkes processes with sparse, weak interactions, we prove that an observation time of order $\log d$ is sufficient and necessary. For the upper bound we construct a two-stage estimator that uses clipped and binned event data for screening, followed by a least-squares refinement, and apply concentration bounds derived from the Poisson cluster representation. For the lower bound we combine Fano's inequality with Jacod's Girsanov formula for point processes on a suitable subclass of networks.

papers.title: Scalar Entropy and Source Terms in Harmonic Ricci Flow on Surfaces
papers.abstract: The modified scalar curvature $S=R-α|\nablaφ|^2$ satisfies a reaction--diffusion equation with a nonnegative source $Q$ under harmonic Ricci flow on a surface. The relative entropy of $|S|$ need not decrease for either sign of $S$. At a nonzero constant initial value its second time derivative is the spatial variance integral of $Q$, divided by $|S|$. We construct closed examples of both signs with spatially varying tension norm. For $S<0$, normalizing by the mass of $-S$ gives an exact covariance threshold for decay and a sufficient bound in terms of the variances of $\frac{Q}{-S}$ and $-S$, the scalar mass and density bounds, and the first positive eigenvalue. On a torus this variance bound gives decay even when the covariance is strictly negative. For $S>0$ we retain the source and boundary flux in the Hamilton square formula. In the fixed harmonic free-boundary disk case the source vanishes, and equality for a nonconstant map forces $S$ to be constant. The appendices give the boundary terms for the coupled Perelman functionals.

papers.title: The singular set of the superconductivity free boundary problem
papers.abstract: We prove the uniqueness and continuous dependence of blow-ups at singular points of the free boundary for the superconductivity problem. As an application, we show that the free boundary is contained in a countable union of $C^1$ submanifolds of dimension at most $n-1$.

papers.title: Affine Supertrusses and Superbraces
papers.abstract: Brzeziński's trusses are ''ring-like'' algebraic structures in which the addition is replaced with an abelian heap operation and the binary product satisfies a natural distributivity rule over the ternary addition. This paper addresses the question of how to define affine super-versions of trusses. Taking our cue from the theory of algebraic supergroups, we define an affine supertruss as a representable functor from the category of unital associative supercommutative superalgebras to the category of trusses. The representing superalgebras are equipped with a ''cotruss'' structure-a new concept in itself. We show that from an affine supertruss, provided the binary product defines a supergroup, one can construct an affine two-sided superbrace, and so generalise Rump's braces to supermathematics. As an application of these constructions, we propose a generalisation of the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation to the setting of affine superschemes via a super-version of Adler's map.

papers.title: Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls: a survey
papers.abstract: What is the largest constant $c\in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of axis-parallel squares in the plane admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $c$ of the area covered by $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T.~Radó in 1928, who was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. R.~Rado later generalized the problem from axis-parallel squares in the plane to homothetic copies of any given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where now we are looking for an optimal constant $F(K)$. In this paper we survey the literature on this problem, with a focus on the case where $K$ is a cube or a ball in the high-dimensional regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. The estimates that we currently have for cubes are much more precise than those for balls: namely if $Q^d$ is a $d$-dimensional cube, then \[ (e^{-1}+o(1))\frac{2^{-d}}{d \log{d}} \leq F(Q^d)\leq 2^{-d}, \] while denoting $B^d$ a $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball, then \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq F(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}.\] Except for the upper bound for cubes, which is classical, the other estimates are due to the authors.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation
papers.abstract: We show the existence of self-similar solutions with constant finite mass to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation for all spatial dimensions $d \ge 1$ and all exponents $m>m_c=(d-2)_+/d$. This range is optimal. We find two types of solution depending on the exponent: compactly supported solutions in the slow-diffusion range $m > 1$ and positive solutions with heavy tails in the sub-critical fast-diffusion range $m_c < m < 1$. The self-similar solutions in the linear case $m=1$ were already known explicitly obtained by the Fourier transform, and we discuss their properties in our settings and the limit $m \to 1$.

papers.title: Heisenberg vertex algebras and abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Here we construct spaces of coinvariants for Heisenberg vertex algebras on abelian varieties and show that these globalize to twisted $\mathscr{D}$-modules on moduli of abelian varieties. We recover the standard construction of these sheaves over the Torelli locus. As an example, in the case of commutative Heisenberg vertex algebras we show that the realization of coinvariants on curves as polynomial functions on one-forms extends to arbitrary abelian varieties. Similarly, we construct twisted coinvariants on the universal abelian variety and show that these recover the standard construction over the universal Jacobian.

papers.title: Motivic local density of isolated surface singularities
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated algebraic surface singularity, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. In this context, we can use an additional data: the inner rate related to the bilipschitz geometry of the singularity, as studied by A. Belotto da Silva, L. Fantini and A. Pichon.

papers.title: Regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities via Optimal Transport and Study of Equality Cases
papers.abstract: We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. Furthermore, we provide a full picture concerning the issues of finiteness of the Brascamp-Lieb constant and of the existence of Gaussian extremizers, and completely determine all optimizers. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. Finally, we give applications retrieving Brascamp-Lieb-type inequalities with respect to the Gaussian measure and a regularized hypercontractivity inequality.

papers.title: Pohozaev identities and Liouville theorems for $L$-tension energies on manifolds
papers.abstract: We study autonomous energies $B(φ,e,\|τ_L\|^2/2)$ for a general Lagrangian $L=L(y,r)$. The scaling derivative $\widehat L=2rL'$ determines the trace of the stress tensor and a vector-field identity on Riemannian domains. For homogeneous $L=a(y)(2r)^{p/2}/p$, the divergence term in this trace vanishes when $p=m$. A conformal vector field with a strictly signed conformal factor then gives $L$-harmonicity for positive mixed tension powers, under explicit integrability and flux conditions. This applies, in particular, to hyperbolic space. On complete gradient Ricci solitons with bounded Ricci curvature, a separate cutoff argument gives a global identity for general $L$. On the cigar and on Euclidean space, direct metric variations give second-order boundary criteria that also cover tension powers $1<q<2$. The applications include target weights and the fourth-power case. Examples distinguish the annular condition from global first-derivative integrability and show why scalar growth bounds or finite tension energy alone do not imply vanishing.

papers.title: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: Hausdorff dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
papers.abstract: We study the classical limiting laws of $\varphi(n)/n$ and $σ(n)/n$ over integers and shifted primes $p-1$. Let $μ_G$ denote the shifted-prime totient law and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. The law $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero, while every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-measure has packing dimension one. All four ratio laws and their logarithmic images have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions satisfying $0.550<\underline{d}_1\le\overline{d}_1<0.571$. The law $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both $μ_G$ and $μ_f$ have quantitative Fourier decay. For $μ_f$, we obtain sharp concentration asymptotics and localize maximizing intervals. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a random Euler product with an independent uniform phase. For a uniform square matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the probability of a primitive-root determinant tends, as the matrix size grows, to $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Over primes, $c(p)$ has limiting law $μ_G$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ over primes $p\le x$ converge to their common progression law with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. We also obtain transport estimates in growing progressions. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for every $A>0$, disproving the Erdős--Kátai singularity conjecture for $A>2$. Applications include extremal determinant bounds and certified prime selection without complete factorization of $p-1$. These results are unconditional; further quantitative refinements assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions.

papers.title: Toroidal families and averages of $L$-functions, II: cubic moments
papers.abstract: Generalizing our previous work on ``toroidal averages'', we study the average of special values of $L$-functions of the form $L(1/2,χ^a)L(1/2,χ^b)L(1/2,χ^c)$ for integers $a$, $b$ and $c$, where $χ$ varies over Dirichlet characters of a given prime modulus. We highlight connections with estimates for bilinear forms of trace functions and with bounds for the number of solutions of monoidal equations in three variables in small boxes over finite fields.

papers.title: The Hofstadter Consecutive-Sum Sequence Omits Infinitely Many Positive Integers
papers.abstract: We study Hofstadter's greedy self-generating sequence, which begins with 1 and 2 and repeatedly chooses the least integer larger than the preceding term that is a sum of at least two consecutive earlier terms. We prove that the excess of its $n$th term over its index is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log n$, up to an additive constant, and that the sequence satisfies a polynomial upper bound. In particular, the sequence omits infinitely many positive integers.

papers.title: Memorization capacity of deep ReLU neural networks characterized by width and depth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the memorization capacity of deep neural networks with ReLU activation. Specifically, we investigate the minimal size of such networks to memorize any $N$ data points in the unit ball with pairwise separation distance $δ$ and labels from a finite set of size $C$. Most prior studies characterize the memorization capacity by the number of parameters or neurons. We extend these results by constructing ReLU networks with adjustable width $W$ and depth $L$ satisfying $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(δ^{-1})+\log C))$ that can memorize any such dataset. We also establish width-depth lower bounds that depend explicitly on $δ$ and $C$ for networks capable of memorizing all such datasets. When $\log(δ^{-1})\asymp\log N$, our construction achieves $W^2L^2\asymp N$ for suitable choices of width and depth. This order is optimal if $\log C\asymp\log N$, and optimal up to logarithmic factors if $\log C=o(\log N)$.

papers.title: Strong Approximation for the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere
papers.abstract: We study the orbits of solutions to the Markoff-type equation $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + AX + BY + CZ + D$$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ for fixed integers $A,B,C,D$ under the group $Γ$ generated by \[\begin{split}&V_1: (x, y, z)\mapsto (A + yz - x, y, z),\\ &V_2: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, B + xz - y, z),\text{ and}\\ &V_3: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, y, C + xy - z).\end{split}\] This equation defines the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere, with $Γ$ arising from the Pure Mapping Class Group. Outside an explicit degeneracy locus, $Γ$ acts transitively on almost all solutions for a density-one set of primes independent of the parameters; the others split into small orbits reflecting finite orbits over $\mathbb{C}$. For ``degenerate'' parameters, we show there are two large orbits (most cases) or four (the rest, excluding $(0, 0, 0, 4)$) for the same primes. These results strengthen for two subfamilies. The first, $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + k,\,\,\,k\neq 4,$$ arises in the combinatorial group theory of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. Combined with Chen's work, $Γ$ acts transitively for all large primes, uniformly in $k$, so the $Q$-classification conjecture of McCullough and Wanderley holds over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for $p$ large. By Martin's work, so do their Classification and $T$-Classification Conjectures. The second, $$x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + a_1x_2x_3 + a_2x_1x_3 + a_3x_1x_2 = (3+a_1+a_2+a_3)x_1x_2x_3,$$ arises from generalized cluster algebras. Our degeneracy notion specializes to that of de Courcy-Ireland, Litman, and Mizuno, whose results similarly imply our orbit count (1, 2, or 4) for all large primes for all nondegenerate and some degenerate surfaces in that family.ds for all sufficiently large primes.

papers.title: Mean-field games with rough common noise: the linear-quadratic case
papers.abstract: Motivated by mean-field games (MFG) with common noise on the one hand and pathwise stochastic control theory on the other, we formulate here a linear-quadratic (LQ) MFG with rough common noise, along with a satisfactory well-posedness theory for the linear-quadratic case. A novel Volterra-type (or mild) formulation allows to keep technical (rough-stochastic) consideration to a minimum. We derive a characterization of the optimal state and optimal control through a rough forward-backward SDE (rough FBSDE), and provide an existence and uniqueness result under the usual assumptions. Our theory is accompanied by stability estimates with respect to initial data and common noise while we also establish continuity of what we call the Itô-Lions-Lyons map for rough mean-field games. Finally, we discuss randomization of the rough common noise under appropriate conditions on the coefficients. When the latter is given by the Stratonovich lift of a Brownian motion independent of the idiosyncratic noise, we show that solutions of the rough LQ MFG coincide with those obtained by conditioning on the common noise.

papers.title: Min-Max Connected Multiway Cut
papers.abstract: We introduce a variant of the multiway cut that we call the min-max connected multiway cut. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a set $Γ\subseteq V$ of $t$ terminals, partition $V$ into $t$ parts such that each part is connected and contains exactly one terminal; the objective is to minimize the maximum weight of the edges leaving any part of the partition. This problem is a natural modification of the standard multiway cut problem and it differs from it in two ways: first, the cost of a partition is defined to be the maximum size of the boundary of any part, as opposed to the sum of all boundaries, and second, the subgraph induced by each part is required to be connected. Although the modified objective function has been considered before in the literature under the name min-max multiway cut, the requirement on each component to be connected has not been studied as far as we know. Our main motivation for studying this problems is its close connection with the spanning tree congestion problem that has been extensively studied but on which little progress has been made. We show various hardness results for this problem, including a proof of weak NP-hardness of the weighted version of the problem on graphs with treewidth two, and $W[1]$-hardness for the problem when parameterized by the treewidth of the graph. Complementing our lower bounds tightly, we also provide a pseudopolynomial time algorithm as well as an FPTAS for the weighted problem on graphs of bounded treewidth. As a consequence of our investigation we also show that the (unconstrained) min-max multiway cut problem is NP-hard even for three terminals, strengthening the known results.

papers.title: The Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence between Gaussian distributions
papers.abstract: We study the Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence when both the source and the target are Gaussian distributions. We prove the existence of a flow that stays in the class of Gaussian distributions, and is unique in the larger class of measures with strongly-concave and smooth log-densities.
