We prove that the flow globally converges toward the target measure when the source's covariance matrix is not singular, and provide counter-examples to global convergence when it is, giving a first answer to an open question raised in [Carlier et al. 2024, \S4.2]. When the covariance matrix of the source distribution commutes with that of the target, we derive more quantitative results that showcase exponential convergence toward the target when the source and the target share their support, but dropping to sublinear rates (O(t^{-1})) if the target is concentrated on a strict subspace of the source's support.

papers.title: Time-Delayed Transformers for Data-Driven Modeling of Low-Dimensional Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose the time-delayed transformer (TD-TF), a simplified transformer architecture for data-driven modeling of unsteady spatio-temporal dynamics. TD-TF bridges linear operator-based methods and deep sequence models by showing that a single-layer, single-head transformer can be interpreted as a nonlinear generalization of time-delayed dynamic mode decomposition (TD-DMD). The architecture is deliberately minimal, consisting of one self-attention layer with a single query per prediction and one feedforward layer, resulting in linear computational complexity in sequence length and a small parameter count. Numerical experiments demonstrate that TD-TF matches the performance of strong linear baselines on near-linear systems, while significantly outperforming them in nonlinear and chaotic regimes, where it accurately captures long-term dynamics. Validation studies on synthetic signals, unsteady aerodynamics, the Lorenz '63 system, and a reaction-diffusion model show that TD-TF preserves the interpretability and efficiency of linear models while providing substantially enhanced expressive power for complex dynamics.

papers.title: An Efficient Projection Enhanced Interpolation Based Tensor Train Decomposition
papers.abstract: The tensor-train (TT) format is a data-sparse tensor representation commonly used in high dimensional data approximations. In order to represent data with interpretability in data science, researchers develop data-centric skeletonized low rank approximations. However, these methods might still suffer from accuracy degradation, nonrobustness, and high computation costs. In this paper, given existing skeletonized TT approximations, we propose a family of projection enhanced interpolation based algorithms to further improve approximation accuracy while keeping low computational complexity. We do this as a postprocessing step to existing interpolative decompositions, via oversampling data not in skeletons to include more information and selecting subsets of pivots for faster projections. We provide a priori error bounds for the projection enhanced TT format and for the proposed dimension parallel algorithm, in which the contributions of the skeleton, the oversampling, and the oblique projections appear as separate terms. We illustrate the performances of our proposed methods with extensive numerical experiments. These include up to 10D synthetic datasets such as tensors generated from kernel functions, and 4D and 6D tensors constructed from Maxwellian distribution functions that arise in kinetic theory. Our results demonstrate accuracy improvements between 2 and 100 times on tested tensors over original skeletonized TT approximations, while using a limited amount of computational resources.

papers.title: On the distribution of multiplicative energy
papers.abstract: This paper extends the investigation of energy distribution in finite settings, building on results established in our earlier work. We analyze the distribution of multiplicative energies of different orders using Fourier-analytic methods. Our results provide new structural insights into energy phenomena in finite fields, complementing earlier discrete analyses. In the last section, as a corollary, we obtain a 'sum-multiplicative energy'-type result.

papers.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{χ_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: Analytically dense Mordell-Weil rank jumps on elliptic surfaces via transverse realization
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{min},n}$ be the moduli stack of minimal Weierstrass fibrations of Faltings height $n$ over an unparameterized $\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{C}}$, and let $\mathcal{W}_n^{\mathrm{sb}}$ be its dense open substack of simply-branched Jacobian elliptic surfaces with only ${\mathop{\rm I}}_1$ singular fibres. For integers $n\ge2$ and $r$ satisfying $1\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{10n-2}{n-1}\right\rfloor$, we prove that every point of $\mathcal{W}_n^{\mathrm{sb}}$ is a limit of pairwise non-isomorphic surfaces in this locus carrying $r$ independent Mordell-Weil sections, while the least canonical height of a non-zero section tends to infinity. Thus the rank-at-least-$r$ locus is analytically dense in $\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{min},n}$. First- and second-order infinitesimal criteria also give exact rank $r$ density for $1\le r\le10$ when $n\ge3$, and for $1\le r\le18$ when $n=2$. The direct realization argument combines Shepherd-Barron's infinitesimal period calculation with a block Vandermonde minor, lattice approximation, and the holomorphic implicit function theorem, and uses neither monodromy nor o-minimality. Finally, we construct section moduli stacks of finite type parametrizing all-${\mathop{\rm I}}_1$ Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Faltings height $n$, equipped with $r$ ordered non-zero sections of fixed canonical heights. At the constructed surfaces and sections, these algebraic stacks are smooth of dimension $10n-2-r(n-1)$, and their germs after base change to marked deformation charts identify with simultaneous fixed class Hodge locus germs cut out transversely by the period equations.

papers.title: On rough ideal convergence
papers.abstract: We continue the study of ideal convergence for sequences $(x_n)$ with values in a topological space $X$ with respect to a family $\{F_η:η\in X\}$ of subsets of $X$ with $η\in F_η$, where each $F_η$ measures the allowed ``roughness'' of convergence toward $η$. More precisely, after introducing the corresponding notions of cluster and limit points, we prove several inclusion and invariance properties, discuss their structural properties, and give examples showing that the rough notions are genuinely different from the classical ideal ones.

papers.title: The Inverse Symplectic Eigenvalue Problem of a Graph
papers.abstract: Symplectic geometry plays an increasingly important role in mathematics, physics, and applications. The concept of symplectic eigenvalues, whose existence for positive definite matrices is known as Williamson's Theorem, naturally gives rise to inverse problems. We introduce the inverse symplectic eigenvalue problem for positive definite matrices described by a labeled graph and solve it for several families and all labeled graphs of order four. We develop various tools such as the Strong Symplectic Spectral Property (SSSP) together with its consequences, graph couplings to describe collections of labelings of a graph that produce the same symplectic eigenvalues, and coupled graph zero forcing. We establish numerous results for symplectic positive definite matrices, including a sharp lower bound on the number of nonzero entries of such an irreducible matrix (or equivalently, the number of edges in its graph). This lower bound is a consequence of a lower bound on the sum of the number of nonzero entries in an irreducible positive definite matrix and its inverse.

papers.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
papers.abstract: We describe an explicit basis for the $\operatorname{SU}(2)$-invariant space of the exterior power $\wedge_{2k} \mathbb{C}^{2m}$ via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with $m$ spin orbitals and $k$ electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gröbner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.

papers.title: Grundy Values of Node-Kayles on Level-Regular Trees
papers.abstract: Node-Kayles is an impartial combinatorial game played on graphs, in which the two players alternately select a vertex and remove it together with all of its neighbours. By the Sprague--Grundy theorem, every position has a Grundy value that determines its outcome under optimal play. In this paper we study the Grundy values of Node-Kayles on level-regular trees $\T{a}$, $a=(a_1,\dots,a_d)$, in which every vertex at level $i-1$ has exactly $a_i$ children. We determine the Grundy values of all level-regular trees of depth at most two, show that $\G(\T{a})\le d+1$, and prove that $\G(\T{a})>0$ whenever $a_1a_2a_3$ is even, using an explicit mirror strategy. We prove a Leaf-Pair Lemma, which shows that the last branching parameter $a_d$ matters only through its parity, and a Twin Lemma for subgraphs that come in isomorphic pairs; as a consequence, $\G(\T{1,2k,s})=1$ for every $k\ge1$ and every finite sequence $s$. For trees containing a long run of ones, we give a general periodicity criterion: if the Grundy values of a tree with a pendant path of length $h$ are $34$-periodic on a finite window, then they are $34$-periodic for all larger $h$. This criterion extends to paths joining two fixed subtrees, and it explains the eventual periodicity of the families $\T{1^k,2}$ and $\T{2,1^k,2}$. We also show that, in this setting, eventual periodicity is equivalent to the boundedness of the Grundy values. Finally, supported by computations, we conjecture that the Grundy values are eventually periodic, with period $2$, in each branching parameter, and eventually periodic in the length of every run of ones.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.

papers.title: Composition laws for homogeneous energies and symphonic maps
papers.abstract: For a spectral energy homogeneous of degree $q>1$ in the differential, we characterize the smooth maps which pull back stationary maps into every Riemannian target. If the scalar density is nonzero, these maps are precisely the $q$-harmonic morphisms. The weak statement requires only $C^1$ regularity in the differential variable. It also covers densities which vanish on the identity of the intermediate tangent space. For the energies of the stress tensor $S$ and its trace-free analogue $T$, the source dimension enters the flux. In dimensions at least two we obtain a complete dichotomy: in equal dimensions the preserving maps are the $2p$-harmonic morphisms, and in unequal dimensions only locally constant maps preserve all targets. A hypersurface of dimension $n$ in a target of dimension $n+1$ detects the obstruction when the source dimension exceeds the intermediate dimension $n$.

papers.title: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
papers.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $ε$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

papers.title: A Taxonomy of Numerical Differentiation Methods
papers.abstract: Differentiation is a cornerstone of computing and data analysis in every discipline of science and engineering. Indeed, most fundamental physics laws are expressed as relationships between derivatives in space and time. However, derivatives are rarely directly measurable and must instead be computed, often from noisy, potentially corrupt data streams. There is a rich and broad literature of computational differentiation algorithms, but many impose extra constraints to work correctly, e.g. periodic boundary conditions, or are compromised in the presence of noise and corruption. It can therefore be challenging to select the method best-suited to any particular problem. Here we review a broad range of numerical methods for calculating derivatives, present important contextual considerations and choice points, compare relative advantages, and provide basic theory for each algorithm in order to assist users with the mathematical underpinnings. This serves as a practical guide to help scientists and engineers match methods to application domains. We also provide an open-source Python package, PyNumDiff, which contains a broad suite of methods for differentiating noisy data.

papers.title: Seaweed algebras with restricted part sizes
papers.abstract: Seaweed algebras are a class of Lie algebras that are naturally characterized by a pair of compositions, which in turn are represented visually as planar graphs called meanders. These meanders provide a straightforward method for computing the index of the associated algebra. The goal of this paper is to enumerate those seaweed algebras with a fixed index and whose associated compositions have restricted part sizes. In particular, we enumerate those with composition part sizes from so-called acyclic sets. We also establish a bijection between sets of indecomposable seaweed algebras with meanders with certain restricted part sizes and sets of permutations with restricted displacements. In certain cases, the index of the algebra can be determined by a simple statistic on the permutation.

papers.title: On the $2$-torsion in class groups of number fields
papers.abstract: In $2020$, Bhargava, Shankar, Taniguchi, Thorne, Tsimerman, and Zhao proved that for a finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $n\geq 5$, the size of the $2$-torsion class group is bounded by $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}+\varepsilon})$, where $D_{K}$ is the absolute discriminant of $K$. In the present paper, we improve their bound by proving that $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}-δ_{K}+\varepsilon})$, for a constant $δ_{K}\geq\frac{1}{28n}-\frac{3}{28n(n-1)}$.

papers.title: Metastability of diffusion processes in narrow tubes
papers.abstract: We study the metastable behavior of diffusion processes in narrow tube domains, where the metastability is induced by entropic barriers. We identify a sequence of characteristic time scales $\{T_ε^i\}_{1 \leq i \leq \abs{V'}}$, where $\abs{V'}$ denotes the number of distinct scales among the vertex neighborhoods, and characterize the asymptotic behavior of the diffusion process both at intermediate time scales and at the first critical time scale. Our analysis relies on a refined understanding of the narrow escape problem in domains with bottlenecks, in particular on estimates for the exit place and on the conditional distribution of the exit time given the exit place, results that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: A kernel method for the learning of Wasserstein geometric flows
papers.abstract: Wasserstein gradient and Hamiltonian flows provide geometric formulations of many partial differential equations. We develop a structure-preserving kernel method for jointly estimating the external potential and interaction kernel governing these flows, assuming a known internal energy. The inverse problem is formulated through a trajectory-dependent observation operator and regularized in a product of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, yielding an explicit finite representation of the estimator. We characterize joint non-identifiability through the null space of the observation operator and derive a Fourier criterion on the torus, distinguishing uniqueness of the regularized estimator from recovery of the underlying physical components. We establish reconstruction error bounds and convergence rates under source conditions and suitable regularization and mesh refinement, together with a stability estimate for Hamiltonian flows with vanishing internal energy. Numerical experiments demonstrate joint reconstruction and illustrate how unobservable interaction modes can prevent accurate potential recovery despite small observation-equation residuals. A comparison with sparse learning illustrates the dependence of reconstruction accuracy on the chosen dictionary.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on High Moments of Twisted Fourier coefficients of Modular Forms
papers.abstract: For any large prime $q$, $x \leq 1$ and any real $k\geq 2$, we prove a lower bound for the following $2k$-th moment \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{χ\in X_q^*}} \Big| \sum_{n\leq x} χ(n)λ(n)\Big|^{2k}, \end{equation*} where $X_q^*$ denotes the set of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ and $λ(n)$ the Fourier coefficients of a fixed modular form. The bound we obtain is sharp up to a constant factor under the generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

papers.title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.

papers.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.title: A Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on non-CMC closed manifolds
papers.abstract: In the paper, we prove the existence of a positive and essentially bounded solution to a Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on a closed manifold with non-constant mean curvature. In particular, the non-constant mean curvature gives rise to supercritical terms in the equation, on top of singular ones. We employ a recent fixed-point argument, which involves sub- and supersolutions. Additionally, we provide several conditions on the coefficients in the equation that prevent the existence of positive classical solutions.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for the subcritical semilinear heat equation in non-convex domains
papers.abstract: We consider the semilinear heat equation $u_t=Δu+|u|^{p-1} u$ in possibly non-convex and unbounded domains. Our main result shows the nonexistence of type II blow-up for possibly sign-changing solutions in the energy subcritical range $(n-2)p<n+2$. This resolves a long-standing open question dating back to the 1980s and also deduces the blow-up of the scaling critical norm.

papers.title: Generalized Centralizers and Polynomial Equivalence of Matrices: Answers to Questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova
papers.abstract:
For $n	imes n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over a field and a scalar $ω
e0$, let $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\{X:AX=ωXA\}$. If $ω$ is a root of unity of order $q\ge2$, then $\mathcal C_{ω^j}(A)=\mathcal C_{ω^j}(B)$ for all integers $j$ if and only if each of $A$ and $B$ is a polynomial in the other with exponents $\equiv1\pmod q$. Over algebraically closed fields, for $ω
e1$, all $A$, and scalars $\varepsilon
e0$, we describe all $Y$ with $XY=\varepsilon YX$ for all $X\in\mathcal C_ω(A)$. Let $a(μ)$ be the size of the largest Jordan block of $A$ at $μ$, or $0$ if there is none. If $\varepsilon$ is a power of $ω$, all such $Y$ are polynomials in $A$ if and only if $a(ωμ)=a(μ)$ for all $μ
e0$, or this fails only at some $ν$ and at $ω^{-1}ν$, where $A$ has a single largest Jordan block at $ν$ and $a(ων)=a(ω^{-1}ν)=a(ν)-1$. This answers two questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova. If $ω
e1$ has finite order, then for such $A$, $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ exactly when $A$ and $B$ are polynomials in each other of this form. For all other $A$ some $B$ that is not a polynomial in $A$ satisfies $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ if the field has more than $n^2+1$ elements. In the $ω$-commuting digraph of Raja and Vaezpour, with an edge from $A$ to $B$ if $AB=ωBA$, vertices with edges to and from the same vertices are twins. Over fields with more than $2n^2+1$ elements we determine the vertices $A$ whose twins are all polynomials in $A$, and describe these twins. We find all $A$, $B$, and $k\ge2$ for which the kernel of $(X\mapsto[A,X])^k$ is the set of $X$ with $[X,[X,\ldots,[X,B]\ldots]]=0$ ($k$ brackets), where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Apart from scalar $B$, this happens only in characteristic $
e2$, for $k=2$ and $2	imes2$ matrices that generate the same quadratic extension.

papers.title: Separability and Submetrizability in Locally Convex Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce the property of countable separation for a locally convex Hausdorff space $X$ and relate it to the existence of a metrizable coarser topology. Building on this, we demonstrate how the separability of $X$ is equivalent to the existence of a locally convex topology on the dual $X'$ that is metrizable and coarser than the weak topology $σ(X', X)$. This result generalizes known conditions for separability and provides a precise duality between separability and metrizability. We also show how to derive new and known conditions for the separability of $X$ from this characterization.

papers.title: On the decomposition of the diagonal for n-fold hypersurfaces via cubic n-1-folds
papers.abstract: We study the question of the existence of a decomposition of the diagonal for very general degree $d\geq 4$ and $(2,d\geq 3)$-complete intersection $n$-folds. Using cycle-theoretic techniques of Lange, Pavic and Schreieder we reduce the question to the existence of such a decomposition for $n-1$-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces. This extends results of Nicaise and Ottem from stable rationality to the existence of a decomposition of the diagonal. A key ingredient is the essential dimension of cubic hypersurfaces due to Voisin. As an application, we use a recent result of Engel, de Gaay Fortman and Schreieder on the decomposition of the diagonal for cubic threefolds to give a new proof of the retract irrationality of a very general complex quartic $4$-fold, originally due to Totaro, and of a very general complex $(2,3)$-complete intersection $4$-fold, originally due to Skauli. As another application we show that a very general quintic fourfold containing a three-dimensional linear subspace with multiplicity $2$, which is unirational due to results of Massarenti, does not admit a decomposition of the diagonal and is therefore not retract rational.

papers.title: A polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of block-structured graphs
papers.abstract: The boxicity of a graph $G$ is the minimum dimension $d$ that admits a representation of $G$ as the intersection graph of a family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Boxicity has applications in ecology and operations research, where it models competition for shared resources. Computing boxicity is an NP-hard problem. Despite considerable theoretical interest, few graph classes are known for which the boxicity can be computed in polynomial time. Following the approach of Cozzens and Roberts (1983), we study directly the boxicity of graph complements, which we call co-boxicity. In this setting, the geometric intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ becomes a graph cover problem involving only complements of interval graphs. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that computes the co-boxicity of $G$ from two pieces of information about each block: its co-boxicity, and how the co-boxicity changes when certain subsets of its vertices become cut-vertices. Using this algorithm, we obtain polynomial-time algorithms for the co-boxicity of trees, graphs with bounded block order, block graphs, and cactus graphs. More generally, our method implies the union of these results: for any fixed $k \geq 3$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of $G$ whenever every block of $G$ is complete, a cycle, or has at most $k$ vertices.

papers.title: Critical phenomena in 2D Coulomb gas: Birth of a gap
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of radially symmetric Coulomb gas systems at inverse temperature $β= 2$. The family is characterised by the property that the density of the equilibrium measure vanishes on a ring at radius $r_*$, which lies strictly inside the droplet. The large-$n$ expansion of the logarithm of the partition function is obtained up to the constant term and features a novel term of order $n^{1/4}$. We perform a double scaling limit of the correlation kernel at the $n^{1/4}$ scale and obtain a new limiting kernel in the bulk, which differs from the well-known Ginibre kernel.

papers.title: Boundary Feller-Dynkin processes associated with Laguerre processes and Pickrell diffusions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a Feller-Dynkin boundary process by applying the method of intertwiners to the coherent family, introduced in our previous work, of Laguerre processes with a fixed parameter. The corresponding boundary process is computed explicitly, and it turns out to be a deterministic dynamical system. Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

papers.title: Concentration Inequalities for Branching Random Walks
papers.abstract: Motivated by phase transition problems in CSPs, we prove a more general concentration inequality that retains classical sub-Gaussian tails under a mild global linear-growth condition $|S_n| < Cn$, relaxing the bounded-increment assumption to finite exponential moments and requiring neither independence nor the martingale property. We further extend it to branching random walks (BRWs), obtaining the first concentration inequality for BRWs.

papers.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
papers.abstract: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.

papers.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
papers.abstract: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($β\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$β$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$β$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $β$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$β$ process over exponentially long time horizons.

papers.title: A Multivariate Generalized Cox Model for Dependent and Simultaneous Default Times
papers.abstract: We propose a framework for dependent default times where each name defaults when an increasing driver crosses an independent unit exponential threshold. As in Gueye and Jeanblanc (2022), the drivers may jump, so defaults may occur at stopping times of the reference filtration, including predictable ones, and a common jump may cause no, one or several simultaneous defaults. For general drivers, we derive the conditional joint survival law by a backward recursion; it is an explicit product of survival functions if and only if, for every set of names, the predictable reduction of the compensator of their first default time is deterministic. If, moreover, defaults avoid predictable stopping times, the law is a fatal shock law with hazards identified from the drivers; predictable default atoms can rule this out. Examples include Lévy subordinators and, with random reductions but explicit laws, Liu's model and shot-noise drivers with memory.

papers.title: Co-periods and central symmetric cube L-values
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the co-period integral attached to an automorphic form on $\GL(2)$ and two exceptional theta series on the cubic Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $\GL(2)$. In the local aspect, we show the $\Hom$-space is always of one dimension and conduct the unramified calculations. In the global aspect, we give the Euler decomposition for the co-period integrals of Eisenstein series and propose an Ichino-Ikeda type conjecture relating the co-period integrals of cuspidal forms to the central critical value of symmetric cube $L$-functions. We also deduce from the local multiplicity one result that there exist cuspidal automorphic forms with prescribed local components and non-vanishing central symmetric cube $L$-values.

papers.title: Approximation of the Lévy-driven stochastic heat equation on the sphere
papers.abstract: The stochastic heat equation on the sphere driven by an additive square-integrable Lévy process is approximated by a spectral method in space and forward and backward Euler-Maruyama schemes in time. New sharp regularity results are proven for its solution. The spectral approximation is based on a truncation of the series expansion with respect to the spherical harmonic functions. For a given regularity of the initial condition and two different settings of regularity for the driving noise, strong convergence rates for the spectral approximation and for the Euler-Maruyama methods are proven. Moreover, weak rates of up to twice the strong rates are shown for Wiener noise and for Lévy noise with independent and up to a deterministic decay rate factor identically distributed components, while for general square-integrable Lévy noise the weak rate depends explicitly on the polynomial order of the test function. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: Regularity of velocity averages in kinetic equations with heterogeneity
papers.abstract: This study investigates the regularity of kinetic equations with spatial heterogeneity. Recent progress has shown that velocity averages of weak solutions $h$ in $L^p$ ($p>1$) are strongly $L^1_{\text{loc}}$ compact under the natural non-degeneracy condition. We establish regularity estimates for equations with an $\boldsymbol{x}$-dependent drift vector $\mathfrak{f} = \mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbolλ)$, which satisfies a quantitative version of the non-degeneracy condition. We prove that $(t,\boldsymbol{x}) \mapsto \int ρ(\boldsymbolλ) h(t,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbolλ)\, d\boldsymbolλ$, for any sufficiently regular $ρ(\cdot)$, belongs to the fractional Sobolev space $W_{\text{loc}}^{β,r}$, for some regularity $β\in (0,1)$ and integrability $r \geq 1$ exponents. While such estimates have long been known for $\boldsymbol{x}$-independent drift vectors $\mathfrak{f}=\mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbolλ)$, this is the first quantitative regularity estimate in a general heterogeneous setting. As an application, we obtain a regularity estimate for entropy solutions to heterogeneous conservation laws with nonlinear flux and $L^\infty$ initial data.

papers.title: First-order methods for stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization with deterministic constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization problems with deterministic constraints. Existing methods typically aim to find an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, in which both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are within a prescribed tolerance $ε$. However, in many practical applications, constraints must be nearly satisfied with certainty, rendering such solutions potentially unsuitable due to the risk of substantial violations. To address this issue, we propose stochastic first-order methods for finding an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, where the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$ and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. Our methods apply an accelerated stochastic gradient (ASG) scheme or a modified variance-reduced ASG scheme $only\ once$ to a sequence of quadratic penalty subproblems with appropriately chosen penalty parameters. We establish first-order oracle complexity bounds for the proposed methods in computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: The Error in a Smooth Weighted Prime Number Formula and Zero-free Regions for the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We study the error bound for a smooth weighted prime number theorem, and its implication to the zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function using the method of Pintz. We also give an application to the average number of smooth weighted Goldbach representations and generalize the result to the case of smooth weighted average k-Goldbach representations.

papers.title: Finite element spaces of double forms
papers.abstract: The tensor product of two differential forms of degree $p$ and $q$ is a multilinear form that is alternating in its first $p$ arguments and alternating in its last $q$ arguments. These forms, which are known as double forms or $(p,q)$-forms, play a central role in certain differential complexes that arise when studying partial differential equations. We construct piecewise polynomial finite element spaces for all of the natural subspaces of the space of $(p,q)$-forms, excluding one subspace which fails to admit a piecewise constant discretization. As special cases, our construction recovers known finite element spaces for symmetric matrices with tangential-tangential continuity (the Regge finite elements), symmetric matrices with normal-normal continuity, and trace-free matrices with normal-tangential continuity. It also gives rise to new spaces, like a finite element space for tensors possessing the symmetries of the Riemann curvature tensor.

papers.title: Morphisms and comorphisms of sites I -- Double categories of sites
papers.abstract: We arrange morphisms and comorphisms of sites as the horizontal and vertical cells of a double category of sites; using the formalism of extensions and restrictions of presheaves, we explains how one can define a sheafification double functor from this double category to the quintet double category of Grothendieck topoi. We describe properties of this double functor and recover some classical results of topos theory through a new notion of locally exact square, generalizing exact squares in the presence of topologies. We also describe a 2-comonad on $\Cat$ for which lax morphisms of coalgebras are morphisms of sites and colax morphisms are comorphisms of sites, explaining the arrangement as a double category.

papers.title: Determining evolutionary equations from a single passive boundary observation
papers.abstract: We study inverse boundary problems (IBPs) for evolutionary partial differential equations from a single passive boundary observation generated by an unknown internal source in an unknown medium. The goal is simultaneous recovery of the source and medium coefficients. In stark contrast to active measurements, where designed inputs provide rich, structured data, passive-observation inverse boundary problems have minimal observable information and intrinsically coupled unknowns. Consequently, these problems have been studied far less systematically than their active counterparts. In this paper, we develop a unified and novel framework based on fundamental integral identities, integrating tools from harmonic analysis, interface asymptotics, and free-boundary regularity together with delicate low- and high-frequency asymptotics. This framework provides the first systematic resolution for a broad class of such inverse problems for {second-order hyperbolic, parabolic, and Schrödinger equations} within a single coherent approach. The key technical condition we impose is that the {cardinality of the measurement dataset exceeds that of the unknowns by at least one dimension}. This extra dimensional room enables us to decouple the unknowns and effectively handle inherent nonlinearity of the inverse problem. The unique identifiability results we obtain are arguably the best possible from a cardinality point of view. They not only subsume all existing results in the literature as special cases, but also cover significantly more general configurations of practical interest. Our framework complements several classical theories for IBPs and opens up a promising new direction with numerous potential developments.

papers.title: The Betti Numbers of Kunz-Waldi Semigroups
papers.abstract: Given two coprime numbers $p<q$, KW semigroups contain $p,q$ and are contained in $\langle p,q,r \rangle$ where $2r= p,q, p+q$ whichever is even. These semigroups were first introduced by Kunz and Waldi. Kunz and Waldi proved that all $KW$ semigroups of embedding dimension $n\geq 4$ have Cohen-Macaulay type $n-1$ and first Betti number ${n \choose 2}$. In this paper, we characterize KW semigroups whose defining ideal is generated by the $2\times 2$ minors of a $2\times n$ matrix. In addition, we identify all KW semigroups that lie on the interior of the same face of the Kunz cone $\mathcal C_p$ as a KW semigroup with determinantal defining ideal. Thus, we provide an explicit formula for the Betti numbers of all those KW semigroups.

papers.title: Low-regularity error estimates of a filtered Lie-Trotter splitting scheme for the Zakharov system in arbitrary dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish low-regularity error estimates for a fully discrete, filtered Lie--Trotter splitting scheme for the Zakharov system on the $d$-dimensional torus. Our analysis relies on multilinear estimates in discrete Bourgain spaces. Specifically, for an exact solution $(E,z,z_t)$ with regularity $H^{s+r+1/2}\times H^{s+r}\times H^{s+r-1}$ on a fixed time interval, we prove an error bound of order $\mathcal{O}(τ^{s/2}+N^{-s})$ in $H^{r+1/2}\times H^r\times H^{r-1}$ for $s\in(0,2]$, where $r=\max\{0,\tfrac d2-1\}$, $τ$ is the time step, and $N$ is the number of spatial grid points in each coordinate direction. The analysis treats the coupled nonlinearities directly, without introducing the time-differentiated auxiliary variables of an Ozawa-type transformation. Under the stated CFL condition, which renders the filter inactive on the Fourier collocation space, the scheme preserves discrete mass exactly in exact arithmetic. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence rates and show small relative energy errors over the tested time intervals.

papers.title: Lifting canonical divisors of the form $2G-D$ in towers of function fields
papers.abstract: We present a method for constructing, given a canonical divisor in a function field of the form $2G-D$, another canonical divisor of the form $2G'-D'$ in an extension of the function field that satisfies certain ramification conditions. This method applies in particular to certain recursive towers that yield sequences of canonical divisors of the form $2G_i-D_i$ for each index $i\geq 0$. Using these divisors, we construct sequences of iso-dual AG-codes and establish the existence of asymptotically good sequences among them. Beyond its simplicity, a key advantage of our approach is its flexibility, which allows it to be applied to a wide range of recursive towers of function fields, thereby providing a more explicit way to construct asymptotically good sequences of iso-dual AG-codes.

papers.title: A remark on the reach and upper bounds on some extrinsic geometry invariants of submanifolds
papers.abstract: We consider a compact submanifold $M$ of a Riemannian manifold $N$ and we use the second variation formula as a tool to drive some geometric results on reach$(M, N)$ the reach of $M$ in $N$, including some useful relations between the extrinsic geometry of $M$ in $N$ and reach$(M, N)$. Our results generalize some theorems previously proved for the special case where $N$ is Euclidean space.

papers.title: Complexity Framework For Forbidden Subgraphs V: Beyond Simple Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate how allowing self-loops and multi-edges (i.e. moving from simple graphs to pseudographs) impacts the complexity of graph problems on finitely defined monotone graph classes. We do this by extending the C123-framework beyond simple graphs. We use several testbed problems to illustrate some of the new and varied behaviours introduced by the transition to pseudographs. We show that Pseudograph Matching Cut and Pseudograph d-Cut are C123-problems. Consequently, for every finite set HH of simple graphs, we obtain a complete complexity classification for these problems on HH-subgraph-free graphs. This sharply contrasts with their simple-graph counterparts, which are not C123-problems and their complexity remains open even for classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph H. We also show that Pseudograph Stable Cut is not a C123-problem. Nevertheless, for graph classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph, the problem mirrors the C123 classification; this correspondence already fails for sets of size 2. This gives the first example of a problem that aligns with C123-problems for a single forbidden subgraph but not for larger sets. Motivated by the interpretation of Stable Cut as a surjective homomorphism to a partially reflexive path, we also study surjective homomorphisms to partially reflexive cycles on k vertices with one irreflexive vertex. These problems share structural similarities with Pseudograph Stable Cut. We prove that for k at least 6, they are NP-complete on triangle-free pseudographs. However, unlike Pseudograph Stable Cut, they are polynomial-time solvable on all graph classes with bounded-degree.

papers.title: A Bourgain-Gromov problem on non-compact Sobolev-Lorentz embeddings
papers.abstract: We study the non-compact Sobolev embeddings into the optimal scale of Lorentz spaces, $W_0^mL^{p,q}(Ω) \to L^{\frac{dp}{d - mp},r}(Ω)$, where $Ω\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $1 \leq m < d$, $0<q<r\le\infty$ with $1<p<\frac dm$ or $p=q=1$. We show that these embeddings are finitely strictly singular with certain upper bounds on the decay rate of the Bernstein numbers. We reduce the Sobolev embeddings to embeddings of Besov spaces and sequence spaces, which simplifies the previous methods by Bourgain-Gromov and Lang-Mihula.

papers.title: Exponential mixing for equilibrium states of time changes of hyperbolic geodesic flows
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic manifold of dimension $n\ge2$, let $ψ$ be a smooth positive function on its unit tangent bundle $SM$, and let $f^t_ψ$ be the time change of the geodesic flow with speed $1/ψ$. We prove that $f^t_ψ$ is exponentially mixing, for Hölder observables, with respect to the equilibrium state of every Hölder potential, as asked by Bowen and Ruelle. This includes the smooth invariant measure and the measure of maximal entropy. The proof runs Dolgopyat's cancellation argument at a variable \emph{local frequency} $Λ_b=|b|(1+\|\bY_b\|)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:localfreq}): the scale $1/|b|$ is replaced by a scale that depends on the point, as in the work of Tsujii and Zhang in dimension three, and the argument runs without a smooth contact structure and without $C^1$ strong foliations. Many of the techniques, in particular the reduction to an expanding semiflow by quotienting along the stable foliation, are inspired by the earlier work of Butterley and War \cite{BW20}.

papers.title: Exact Sequence Interpolation with Transformers
papers.abstract: We prove that transformers can exactly interpolate datasets of finite input sequences in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\geq 2$, with corresponding output sequences of smaller or equal length. Specifically, given $N$ sequences of arbitrary but finite lengths in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and output sequences of lengths $m^1, \dots, m^N \in \mathbb{N}$, we construct a transformer with $\mathcal{O}(\sum_{j=1}^N m^j)$ blocks and $\smash{\mathcal{O}(d \sum_{j=1}^N m^j)}$ parameters that exactly interpolates the dataset. Our construction provides complexity estimates that are independent of the input sequence length, by alternating feed-forward and self-attention layers and by capitalizing on the clustering effect inherent to the latter. Our novel constructive method also uses low-rank parameter matrices in the self-attention mechanism, a common feature of practical transformer implementations. These results are first established in the hardmax self-attention setting, where the geometric structure permits an explicit and quantitative analysis, and are then extended to the softmax setting. Finally, we demonstrate the applicability of our exact interpolation construction to learning problems, in particular by providing convergence guarantees to a global minimizer under regularized training strategies. Our analysis contributes to the theoretical understanding of transformer models, offering an explanation for their excellent performance in exact sequence-to-sequence interpolation tasks.

papers.title: Tropical Lagrangian coamoebae and generalized dimer models
papers.abstract: We study the coamoebae of Lagrangian submanifolds of $(\mathbb{C}^\times)^n$, specifically how the combinatorics of their degenerations encodes the homological algebra of mirror coherent sheaves. Concretely, to a minimal free resolution $F^\bullet$ of a module $M$ over $\mathbb{C}[z_1^{\pm 1}, \dotsc, z_n^{\pm 1}]$ we associate a simplicial complex $T(F^\bullet) \subset T^n$. We call $T(F^\bullet)$ a tropical Lagrangian coamoeba. We show that the discrete information in $F^\bullet$ can often be recovered from $T(F^\bullet)$, and that more generally $M$ is mirror to a certain constructible sheaf supported on $T(F^\bullet)$. The resulting interplay between coherent sheaves on $(\mathbb{C}^\times)^n$ and simplicial complexes in $T^n$ provides a higher-dimensional generalization of the spectral theory of dimer models in $T^2$, as well as a symplectic counterpart to the theory of brane brick models.

papers.title: On loops in the complement of dimers
papers.abstract: We consider ergodic translation-invariant Gibbs measures for the dimer model (i.e. perfect matchings) on the hexagonal lattice. The complement of a dimer configuration is a fully-packed loop configuration: each vertex has degree two. This is also known as the loop $O(1)$ model at $x=\infty$. We show that, if the measure is non-frozen, then it exhibits either infinitely many loops around every face or a unique bi-infinite path. Our main tool is the flip (or XOR) operation: if a hexagon contains exactly three dimers, one can replace them by the other three edges. Classical results in dimer theory imply that such hexagons appear with a positive density. To some extent, this replaces the finite-energy property and allows to make use of tools from the percolation theory, in particular the Burton--Keane argument, to exclude existence of more than one bi-infinite path.

papers.title: Finite-Dimensional Protori Are Adelic Tori
papers.abstract: We show the category of finite-dimensional compact connected abelian groups (finite-dimensional protori) {\it is} the category of {\it adelic tori}, for which there is a complete Lie theory: for each adelic torus $G$ there is a proper short exact sequence $0\ra\q^n\ra \mathcal{L}(G)\xrightarrow{\exp} G\ra 0$ with $\exp$ the {\it adelic exponential}. Extending the definition of nonarchimedean dimension to apply to number fields, the capstone result is the fact that all number fields have nonarchimedean dimension 1.

papers.title: The internal languages of univalent categories
papers.abstract: Internal language theorems are fundamental in categorical logic, since they express an equivalence between syntax and semantics. One such theorem was proven by Clairambault and Dybjer, who corrected the result originally by Seely. More specifically, they constructed a biequivalence between the bicategory of locally Cartesian closed categories and the bicategory of democratic categories with families with extensional identity types, $Σ$-types, and $Π$-types. This theorem expresses that the internal language of locally Cartesian closed categories is extensional Martin-Löf type theory with dependent sums and products. In this paper, we study the theorem by Clairambault and Dybjer for univalent categories, and we extend it to various classes of toposes, among which are $Π$-pretoposes, elementary toposes, and elementary toposes with a universe. The results in this paper have been formalized using the proof assistant Rocq and the UniMath library.

papers.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
papers.abstract: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.

papers.title: Remarks on nonlinear dispersive PDEs with rough dispersion management
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Cauchy problem for a class of dispersive PDEs where a rough time coefficient is present in front of the dispersion. Under minimal assumptions on the occupation measure of this coefficient, we show that for the large class of semilinear dispersive PDEs whose well-posedness theory relies on linear estimates of Strichartz or local smoothing type, one has the same well-posedness theory with or without the modulation. We also show a regularization by noise type of phenomenon for rough modulations, namely, large data global well-posedness in the focusing mass-critical case for the modulated equation. Under rougher assumptions on the modulation, we show that one can also transfer the well-posedness theory based on multilinear Fourier analysis from the original dispersive PDE to the modulated one. In the case of the NLS equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{T}^d$, this covers all the sub-critical and critical regularities, thus completing and extending the various results currently available in the literature. At last, in the case of the periodic Wick-ordered cubic NLS, we show an even stronger form of regularization by noise, namely well-posedness in the critical Fourier-Lebesgue space for rough modulations.

papers.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
papers.abstract: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $ω$-ASD connections (where $ω$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

papers.title: A Classification Theorem on Non-compact Embeddings between Besov Spaces
papers.abstract: We analyze the embedding properties between Besov spaces, defined on the total space $\mathbb R^n$ and on bounded domains. We give a complete classification on whether or not these embedding maps satisfy certain weaker forms of compactness characterized by the so-called strictly and finitely strictly singular conditions. The result extends the recent findings on Sobolev embeddings by offering a refined description of the quality of non-compactness in the setting of Besov spaces.

papers.title: Picard Groups of Spectral Varieties and Moduli of Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of Higgs sheaves valued in line bundles and the associated Hitchin maps on surfaces. We first work out Picard groups of generic (very general) spectral varieties which holds for dimension of at least 2, i.e., a Noether--Lefschetz type theorem for spectral varieties. We then apply these Picard-group calculations to obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the non-emptiness of generic Hitchin fibers in the range where the spectral Noether--Lefschetz theorem applies. Then we move on to detect the geometry of the moduli spaces of Higgs sheaves as the second Chern class varies.

papers.title: Exploiting the nonzero diagonal pattern in matrix function computations
papers.abstract: We consider the task of approximating a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a matrix in which only a relatively small number of (not necessarily consecutive) sub- and superdiagonals contain nonzero entries. Approximating $f$ by a low-degree polynomial $p$ allows us to obtain sparse approximations to $f(A)$, which one can efficiently work with (while, in general, $f(A)$ is a dense matrix, even when $A$ is sparse). Our approach is based on carefully inspecting the locations where nonzeros can occur in $p(A)$, and identifying the entries in $A$ that influence them. In particular, we illustrate how this approach can be used for efficiently approximating the trace of $f(A)$ and identify how this approach is related to established (stochastic) probing methods for trace estimation. Another application area in which our approach works particularly well is the computation of functions of Toeplitz matrices. Here, studying the sparsity pattern of $p(A)$ allows us to reduce the computation of the whole matrix polynomial to that of a single small-scale submatrix, yielding an algorithm that scales exceptionally well to large problem sizes.

papers.title: Inequalities involving Higher Degree Polynomial Functions in $π(x)$
papers.abstract: Earlier research reflects that the two sides of Ramanujan's inequality for the prime-counting function \begin{align*} π(x)^2<\frac{ex}{\log x}π(x/e) \end{align*} happens to agree through four asymptotic orders. In this paper, we try to examine how this cancellation arises in higher-degree expressions and how shifts affect the size of the resulting gaps. In signed sums of equal powers of shifted prime counts, the first nonvanishing moment of the logarithmic shifts determines the leading term. A cubic comparison at five dilations exhibits four successive cancellations, leaving a gap of order $x^3/(\log x)^7$. A finite-difference argument proves its positivity for every real $x\geq e^{52}$ when the logarithmic shifts are spaced by $2$. When the shifts and nonnegative weights are fixed, the weighted Ramanujan gap retains order $x^2/(\log x)^6$. Its leading coefficient is $c^2(1+σ^2)$, where $c$ is the total rescaled weight and $σ^2$ is the weighted variance of the logarithmic shifts. We also give the explicit range $x\geq 85e$ for the logarithmically weighted five-shift inequality and determine the eventual sign of a polynomial family in every fixed integer degree $m\geq 3$. Exact counts and interval enclosures illustrate the expansions and the effect of variance at fixed rescaled weight and mean.

papers.title: Clustering in pure-attention hardmax transformers and its role in sentiment analysis
papers.abstract: Transformers are extremely successful machine learning models whose mathematical properties remain poorly understood. Here, we rigorously characterize the behavior of transformers with hardmax self-attention and normalization sublayers as the number of layers tends to infinity. By viewing such transformers as discrete-time dynamical systems describing the evolution of points in a Euclidean space, and thanks to a geometric interpretation of the self-attention mechanism based on hyperplane separation, we show that the transformer inputs asymptotically converge to a clustered equilibrium determined by special points called \textit{leaders}. We then leverage this theoretical understanding to solve sentiment analysis problems from language processing using a fully interpretable transformer model, which effectively captures `context' by clustering meaningless words around leader words carrying the most meaning. Finally, we outline remaining challenges to bridge the gap between the mathematical analysis of transformers and their real-life implementation.

papers.title: On non-isomorphic universal sofic groups
papers.abstract: We show that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ non-isomorphic universal sofic groups. This proves a conjecture of Simon Thomas.

papers.title: A one-dimensional model of catheter aspiration in blood vessels
papers.abstract: Aspiration thrombectomy is a primary endovascular treatment option for acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusions, in which a catheter is navigated to the occlusion site and suction is applied to remove the thrombus. This work introduces a reduced one-dimensional model for aspiration in blood vessels that accounts for the elasticity of both the vessel wall and the catheter. The inclusion of vessel wall visco-elasticity transforms the governing equation for the flow rate into a parabolic form, enabling an accurate resolution of the diffuse pressure gradients near the catheter tip observed in CFD simulations. The numerical treatment is based on a relaxation of the hyperbolic subsystem that facilitates nodal solvers, enabling efficient coupling between catheterized and uncatheterized vessel segments, including bifurcations and the catheter tip. A splitting strategy ensures that the visco-elastic terms incur only negligible additional computational cost relative to the purely hyperbolic model. The model is benchmarked against three-dimensional CFD simulations and reference data from the literature. Numerical experiments investigating the role of catheter elasticity and suction force on the hemodynamics are presented, and an uncertainty quantification study demonstrates the suitability of the framework for efficient parameter studies. The results indicate that the proposed model resolves blood flow comparably accurate to three-dimensional simulations at a fraction of the computational cost. While further in vitro and in vivo validation is required, the framework represents a promising step toward computationally efficient preoperative planning and uncertainty-aware decision support in aspiration thrombectomy.

papers.title: Uniqueness of ground state solutions for fractional Schrödinger equations with general nonlinearities
papers.abstract: In 2013, R.L. Frank and E. Lenzmann [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, Uniqueness of non-linear ground states for fractional Laplacians in $\mathbb{R}$, Acta Math. 210 (2) (2013) 261-318] studied the following problem: \begin{align*} (-Δ)^su + u = u^{p-1} \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \end{align*} where $s \in (0,1)$, $N = 1$, $p \in (2,2_s^*)$, and $2_s^*$ is the critical fractional Sobolev exponent. They proved that the ground state is unique (up to translations). Then in 2016, they, together with L. Silvestre [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, L. Silvestre, Uniqueness of radial solutions for the fractional Laplacian, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 69 (9) (2016) 1671-1726], showed similar uniqueness results for high dimensions ($N \geq 2$), in which they proposed a challenging open problem to extend their results about non-degeneracy and uniqueness of ground states to nonlinearities $f(u)$ beyond the pure-power case. In this paper, we aim to give an affirmative answer to this open issue for two classes of more general nonlinearities, including the case of sums of powers with certain conditions on exponents.

papers.title: Statistical Performance Guarantee for Subgroup Identification with Generic Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Across a wide array of disciplines, many researchers use machine learning (ML) algorithms to identify a subgroup of individuals who are likely to benefit from a treatment the most (``exceptional responders'') or those who are harmed by it. A common approach to this subgroup identification problem consists of two steps. First, researchers estimate the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) using an ML algorithm. Next, they use the estimated CATE to select those individuals who are predicted to be most affected by the treatment, either positively or negatively. Unfortunately, CATE estimates are often biased and noisy. In addition, utilizing the same data to both identify a subgroup and estimate its group average treatment effect results in a multiple testing problem. To address these challenges, we develop uniform confidence bands for estimation of the group average treatment effect sorted by generic ML algorithm (GATES). Using these uniform confidence bands, researchers can identify, with a statistical guarantee, a subgroup whose GATES exceeds a certain effect size, regardless of how this effect size is chosen. The proposed methodology uses random treatment assignment, random sampling of units, and continuity and moment conditions, without requiring consistency or monotonicity of the ML score. We derive a Wiener representation of the estimation error, with corrections for the empirical subgroup threshold and the fixed treatment sample size. Estimating this representation gives asymptotically exact uniform coverage using Gaussian draws, without refitting the ML model. We also develop uniform bands for mean-adjusted treatment effects and other evaluation metrics. A simulation design and an application to a clinical trial of late-stage prostate cancer illustrate the subgroup identification problem.

papers.title: Adaptive mesh refinement for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.abstract: We propose a new adaptive algorithm for the approximation of the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation via a higher-order tangent plane scheme. We show that the adaptive approximation satisfies an energy inequality and demonstrate numerically that the adaptive algorithm outperforms uniform approaches.

papers.title: Coinvariants of metaplectic representations on moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We construct spaces of coinvariants at principally polarized abelian varieties with respect to the action of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra. We show how these spaces globalize to twisted $\mathscr{D}$-modules on moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties, and we determine the Atiyah algebra of a line bundle acting on them. We prove analogous results on the universal abelian variety. An essential aspect of our study involves analyzing the Atiyah algebra of the Hodge and canonical line bundles on moduli of abelian varieties and the universal abelian variety.

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, V
papers.abstract: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, which dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, IV
papers.abstract: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.

papers.title: Scattering in the planar restricted $(N+1)$-body problem
papers.abstract: In the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem, as time goes to positive or negative infinity the massless body has four possible final motions: hyperbolic, parabolic, oscillatory and bounded. In the hyperbolic case, the massless body comes from or goes to infinity with a non-zero limiting energy and a limiting direction, and in the parabolic case, it comes from or goes to infinity with a zero limiting energy and possibly a limiting direction. In this paper we study scattering orbits that come from infinity and then go to infinity. It will be proven that for the planar restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with the motions of the primaries being collision-free and periodic, for any two given asymptotic directions, there exists at least one hyperbolic scattering orbit for any positive limiting energy and one parabolic scattering orbit. The orbits are either always collision-free or regularizable with one collision.

papers.title: Total stability and Auslander-Reiten theory for Dynkin quivers
papers.abstract: This paper concerns stability functions for Dynkin quivers, in the generality introduced by Rudakov. We show that relatively few inequalities need to be satisfied for a stability function to be totally stable (i.e. to make every indecomposable stable). Namely, a stability function $μ$ is totally stable if and only if $μ(τV) < μ(V)$ for every almost split sequence $0 \to τV \to E \to V \to 0$ where $E$ is indecomposable. These can be visualized as those sequences around the "border" of the Auslander-Reiten quiver.

papers.title: Greatest Common Divisors and an Unlikely Intersection Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove inequalities involving greatest common divisors of functions at integral points with respect to numerically parallel divisors, generalizing a result of Wang and Yasufuku (after work of Bugeaud-Corvaja-Zannier, Corvaja-Zannier, and the second author). In addition to proving results in a broader context than previously considered, we also study the exceptional set in this setting, for both the counting function and the proximity function. Based on our study of exceptional sets, we propose new conjectures connected to the topic of unlikely intersections. We prove special cases of the conjectures on abelian varieties and the algebraic torus, including a completely explicit result in the former case, and provide a link between the conjectures and exceptional sets for inequalities involving greatest common divisors.

papers.title: On the Kantor product, II
papers.abstract: We describe the Kantor square (and Kantor product) of multiplications, extending the classification proposed in [I. Kaygorodov, On the Kantor product, Journal of Algebra and Its Applications, 16 (2017), 9, 1750167]. Besides, we explicitly describe the Kantor square of some low dimensional algebras and give constructive methods for obtaining new transposed Poisson algebras and Poisson-Novikov algebras; and for classifying Poisson structures and commutative post-Lie structures on a given algebra.

papers.title: Smooth Surfaces via Nets of Geodesics
papers.abstract: We study the reconstruction of smooth surfaces from networks of spatial curves prescribed as geodesics. Motivated by applications in computer-aided geometric design and the perception of three-dimensional shape, we propose a variational approach minimizing the integral of squared Gaussian curvature over surfaces spanning geodesic contours. Using isothermal coordinates, we derive the Euler-Lagrange equation for the conformal factor of the metric and the associated Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We also consider a biharmonic approximation obtained by linearizing the nonlinear equation. Numerical experiments are performed on four quadrilateral cells of a geodesic network constructed on an ellipsoid. We compute approximate isothermal coordinates, solve the biharmonic boundary-value problem, and compare the resulting curvature with that of the reference surface. These experiments consist of an important step towards a complete framework for the computation of smooth surfaces from geodesic curves.

papers.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.

papers.title: An application of "Selmer group Chabauty" to arithmetic dynamics
papers.abstract: We describe how one can use the "Selmer group Chabauty" method developed by the author to show that certain hyperelliptic curves of the form $$ C \colon y^2 = x^{2g+1} + h(x)^2 \,, $$ with $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $\operatorname{deg} h \le g$ and $h(0)$ is odd, have only the "obvious" rational points $\infty$ (the unique point at infinity on the smooth projective model of the curve) and $(0, \pm h(0))$. Let $c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and write $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$. We denote the iterates of $f_c$ by $f_c^{\circ n}$; i.e., we set $f_c^{\circ 0}(x) = x$ and $f_c^{\circ(n+1)}(x) = f_c(f_c^{\circ n}(x))$. As an application of the method, we prove that if $f_c^{\circ 2}$ is irreducible, then $f_c^{\circ 6}$ is also irreducible. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), it also follows that $f_c^{\circ 10}$ is irreducible.

papers.title: Sharp spectral gap and large time asymptotics for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with confinement
papers.abstract: We study the Poisson--Nernst--Planck (Debye--Hückel) system for a single species of charged particles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d=2$ or $3$, with an external confinement potential. The particles repel each other through the Coulomb interaction. For a class of potentials with at least linear growth at infinity, solutions converge to the unique stationary state at an exponential rate in a weighted $\mathrm L^2$ space. The rate is given by the spectral gap of the linearized operator, which is symmetric for a scalar product adapted to the free energy. Our main result is that, for the harmonic potential $φ(x)=\frac\mu2\,|x|^2$, this spectral gap is exactly $μ$, for any mass and in both dimensions. The corresponding eigenspace is spanned by the translation modes. Unlike the attractive (Keller--Segel) case, the repulsive interaction destroys the monotonicity of the spectrum with respect to the angular momentum. We overcome this difficulty with a duality criterion and explicit \emph{chiral fluxes} built from vector spherical harmonics. These reduce the non-local spectral problem to one-dimensional weighted inequalities, which we prove by a ground state transform. The center of mass decays exactly like $e^{-μt}$. After removing this motion, the convergence rate improves to a second spectral gap $Λ_2>μ$, for which we prove an explicit lower bound in terms of the central density of the stationary state. As consequences, we obtain rates of convergence in $\mathrm L^p$ norms, and improved intermediate asymptotics for the unconfined system in $\mathbb R^2$, after recentering at the center of mass.

papers.title: The universal conservative superalgebra
papers.abstract: We introduce the class of conservative superalgebras, in particular, the superalgebra $\mathcal{U}(V)$ of bilinear operations on a superspace $V$. Moreover, we show that each conservative superalgebra modulo its maximal Jacobi ideal is embedded into $\mathcal{U}(V)$ for a certain superspace $V$.

papers.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.

papers.title: Waldspurger's formula via a prehomogeneous zeta integral on $F^2 \otimes \bigwedge^2 F^4$
