papers.abstract: We study the initial value problem associated with the dispersive generalized Benjamin-Ono equation \begin{equation*} \partial_{t}u-\partial_{x}|D_{x}|^{a}u+u\,\partial_{x}u=0,\quad 1<a<2, \end{equation*} in weighted Sobolev spaces. First, we show that if the solution belongs to $L^{2}(|x|^{2α}dx)$ at two different times, then it gains regularity, namely $u\in C([-T,T]:H^{aα}(\mathbb{R}))$, for $α<5/2+a$ and suitable initial regularity. Second, we establish the persistence of the solution flow in $H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{2}(|x|^{2α}dx)$ under the sharp regularity assumption $s\ge aα$, for $α\in[1/2,5/2+a)$, where the zero mean condition is required for $α\ge 3/2+a$. Finally, we prove the unique continuation principles associated with the optimal decay rates $|x|^{3/2+a}$ and $|x|^{5/2+a}$ under optimal regularity assumptions. Our approach relies on weighted energy estimates, commutator expansions for the fractional Laplacian and pseudo-differential calculus.

papers.title: On Covariance Steering with Nonlinear Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper examines two ways nonlinear measurements complicate the statistical predictions during covariance steering. The covariance steering problem optimizes a control policy across a distribution of possible trajectories rather than a single specific trajectory. This approach has attracted growing interest as a way to account for uncertainty in aerospace applications such as trajectory optimization, stationkeeping, and landing. In many of these applications, covariance steering can account for measurement uncertainty through output feedback. Because standard formulations assume linear dynamics and measurements, applications with nonlinear measurements typically use an extended Kalman filter to estimate the state. This paper shows that techniques used to improve filter convergence, such as measurement underweighting, can reduce the accuracy of conventional covariance steering predictions by violating a key assumption. This is addressed with a new convex formulation that relaxes the assumption. This paper also demonstrates that adjusting the control policy during execution can improve agreement between predicted and actual state statistics. A numerical example of angles-only spacecraft rendezvous illustrates the benefits of the proposed method, and discussions are made regarding the implications of this generalized covariance steering formulation.

papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
papers.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nyström trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)=f, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+δ, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
papers.abstract: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4π$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current.

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ with $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$, let $S(p)$ be the minimum of $|p(c)/(c\,p'(0))|$ over the critical points $c$ of $p$, and let $K(d)$ be the supremum of $S(p)$ over all such $p$ of degree $d$. In 1981 Smale proved that $K(d)\le 4$ for every $d$, and asked whether $4$ can be replaced by $1$. We prove that Smale's mean value constant $\sup_dK(d)$ equals $4$ and that $K(d)\to4$ as $d\to\infty$, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. Each $K(d)$ is known to be below $4$, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. We can generalize the first-order Schreier sets recursively to higher orders, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element $2$ and the index shift of a convolution of the Fibonacci numbers (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

papers.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger algebras
papers.abstract: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schrödinger algebras to have bracket width one.

papers.title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract: A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(η,ω)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $η$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $ω$ satisfying \[ dω=η\wedgeω. \] We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families. Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $α$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by \[ η=π_2^*ξ,\qquad ω=d(π_1^*α)+π_1^*α\wedgeη, \] where $π_1$ and $π_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $ξ$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular, none of these compact homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic structure, even without any invariance assumption. As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.

papers.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
papers.abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was first established by SAT searches of the first author and independently confirmed by the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4, using only Lean's three standard axioms (propositional extensionality, choice and quotient soundness).

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollobás's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.

papers.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
papers.abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $Ψ_F$, the Boij-Söderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leqΨ_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $Ψ$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

papers.title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
papers.abstract: Bonnefont, Rajamäki and Vargas conjectured that, for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field, the Fourier dimension at $α+iβ$ equals the dimension of the real chaos at $α$ minus $β^2$. We prove the conjecture on the circle throughout their stated parameter range. For the canonical holomorphic family, the identity holds on one event of probability one for all $γ=α+iβ$ in the union of the open unit disk and the region $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$, $|α|+|β|<\sqrt2$. For each fixed parameter on the conjecture's sloping boundary, where $1<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|α|+|β|=\sqrt2$, the Fourier coefficients decay at a logarithmic rate almost surely and the Fourier dimension is zero. For nonzero interior parameters with $|α|\ne1/\sqrt2$, the critical Sobolev index is half the Fourier dimension minus $1/2$. The chaos fails to belong to the corresponding space when $|α|<1/\sqrt2$ and belongs to it when $|α|>1/\sqrt2$. For $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|β|\le\sqrt2-|α|$, we bound the Fourier coefficients at the decay power predicted by the dimension formula, up to logarithmic factors. For $0<|γ|<1$ and $α^2<1/2$, the measures obtained by multiplying the squared modulus of the smoothed chaos by $ε^{|γ|^2}$ converge weakly almost surely along $ε=e^{-m}$, uniformly on compact parameter sets, to explicit multiples of the real chaos at $2α$.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We reconstruct smooth cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution through classical interpolation of smooth plane conics from five distinct points, or four with their cross-ratio. If the quadratic coefficient map has rank three and the fixed cubic surface has trivial automorphism group, five polarized anti-invariant Jacobian factors of smooth Eckardt sections suffice, or four with their parameters. Both bounds are optimal. By contrast, in rank two we construct two-dimensional families of equivariantly nonisomorphic fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. The factor family also has an integral projective Lagrangian closure in an associated OG10 compactification.

papers.title: What the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determines: time reversal and principal minors
papers.abstract: What does the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determine about its generator $Q$? From the stationary start, the law of the occupation times at one time determines $Q$ up to time reversal and reversals of memoryless blocks, the sets of states that are all left at one rate with one landing law and are entered in proportion to the stationary law. These reversals commute and give exactly $2^k$ generators, with $k$ read off a tree of memoryless blocks. This leaves only time reversal when $Q$ has no rank-one cut, when there are at most 4 states, and generically. The law at one time determines the law at every time, and a generic start determines $Q$. A renewal block is a set of states that is left at the same rates from each of its states, is entered with one law, and is charged by the start in proportion to that law. From every start the law determines $Q$ up to lumped reversals, which lump disjoint renewal blocks to single states and reverse a memoryless block of the lumped chain. We also find every start that hides time reversal. At the scale of large deviations, the functional of Donsker and Varadhan determines exactly the principal minors of $-Q$.

papers.title: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
papers.abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\mathrm{deg}( x_p )=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles Kátai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $β_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

papers.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
papers.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is almost an order of magnitude faster than a comparable FEM. Finally, the Neural Physics method is applied to a real-world test case with integrated experimental data and simulates the infiltration of water through a rain garden. This new approach therefore provides a route to efficiently and accurately solve Richards equation for a wide array of hydrological applications.

papers.title: Patch LegONet: Resolving Localized High-Frequency PDE Dynamics with Low-Frequency Operator Blocks
papers.abstract: Localized interfaces, layers, and shocks can require high spatial resolution even when most of a partial differential equation (PDE) solution remains smooth. In global spectral methods, resolving these features requires increasing the approximation order across the entire domain. LegONet builds PDE solvers from reusable mechanism blocks, but its global coefficient representation faces the same limitation. We introduce Patch LegONet, which reuses pretrained mechanism blocks on smaller physical patches to resolve localized fine scales. The solution consists of a global background and local corrections. Mapping a fixed reference representation onto smaller patches increases local resolution without enlarging the blocks. The corrections join smoothly to the global background at patch boundaries. Differential operators are rescaled analytically to account for each patch's physical size. Nonlinear mechanisms are evaluated on the combined solution to include interactions between the background and local corrections. Patches can move, merge, or be removed during rollout while the pretrained patch blocks remain frozen. Six experiments on Allen-Cahn and viscous Burgers equations assess static, multiple, and moving patches in one to three dimensions. At comparable numbers of degrees of freedom, Patch LegONet consistently lowers the final relative solution error compared with global refinement. The reduction is approximately one order of magnitude in most tests. These results extend mechanism reuse across spatial scales and provide a practical route to local refinement in learned PDE solvers.

papers.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
papers.abstract: We introduce Forelli--Rudin-type integral operators on the open unit ball of \(\ell^2\). We completely characterize the boundedness of these operators between weighted \(L^p\) and \(L^q\) spaces for all \(p,q\in[1,\infty]\), as well as their membership in every Schatten class of operators between the corresponding weighted \(L^2\) spaces. We also establish trace formulas for these operators that cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by a formal passage to the limit as the dimension tends to infinity. Our results are not merely infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). Rather, they reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the fundamental geometric and measure-theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. A key ingredient in our proofs is the establishment of new Forelli--Rudin-type asymptotic estimates in infinite dimensions. These estimates also provide new insights into the development of function theory on the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

papers.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
papers.abstract: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ ($0<δ<π$) from its finite oversampling data $f(j),-n+1\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formulas have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. A recent sinh regularized formula achieved so far the best rate $$ O(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(π-δ)n)). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}$ satisfying $$ \frac{c_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}\le ρ_{n,δ}\le \frac{C_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}, 0<δ\leqπ, n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C_*$ are explicit positive constants independent of $n$ and $δ$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words, $$ ρ_{n,δ} \asymp \frac{\sqrt{\tan\fracδ4}}{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-c_δ(π-δ)n), $$ where $c_δ$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,π]$ and $$ \lim_{δ\toπ^-}c_δ=1,\ \lim_{δ\to 0^+}c_δ=+\infty. $$ For one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $-n+1\le j\le 0$, we also obtain the sharp approximation order of optimally recovering function values on $[0,1]$: $$ ρ_{n,δ}^-\asymp \sqrt{δ/π}\sin^n(δ/2),\ 0<δ<π,\ n\ge1, $$ which improves the celebrated result of H. J. Landau on extrapolation of bandlimited functions.

papers.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points in the plane developed by Haiman.

papers.title: Complement Cancellation and the Spectral Characterization of Three-Point Recurrence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate both two-sided and one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence within the framework of weakly mixing measure-preserving systems. As our principal result, we establish an exact spectral characterization for the failure of two-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence: namely, a subset \(R\subseteq\mathbb N\) fails to possess this property if and only if there exist a continuous symmetric probability measure \(σ\) on \(\mathbb T\) and a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying \[ 2\widehatσ(n)+\widehatσ(2n)\leq-\varepsilon \qquad(n\in R). \] Our proof of the necessity relies upon a complement-symmetrized correlation identity, whereas the converse is achieved through a construction involving a stationary Gaussian system, a bounded odd observable, Hermite expansions, and an independent Bernoulli extension. Furthermore, we extend this characterization to three-point polynomial configurations as well as to actions of countable abelian groups. In addition, we derive an unconditional analogue in which arbitrary symmetric probability measures take the place of continuous ones, thereby demonstrating a strict separation between the ergodic and weakly mixing classes of recurrence. Subsequently, we turn our attention to the distinction between two-sided and ordinary one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence. It is shown that a suitable negative spectral condition compels the failure of one-sided recurrence. More remarkably, we construct an explicit weakly mixing system wherein the quadratic spectral expression remains uniformly positive, yet the presence of a negative cubic correlation still induces a one-sided recurrence deficit. Consequently, it follows that two-point spectral data alone are insufficient to govern one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence.

papers.title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.

papers.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

papers.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. Our main result concerns products of convex bodies. Each block contains an inner ball and lies in a concentric outer ball. The inner radii have a common positive lower bound, and each outer radius is at most a fixed multiple of the corresponding inner radius. This class includes common constraints such as balls and boxes. On each prescribed feasible set of dimension $d$ in this class, every deterministic algorithm using a local oracle needs $\exp(Ω(d))$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case at fixed, sufficiently small accuracies $δ$ and $ε$. The objective Lipschitz and initial objective-value gap bounds are fixed, and each constructed function has a global minimizer in the interior of the feasible set. For broader classes of constraints, supplementary results show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. The constants depend on the interior-ball radius and, for inequalities, the local Lipschitz and Slater bounds. These supplementary results cover closed sets that are star-shaped with respect to a ball and convex coercive inequalities with a Slater point, and hold even for convex objectives.

papers.title: A Dobrushin-Major-Taqqu Theorem for Hilbert Space-Valued Random Variables
papers.abstract: Let $\{X_t\}_{ t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary Gaussian process taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb H_1$, with long-range dependence defined in the spectral domain through a memory operator $A:\mathbb H_1 \to \mathbb H_1$. For square-integrable, nonlinear operators $G:\mathbb H_1\to\mathbb H_2$, taking values in another separable Hilbert space $\mathbb H_2$, we establish a non-central limit theorem for the centered partial-sum process of $\{G[X_t]\}_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$, whenever $G[X_t]$ inherits the long-range dependence behavior from its Gaussian input process. We identify an operator normalization that accounts for both the underlying memory structure, characterized by the memory operator $A$, and the nonlinear transformation $G$. The limiting Hilbert space-valued process is, in general, non-Gaussian and can be expressed as multiple Wiener integrals involving only finitely many Wiener chaos orders along fixed directions in $\mathbb{H}_2$. The proof introduces a Hilbert space-valued generalization of the reduction principle, identifying the dominant Hermite components and showing that the remainder is negligible under our operator normalization. We employ our results to prove non-central limit theorems for nonlinear transformations of functional FARIMA processes and sojourn functionals of temporally dependent spherical Gaussian fields.

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
papers.abstract: We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.

papers.title: On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
papers.abstract: The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$ of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional subsphere of $\mathcal{S}$ spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.

papers.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not scalar-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in[0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.

papers.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-contractive bijection of a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space $(X, d)$. We show that $F$ is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits: for every $a \in X$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, $0 \le d(Fx, Fy) - d(x, y) < \varepsilon$ for all $y$ and all $x$ sufficiently far in the backward orbit of $a$. More precisely, $d = λ^{-} + D_0$, where the asymptotic distance $λ^{-}(x, y) = \lim_k d(F^{-k}x, F^{-k}y)$ is the largest quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which $F$ is an isometry, and the defect $D_0(x, y)$ lies between explicit bounds given by $λ^{-}$ and by a function $c$ that is nondecreasing along orbits and tends to $0$ along backward orbits. On each orbit, $λ^{-}$ induces, after completion, an invariant quasi-pseudo-metric on a compact metrizable monothetic group on which $F$ acts as a rotation, with the compact group topology. Conversely, every infinite compact metrizable monothetic group, with any rotation by a generator and any invariant quasi-pseudo-metric whose symmetrization is a compatible metric, arises in this way from a map that is not an isometry. Every such $c$ occurs over every possible $λ^{-}$, and the defects on a single orbit are characterized. These results give a structural answer to a classification question from the author's paper on the toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973), a non-isometric bijection of this kind answering a question of Zavarzina. Three examples on the integers show that the defect is not determined by $c$, and that the question, read as asking for a toll charged on descents only, has a negative answer, even up to bi-Lipschitz conjugacy. The results hold for quasi-pseudo-metric spaces in which every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence. Except for the statements listed at the end, among them the completion to a compact group, the results are machine-checked in Lean.

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ norm and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

papers.title: On Higher Order Elliptic Differential Operators
papers.abstract: In this note we examine the positive preserving properties, or the lack thereof, for Green's operators of elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds. We will obtain the existence of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds whose lowest eigenvalue is not simple, and the existence of a large family of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds that only have signed eigenfunctions associated with the lowest eigenvalue. That is, we will see that there is both "good news" and "bad news" when one studies the positivity preserving properties of Green's operators associated with higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds and the eigenproblem for higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
papers.abstract: We study separation points for the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and boundary data compactly supported in space and time. We call a space-time point on the boundary and outside the spatial support of the data a separation point of a velocity component if the component takes both signs on sets of positive measure in every sufficiently small adjacent neighborhood. The main ingredient of the analysis is the explicit representation of the velocity and pressure in terms of the boundary data using the confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, under the regularity and unimodality assumptions, log-concavity of the temporal profile yields a unique separation time for the tangential component at every boundary point with \(|x_i|>1\), while the normal component has exactly two separation times for sufficiently large \(|x'|\). For every nonzero nonnegative temporal profile satisfying the regularity assumption, \(\partial_{x_n}^2w_n(x',0,\cdot)\) has a unique simple zero for \(t>1\) when \(|x'|\) is sufficiently large. We also obtain monotonicity and asymptotic behavior of the separation times and quantitative rates at which the corresponding normal derivatives vanish. For tangential data in \(n\geq3\), a separation time for the parallel component exists precisely when \(\partial_{x_1}R_1'ψ(x')>0\), with \(R_1'\) the first Riesz transform; log-concavity makes the separation time unique. For the remaining components, we also prove existence and uniqueness. In both cases, we derive asymptotic formulas involving spatial moments and the geometry of \(\suppψ\). We determine signs of tangential pressure derivatives and, for radial \(ψ\), establish uniqueness and asymptotics of their zeros.

papers.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
papers.abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and in practice behaves like an accelerated method. This led to the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions as well. The conjecture is false. Consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. Uniform acceleration then requires either a window whose length grows as the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate of at least the order of the inverse square root. For one filter pair with a fixed factor and a bounded window this scale of forgetting is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions that are quadratic near the minimizer. A short window, in contrast, converges locally quadratically over blocks of steps when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Pairs of geometric filters created at fixed times give a uniformly accelerated method with logarithmic memory and no problem constants, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor needs two vectors and is accelerated up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\mathbb{C}$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3\to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).

papers.title: Central Limit Theorems and Network-Free Inference for Heterogeneous Spatial Autoregressions on Sparse Graphons
papers.abstract: Network dependence is widely regarded as a fundamental obstacle to inference: outcomes linked through a graph are not independent, the graph is rarely observed in full, and models for how dependence propagates are easily misspecified. We show that for a broad class of responses generated through a random network, the obstacle is smaller than it appears. We study a heterogeneous spatial autoregression on a sparse graphon, in which each node's response is a weighted average of its neighbors' responses with a node-specific, nonparametric coefficient plus a node-specific input, and we prove that sample means and smooth functions of vector means are asymptotically Gaussian down to average degree nearly logarithmic in the population size, allowing unbounded graphons with hubs and heavy-tailed inputs. The limiting variance interpolates exactly between two regimes according to the sampling fraction. When the observed nodes are a vanishing fraction of the population, the variance is the marginal variance of the response, the ordinary sample variance is consistent, and the usual $t$-interval is valid with no knowledge of the network. The proof averages over the graph rather than conditioning on it, isolating the behavior of the response through an exact identity for resolvents of Markov kernels and controlling the network noise by an Efron-Stein inequality; neither step requires the walk-by-walk covariance bounds of fixed-network analyses. Consequences for regression with node-level and network-derived covariates are derived.

papers.title: Embedding dense minors via crux
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

papers.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
papers.abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

papers.title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $δ_i(g)=X_i$ and $δ^α(g)=(\partial^αh^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $δ^α(g)=0$ for $|α|=(°h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $δ^α(g)(x_0)/α!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic not 3
papers.abstract: This article takes place in the extension and generalization proposed by Corredor, Deloro and Wiscons of the works of Dickson and Wagner regarding the Classification of minimal $\text{Sym}(n)$- and $\text{Alt}(n)$-modules. In particular, we classify the minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(6)$-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(n)$- and $\text{Sym}(n)$-modules with an additive dimension.

papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing \(R=|X_1|\), the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass exactly when \(\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty\); otherwise they converge to zero. Radial and Fourier--radial approximations have distinct sharp \(L^q\) convergence criteria at each \(0<q<1\); convergence at every such order holds for both families exactly when \(\mathbb{E}e^{sR}<\infty\) for every \(0<s<2\). In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors multiplied by \((\log n)^{1/4}\) and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. A uniformly bounded input family gives uncountably many coefficient-limit laws inequivalent under nonzero deterministic complex rescaling. We distinguish these laws using exact weighted tails under \(\mathbb{E}I_0(2R)<\infty\), where \(I_0\) is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments. For \(\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-λu^α\), \(0<α<1\) and \(λ>0\), the normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, while every positive limit moment diverges; we determine the logarithmic tails. Finite limiting moments need not imply convergence of the original coefficient moments. In the positive-limit class, coefficient periodograms recover the critical measure and energy normalization gives Gaussian limits. Hardy nonmembership holds under finite variance alone; the positive-limit class has sharp weighted Bergman criteria for \(0<p\le2\) and boundary Sobolev threshold \(s=-1/2\).

papers.title: Magnetic billiards: duality and magnetic Radon property
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2π/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of Dirichlet problems in supercritically perforated domains via quantification by torsional rigidity
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem $-\mathrm{div}(A^{\varepsilon}\nabla u^{\varepsilon}) = f$ on varying open sets $D^{\varepsilon}$, with uniformly elliptic coefficients $A^{\varepsilon}$, in the regime where the solutions vanish in the limit for every source. For periodically perforated domains, this is the supercritical regime. We show that the torsional rigidity $T(D^{\varepsilon})$ is the natural normalization: up to a subsequence, $u^{\varepsilon}/T(D^{\varepsilon})$ converges weakly as measures to $kf$ for every continuous source $f$, where $k$ is a nonzero finite measure independent of $f$, which we call the effective measure. The key ingredient is an estimate comparing $u^{\varepsilon}$ with the product of $f$ and the torsion function, whose rate depends on the domains only through $T(D^{\varepsilon})$. We also show that this rate is optimal. No structural assumption on the perforation is needed, and the results hold for relaxed Dirichlet problems. Every nonzero finite measure arises as an effective measure, so the continuity of the source cannot be dropped in general. For rougher sources, we characterize the convergence by a condition on the domains alone, expressed through their torsion functions or, equivalently, their Poincaré constants. We also prove that the effective measure is local, satisfies optimal two-sided bounds and is monotone with respect to the coefficients, and we study the role of the antisymmetric parts of the coefficients.

papers.title: Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: For $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\geq 3$ and an $r$-graph (i.e., an $r$-uniform hypergraph) $H$, the Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every red/blue coloring of the hyperedges of the $N$-vertex complete $r$-graph $K_N^{(r)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(r)}$. For every integer $r\geq 3$, we characterize all $r$-graphs $H$ for which $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$. Explicitly, we prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, that $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of a lexicographic power of $K_r^{(r)}$. This concludes an extensive line of work initiated by Erdős and Hajnal in 1972 on characterizing the polynomial growth of off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers.

papers.title: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared weighted reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the weighted-norm optimality and coefficient-space quasi-optimality of local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
papers.abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided. Moreover, we show that it is a braided module category over a suitable monoidal subcategory.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: Uniform Confinement for One-Dimensional Pressureless Euler--Poisson: Existence and Asymptotics
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are attractive at long ranges serve as simplified models that describe aggregation phenomena. We prove uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system where the potential satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions, requiring the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. When the potential is semiconvex, these bounds yield compactness of time-translated trajectories, which converge to a solution on all of $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ of a simpler equation. Often, these limiting solutions possess substantial rigidity that determines the asymptotic behavior of the original solution, which we explore in a few applications. This method is robust with respect to the choice of potential, and in contrast to previous work does not require the solution operator to have a closed-form expression. As a corollary of our uniform bounds, we also obtain existence of solutions for non-semiconvex potentials, although such solutions may not retain stickiness.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the Néron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$. When $X\subset\mathbb P^r$ is not necessarily a complete intersection, assuming that the Picard group of $X$ is generated by the hyperplane section class, we obtain the coarse bound $p_a(C)\leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+\left(\frac{11}{24}n+4\right)$ for $d\gg n$.

papers.title: Complete solutions and subharmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X \rightarrow X$ the canonical bundle, and $T_X\coloneqq K_X^{-1}\rightarrow X$ the dual bundle of the canonical bundle. For each integer $r \geq 2$, each $q \in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of the square root $K_X^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle, we canonically obtain a Higgs bundle $(\K_r,Φ(q))\rightarrow X$, which is called a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal solution $h = (h_1, \dots, h_r)$ to the Hitchin equation on a cyclic Higgs bundle yields $r-1$ Hermitian metrics $H_1, \dots, H_{r-1}$ on $T_X\rightarrow X$, defined as $H_j \coloneqq h_j^{-1} \otimes h_{j+1}$ for each $j=1,\dots, r-1$, while $h_1$, $h_r$, and $q$ yield a Hermitian metric $H_r$ on $T_X \rightarrow X$ which is degenerate at the zero set of $q$. A diagonal solution is said to be complete if the Kähler metrics induced by $H_1,\dots, H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki established a theorem stating that, for any Riemann surface $X$ and any $q$ that is non-zero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete solution $h$ to the Hitchin equation for the cyclic Higgs bundle $(\K_r,Φ(q))$ with $\det(h)=1$. The holomorphic section $q$ induces a subharmonic weight function $φ_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X\rightarrow X$, and the Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through this weight function. In previous work, the author introduced a variant of the Hitchin equation associated with an arbitrary subharmonic weight function $\varphi$. In this paper, we extend the Li--Mochizuki theorem to complete solutions of the extended Hitchin equation associated to any subharmonic weight function $\varphi$ that is not identically $-\infty$ unless $X$ is hyperbolic.

papers.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined on Curves of Genus 2
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

papers.title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
papers.abstract: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets. We prove that it does. The proof combines direct decompositions with an auxiliary ordering of connected ordered sets and a careful choice of intervals of maximum height. We then extend the reconstruction result to several forms of repeated exponentiation.

papers.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

papers.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
papers.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and Şavk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite and Borel's theorem, the symmetries of the hyperbolic knot Th(p,q) are the symmetries of its standard diagram once that diagram has no non-trivial flypes (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes in the sense made precise in the paper (a closely related statement is due to Shimizu, Gill and Joshi) and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

papers.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le α<1$, we construct a $C^{1,α}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. In step-2 Carnot groups, we show that every $C^{1,α}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension less than or equal to $q-\frac{1+α}2$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. This upper bound is actually attained by the $C^{1,α}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces of our construction, hence their Euclidean Hausdorff dimension is maximal. As a technical result of independent interest, we show that the implicit function associated with a $C^{1,α}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface is $\frac{1+α}2$-Euclidean Hölder continuous, with $0\leα\le 1$. In particular, $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces in step-2 Carnot groups are rectifiable in the classical sense, therefore the range of unrectifiability $0\le α<1$ is sharp. We also prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. The previous results extend the seminal work of Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group and settle a question concerning the singular surface they constructed, by proving that its $\frac52$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure is zero.

papers.title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
papers.abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.

papers.title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
papers.abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-Hölder in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(φ)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity established by Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

papers.title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
papers.abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.

papers.title: Explaining the Saliency Map Sparsity of Adversarially-Trained Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Understanding why deep neural networks make a given prediction is of great importance for their safe deployment. In computer vision, saliency maps, which highlight the image region most influential for a prediction, remain a widely-used form of explanation. An empirical observation is the apparent sparsity of gradient saliency maps of adversarially-trained neural networks. In this paper, we propose a theoretical explanation of this phenomenon for two-layer ReLU networks. We build on the established equivalence of adversarial training to the minimization of the empirical risk with weight-decay penalization and an added adversarial total variation term -- valid for certain loss functions. As the number of data points and neurons grows and the regularization parameters are sent to zero at appropriate rates, we prove that minimizers converge to a Bayes classifier with minimal gradient and Barron norm. Sparsity appears since for adversarial training with $\ell_\infty$-attacks the gradient norm is anisotropic and favors axis-aligned / sparse gradients. We illustrate our theoretical findings experimentally by evaluating the gradient $\ell_1$-norm and thresholded sparsity of naturally versus adversarially trained models.

papers.title: Chiral Extensions of Cotangent Yangian
papers.abstract: We construct chiral extensions of the cotangent Yangian using vertex algebroids. At zero level, the construction yields a vertex algebra with a compatible coproduct, whose Zhu reduction recovers the cotangent Yangian of Abedin and Niu. We also construct vertex algebra extensions at non-zero levels and study level-additive coproducts. The zero-level vertex algebra admits two natural quasi-conformal structures. We compute the corresponding sphere one-point conformal blocks and equip each block space with an associative product induced by the coproduct.
