For the first quasi-conformal structure, the blocks space can be identified with the dual of a certain Lie algebroid homology; for the second, we describe the block algebra and its classical limit in terms of mini-twistor geometry.

papers.title: Uniformly Positive Scalar Curvature on Manifold Interiors
papers.abstract: We obtain topological obstructions to the existence of a complete Riemannian metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature on the interiors of certain 4-manifolds using Seiberg--Witten theory. In particular, no punctured blowups of a homotopy K3 manifold admit complete metrics of uniformly positive scalar curvature. Further, let $X$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n$. We show that if $n=6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of uniformly positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric which is a product near the boundary. In dimension 5, an analogous result holds under additional hypotheses and after possibly changing the smooth structure on $X$. If $n=5,6,7$ and $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric with minimal boundary. One ingredient is a new PSC deformation result.

papers.title: Comparing the reliability of coherent systems with heterogeneous, dependent and distribution-free components
papers.abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in comparing the reliability of systems with dependent components. Most of the recent works consider Archimedean copulas to define the dependency structure of systems and examine specific familiy of distributions. In this work, we provide distribution-free results to compare, in the usual stochastic order under some majorization conditions, coherent systems with heterogeneous and dependent components where the dependency structure can be defined by any copula. Applications of our main results for specific copulas and different families of marginal distributions are also given.

papers.title: The set-theorist's real numbers
papers.abstract: Descriptive set theorists often refer to elements of the Baire space, $\mathcal{N} = {}^ωω$, as ``reals.'' In this expository article, we present mathematical justification for this practice and highlight the advantages of working with $\mathcal{N}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ in the context of descriptive set theory.

papers.title: Presentation of Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local rings
papers.abstract: We obtain presentations of Borel subgroups of certain Chevalley groups and Kac-Moody groups of simply laced type. More precisely, we show that Borel subgroups of simply laced Chevalley groups over a commutative, unital ring (satisfying a minor technical condition), are the amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups, generalising a result of Tits over fields (different from $\mathbb{F}_2$). We moreover show that Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local Bézout domains also have a presentation as an amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups as soon as this holds for their rank 3 subgroups. In particular we deduce that Borel subgroups of simply laced Kac-Moody groups over a local Bézout domain (with residue field different from $\mathbb{F}_2$) have such a presentation if and only if they are of 3-spherical type.

papers.title: Rank-One HCIZ Integrals and Multiplicative Convolutions
papers.abstract: We study how spectral averaging interacts with the logarithm in large-dimensional rank-one Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber (HCIZ) integrals. For independent bi-unitarily invariant matrices $A,B$ with uniformly bounded deterministic singular values and weakly convergent empirical spectral measures of their Gram matrices, the integral for $(BA)^*(BA)\otimes\mathbf{1}_N$ has two limiting descriptions at speed $N^2$ for small real parameters: averaging its logarithm gives free multiplicative convolution, whereas taking the logarithm after averaging gives classical multiplicative convolution. We also prove an exact finite-dimensional equality between this annealed integral and the one for $(A^*A)\otimes(B^*B)$. For any fixed $k\ge3$ factors under the hypotheses stated for $A,B$, the annealed limits at speed $N^k$ generally differ for small positive parameters, and we characterize the equality cases. For tensor products with any fixed number $k$ of factors, global Haar vectors at speed $N^k$ and product-state vectors at speed $N$ yield classical and free multiplicative convolution, respectively, for small real parameters under the corresponding hypotheses. We also derive the known multiplicativity of the $S$-transform.

papers.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Step-size selection remains a central challenge in large-scale neural network optimization; conservative steps slow convergence, while aggressive steps can destabilize it. We combine Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) and propose a lightweight framework that decouples direction selection from step-size. ZFO uses a trusted first-order optimizer to determine the direction and performs zeroth-order evaluations only along this one-dimensional subspace to choose how far to move. Using the current {gradient information} and two additional objective function evaluations, ZFO instances construct a local model of the objective function along the proposed direction and select a curvature-aware step within a bounded search interval. This yields an adaptive step-selection mechanism that costs less than a full line search. We provide theoretical guarantees to show that shared-sample evaluations produce reliable finite-difference curvature estimates, that the induced local model selects a near-optimal step along the search interval, and that ZFO converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point. Across the evaluated settings, language models and datasets, ZFO frequently improves optimization and final performance relative to fixed-step first-order baselines, with the magnitude and preferred local model depending on the objective. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/nizswan/Zeroth-First-Order-Framework.

papers.title: Zong's problem on $2d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball
papers.abstract: We prove that the intersection of $2d$ half-spaces containing the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{d}$. Equality in the radius bound characterizes the cube up to orthogonal transformations. The proof gives a lower bound for the average squared norm of the vertices, weighted by the Gaussian measures of their normal cones. This estimate follows from an inequality for the Gaussian measures of a simplicial cone and its projected facets, which in turn reduces to a linear estimate for the Gaussian centroid of a simplicial cone. We also discuss a quadratic extension of the problem and give a bound for it using an independent spectral argument. This bound implies that the intersection of any $m > d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{m}\,\ln\frac{m}{m-d}$.

papers.title: Existence of three solutions for parametric $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with a nonlinear elliptic problem in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ involving the $p$-Laplacian operator with $p>N$. Under suitable assumptions on the potential term and on the nonlinearity, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational and relies on two different three critical points theorems. The results extend to higher dimensions some recent multiplicity theorems for one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian equations on the real line, and provide explicit ranges for the parameter $λ> 0$ ensuring the existence of multiple solutions, which are nonnegative under additional sign conditions. The nontriviality of the solutions is also discussed. Finally, applications to problems whose nonlinearities have separated variables are presented.

papers.title: Elections, Fractional Dichromatic Number and Domination in Tournaments and Digraphs
papers.abstract: The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of induced acyclic sets into which its vertex set can be partitioned. The fractional dichromatic number is its fractional relaxation. Bourneuf, Charbit and Thomassé showed that the domination number of a tournament can be bounded as an (exponential) function of its fractional dichromatic number. This naturally leads to the question of finding a polynomial bound. We show that this bound is linear. To do this, we show a connection between undominated sets in elections and dominating sets in tournaments with bounded fractional dichromatic number. Within this framework, we also connect the well-known question of the existence of small Condorcet winning sets in elections to domination problems in digraphs with fractional dichromatic number less than 2. Thus, we open a new path to investigating these popular open problems in social choice from the perspective of graph theory.

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: When Should a Human Take Back Control? Optimal Delegation under Turbulent AI Risk
papers.abstract: When should a human take control from an autonomous AI agent, how much checking is worthwhile, and when should autonomy resume? These decisions become harder when incidents cluster and recent errors signal elevated risk. Exploratory analyses of AgentLogs coding-agent traces and ODCV-Bench task runs show higher held-out log likelihood for Hawkes incident-history models than matched no-history baselines, with positive gains whose conditional $90\%$ intervals exclude zero. AgentLogs evaluates continuous-time incident timing and type; ODCV evaluates failure occurrence at discrete decisions. Motivated by this predictive evidence, we formulate a continuous-time delegation problem that jointly chooses productive action, verification effort, and switching rates between human-directed, AI-assisted operation and autonomous AI operation. The model assumes that verification weakens incident propagation and balances project benefits against operating, supervision, risk, and handoff costs. Our Hawkes-PPO method summarizes observed incidents with exponential memory filters and learns these decisions from rewards. In synthetic experiments, it achieves a higher evaluated objective than either fixed regime and PPO without history filters, and approaches an approximate full-information benchmark. Further experiments show how incident excitation and supervision costs shape delegation.

papers.title: Common invariant measures for beta-transformations: affine relations and squared bases
papers.abstract: We classify the common invariant probabilities of two beta-transformations in two families. In the first, the bases satisfy $γ=aβ+c>1$ with $β>1$ irrational, $a,c\in\mathbb Q$ and $a+c\ne1$. In the second, they are an irrational $β>1$ and its square. In both families every common singular invariant probability is the point mass at zero; combining this with the classification of coincident Rényi--Parry measures gives all common invariant probabilities, with no entropy, ergodicity or multiplicative-independence hypothesis.

papers.title: Dynamic Service Recommendation with Congestion-Dependent Joining: Near-Optimal and Constant-Factor Approximation Algorithms
papers.abstract: Modern service platforms often show customers real-time congestion information, such as anticipated waiting times, before they decide whether to use a service. This creates an intertemporal tradeoff: directing a customer to a service may generate immediate value, but the resulting congestion can make that service less attractive to future customers. We study this tradeoff in a finite-horizon problem in which a platform recommends one of multiple services, each represented by a queue, and customers' joining probabilities decrease with congestion. We show that optimal recommendations generally depend on the joint congestion state and cannot be reduced to indices that depend only on each service's own state. Hence, exact dynamic programming suffers from a curse of dimensionality. We develop approximation algorithms that retain progressively less of this joint state. First, we construct a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme that achieves a $(1-ε)$-approximation for any $ε>0$. It rounds the model primitives and truncates the relevant queue lengths to compress the joint state into a histogram over service types, and our coupling arguments bound the resulting revenue loss. Second, under general monotone joining and service capacities, we study policies that retain only per-service information. A greedy policy, which uses only each service's current queue length, is a tight $1/2$-approximation, as it ignores the congestion externality that a customer imposes on later customers. An LP-guided algorithm that plans each service's queue-length distribution over the horizon accounts for this externality and achieves a $(1-1/e)$-approximation. Finally, monotone joining is what makes the problem tractable: with nonempty initial queues, both constant-factor guarantees hold under monotonicity, whereas without it the problem is NP-hard to approximate within any constant factor.

papers.title: Hull Games of Induced Path Convexities in Graphs
papers.abstract: In 1984, Frank Harary introduced the first convexity games in graphs, all of them based on the geodesic convexity, which is the graph convexity related to shortest paths. In 2024, Araújo et al. obtained the first PSPACE-hardness proofs on some of these geodesic games and generalized them to any graph convexity. In this paper, we investigate convexity games on several known induced path convexities: the monophonic $\mathrm{m}$-convexity and the $\ell_k$-convexities, based on induced paths and on induced paths of size at most $k$. We prove that the hull games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$, $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ and their misère variants are PSPACE-complete for every $k\ge2$ even in graphs with diameter at most 3. We also use the Sprague-Grundy Theory to obtain a polynomial time algorithm to decide the winner of the games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ for any $k\ge2$ in disjoint unions of paths and cycles. For $k\ge3$ odd, we prove that Alice (1st player) wins $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in the path $P_n$ if and only if $n$ is odd and she wins in the cycle $C_n$ if and only if $n=3$ or $n=α\cdot (k+1)-1$ with $α\ge2$. For $k\ge2$ even, the only periodic nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ obtained through extensive computational testing occurred for $k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$, e.g, $k\in\{4,12,28,60,\ldots\}$. In this case ($k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$), we prove that the nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in $P_n$ and in $C_n$ are periodic and Alice loses (resp. wins) in $P_n$ (resp. $C_n$) with $n>k$ only when $n=3k+4$ (resp. $n\in\{2k+1,5k+3\}$). Finally, we show that, for $k=2$, the game $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_2}$ in paths $P_n$ is closely related to the classical game \emph{Couples-are-Forever} of J. H. Conway: it is still an open problem if the nimber sequence is periodic or not and Alice loses only for 12 values of $n$ up to $200$ million.

papers.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
papers.abstract: On a compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold, the existence of a strictly positive plurinegative $(1,1)$-current with smooth exterior derivative implies that the canonical bundle is nef, and ample if every positive Lelong upper level set of the current has complex dimension at most two; in dimensions one and two, hyperbolicity alone suffices for ampleness. Next, we study Hermitian metrics of constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature $c$. Locally and without compactness assumptions, any such metric with $c\ne0$ is Kähler in dimension three, on balanced fourfolds, and under rank bounds on the iterated Chern curvature hull of the $(1,0)$ torsion derivative. Globally, on compact manifolds in Fujiki's class, the metric is Kähler--Einstein when $c<0$ and Kähler flat when $c=0$. Without the Fujiki hypothesis, $c=0$ need not imply Chern flatness: for every dimension $n\ge7$, we construct compact balanced nonflat examples with all four Chern--Ricci contractions vanishing. Nevertheless, on a compact Hermitian manifold with $c=0$ and vanishing first Chern--Ricci form, Kähler flatness follows if there exists a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form positive definite at one point.

papers.title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter in $\mathbb{Z}_N^d$
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic spectral synthesis on $\mathbb Z_N^d$ using the Fourier ratio, the quotient of the counting-measure $\ell^1$ and $\ell^2$ norms of the unitary Fourier transform. For supports of cardinality $N^{α+o(1)}$, the Fourier-ratio concentration exponent satisfies $0\leqκ\leq\fracα{2}$. We prove a finite-scale synthesis estimate that uses either the Fourier ratio of a function or that of its support indicator. In particular, the indicator condition applies uniformly to arbitrary weights on the support. Uniform $\ell^p$ bounds imply decay of the largest Fourier coefficient when $2\leq p<\frac{2(d-2κ)}{α-2κ}$, with every finite $p\geq2$ allowed at maximal concentration. Random unions of cosets show that the finite critical exponent is sharp for every admissible pair in each prescribed ambient dimension, along prime-power moduli. We also determine the exact synthesis constant for sets with a transitive group of affine symmetries. For paraboloids this constant is an explicit divisor sum. The formula proves endpoint synthesis along powers of a fixed odd prime, although the endpoint fails along primes. Along products of distinct small primes, synthesis extends to a larger exponent. These families have the same Fourier-ratio exponent. Finally, we relate Fourier concentration to generalized Salem estimates, additive energy, Fourier algebra norms, and necessary conditions for extension estimates.

papers.title: A finite Livshits theorem and local length spectrum rigidity
papers.abstract: We show that for closed negatively curved Riemannian manifolds whose length spectrum is exponentially separated, the length spectrum is a local isometry invariant. The main tool used in the proof is a finitary version of the Livshits theorem with an exponential tail that improves with the regularity.

papers.title: Norms of Schneider--Teitelbaum Polynomials in $p$-adic Fourier Theory
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and let $P_n(X)$ denote the Lubin--Tate analogues of the binomial polynomials arising in the $p$-adic Fourier theory of Schneider and Teitelbaum. For a particular choice of Lubin--Tate logarithm, we determine explicitly the norms of the functions $P_n(xΩ)$ on the Banach spaces of locally $F$-analytic functions of fixed order, where $Ω$ is a Lubin--Tate period. Our computation is based on a recent valuation formula of Ardakov and Berger for the values $P_n(Ω)$. As an application, we improve the Bannai--Kobayashi normalization of these polynomials. Each element of the resulting basis has norm one.

papers.title: Percolation Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: We study Percolation Markov Decision Processes (PMDPs), where the decision maker repeatedly moves a token through the d-dimensional integer lattice with deterministic transitions and random payoffs assigned to the edges. Payoffs are revealed before the beginning of the decision process and the decision maker aims to maximize the average accumulated payoff over a fixed horizon. First, we address general asymptotic control-theoretic questions by proving the existence of the uniform value and 0-optimal strategies. Furthermore, we examine the structural properties of optimal strategies: we establish the existence of stationary 0-optimal strategies for a class where the token moves in a fixed direction independent of the player's actions, and we provide low-dimensional examples to illustrate their complexity. Moreover, we introduce a dimensional lifting property that allows PMDPs to be approximated by lower-dimensional PMDPs, offering a representation of the approximation of critical probability thresholds in percolation theory via PMDPs.

papers.title: Uniqueness of embedded minimal Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{CP}^2$
papers.abstract: We prove that any embedded minimal Lagrangian torus in the complex projective plane is congruent to the Clifford torus. This settles the orientable case of Oh's classification conjecture. The proof uses a new two-point function constructed from Hermitian products of normalized horizontal lifts.

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

papers.title: Equilibrium selection and sharp convergence rates for a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with simplex-volume interactions
papers.abstract: We study a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. The associated free energy is not isplacement semiconvex when the simplex dimension $n$ is at least two. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a noncompact continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. The limit is then selected by the initial covariance, whose eigenvectors and eigenvalue gaps are preserved by the flow. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates. For compactly supported initial data with nonstationary covariance, the sharp rate is the smaller of the covariance relaxation rate and three times the slowest transport rate, provided that the third moments do not vanish along the directions of slowest transport. The skewness of the initial datum, rather than its covariance, may therefore dictate the long-time behavior.

papers.title: An inverse problem on eigenfunction triple products
papers.abstract: On a connected closed smooth Riemannian manifold, the algebraic structure of the Laplace eigenfunctions, as described by eigenfunction triple products, uniquely determines the geometry. We refine this correspondence by introducing the notion of an $N$-product eigenbasis, which consists of eigenfunctions whose pairwise products may be written as linear combinations of at most $N$ basis elements. We prove that a manifold admits a $2$-product eigenbasis if and only if it is a flat torus. We also prove an analogous result for Laplace eigenvectors of bounded-degree graphs.

papers.title: On the Markov semigroup generated in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by linear fractional divergence form operators
papers.abstract:
Let $0<s<1$ and $A$ be a constant symmetric positive definite matrix. Given the quadratic form $$ Q_A(u)=\int_{\R^N} A
abla^s u(x)\cdot 
abla^s u(x)\,dx, $$ where $
abla^s$ denotes the Riesz fractional gradient, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions such that $Q_A$ defines a Dirichlet form. In strike contrast with the local case $s=1$, positive definiteness of a constant matrix is not sufficient for the Markov property when $0<s<1$. We also describe the associated symmetric Markov semigroup and its $L^p$ realizations, prove the existence of a smooth nonnegative heat kernel and establish a bounded $H^\infty$ functional calculus.

papers.title: Spherical and lacunary maximal operators on rank one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type
papers.abstract: The spherical maximal operator of order $μ$ was introduced by El Kohen in the setting of real hyperbolic spaces, where its $L^p$-boundedness properties were investigated. In this paper, we extend this operator to rank-one Riemannian symmetric spaces of noncompact type and establish sufficient conditions on $μ$ for its boundedness on $L^p$, $1<p\leq\infty$. We also obtain a necessary condition for $L^p$-boundedness when $μ$ is real and $1<p<\infty$. For $1<p\leq 2$, the necessary and sufficient conditions coincide, yielding the sharp range of real $μ$ in this regime. Finally, we establish sufficient conditions for the $L^p$-boundedness of the corresponding lacunary spherical maximal operator for $1<p\leq\infty$.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra when $2 \in R^\times$, costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over these fields is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ when $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. An implementation for the standard tower over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $q = p^k$ with $p \le 2^{31}-1$ an odd prime and $k \le 12$ is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface pyfastcd, available on PyPI. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method over $\mathbb{R}$, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$ for both single and batched products and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication.

papers.title: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
papers.abstract: We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{θ\in\mathbb{R}}\int_θ^{θ+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$. The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.

papers.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
papers.abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through an effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

papers.title: Moments of crosscorrelation demerit factors of binary sequences
papers.abstract: Families of sequences with low mutual aperiodic crosscorrelation assist the design of systems for multi-user asynchronous communications and multiple-input multiple-output radar. The crosscorrelation demerit factor of a pair of sequences is the sum of the squared magnitudes of their crosscorrelation values at every shift when the sequences are normalized to unit Euclidean norm, and the merit factor is the reciprocal of the demerit factor. For each positive integer $\ell$, we endow the $2^{2 \ell}$ pairs of binary sequences of length $\ell$ with uniform probability measure and study the distribution of their crosscorrelation demerit factors. Sarwate showed that the mean value is always $1$ regardless of length $\ell$. We develop a method for finding an exact formula for the $p$th central moment (for any positive integer $p$) as a function of $\ell$. Formulae for the variance and third central moment ($p=2$ and $3$) are then obtained by hand calculations, while the fourth through sixth central moments are obtained by computer-assisted calculations. Our theory also shows that all the central moments must be strictly positive for $p\geq 2$ and $\ell \geq 3$.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: Relative Fourier--Mukai theory for algebraic spaces
papers.abstract: We study the variation of Fourier--Mukai equivalences in proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. For bounded pseudocoherent kernels, we prove that the equivalence locus is open and commutes with arbitrary Noetherian base change. To do so, we develop a theory of relative perfectness and relative quasi-perfectness for algebraic spaces. This includes a fiberwise criteria for integral transforms with nonperfect kernels. As an application, we construct an explicit autoequivalence for elliptic fibrations.

papers.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
papers.abstract: We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$σ$-weak topology. For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai. For $η(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $σ$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence. Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.

papers.title: Band edges of periodic Schrödinger operators are generically isolated and nondegenerate
papers.abstract: For periodic Schrödinger operators $H_V=-Δ+V$ with bounded real-valued potentials on $\mathbb R^d$ with $d\ge2$, we show that for generic potentials, each endpoint of every spectral gap is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and has a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point. This proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators.

papers.title: Tropical Matsusaka and Matsusaka--Ran Criteria
papers.abstract: The tropical Schottky problem asks which principally polarized tropical abelian varieties are isomorphic to tropical Jacobian varieties equipped with their canonical principal polarizations. We prove the tropical Matsusaka criterion and the tropical Matsusaka--Ran criterion, which are the main results of this paper, and show that their hypotheses are equivalent. Together with the tropical Poincaré formula proved by Gross--Shokrieh, these results give a geometric solution to the tropical Schottky problem. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to a question posed by Brannetti--Melo--Viviani. Several tools are developed for the proofs of the two criteria. In particular, we establish Hodge-type inequalities for ample tropical Cartier divisors on tropical abelian varieties and prove a splitting criterion for principally polarized tropical abelian varieties.

papers.title: A Chvátal--Erdős type condition for supereulerian digraphs with $α_{2}=4$
papers.abstract: A digraph is \textbf{supereulerian} if it contains a spanning closed trail. Let $α_2(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing no 2-cycle. In this paper, we study the supereulerianity of digraphs with arc-strong connectivity at least 2. We identify a family $\mathcal H$ of nonsupereulerian 2-arc-strong digraphs and prove that every 2-arc-strong digraph $D$ with $α_2(D)\leq 4$ is supereulerian if and only if $D\notin\mathcal H$. In particular, every digraph $D$ satisfying $α_2(D) \le 4$ and $λ(D) \ge 3$ is supereulerian.

papers.title: On the weak Lefschetz property of Artinian Gorenstein algebras of codimension three in arbitrary characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf k$ be a field, $S=\mathsf k[x,y,z]$, and $R=S/I$ be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein $\mathsf k$-algebra of codimension three. The $h$-vector of such an algebra is known to be symmetric and unimodal. Miró-Roig proved that if $\mathsf k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero and the $h$-vector of $R$ has at least three peaks, then $R$ has the weak Lefschetz property. We first observe that this statement holds over any infinite field of arbitrary characteristic, and that it follows from a theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev by an argument which is already used in special cases in the literature. We then give a second, characteristic-free proof, following the strategy of Migliore--Zanello, which is elementary and does not use the theorem of Iarrobino--Kanev, and hence does not use the Buchsbaum--Eisenbud structure theorem.

papers.title: Locally finite fixed points of branching Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We give a full characterization of the fixed points of Branching Brownian motion with critical and supercritical drifts under no additional assumptions besides it being locally finite almost surely. In particular, we do not assume finite intensity (Kabluchko, 2012) or the finite top particle (Chen-Garban-Shekhar, 2023) conditions. We also give a full characterization of the domain of attraction of the fixed points of BBM.

papers.title: Structural and Dynamical Properties of Subfactor Commuting Squares
papers.abstract: This paper explores the algebraic invariants and ergodic behavior of the finite-index inclusions forming commuting squares of $\text{II}_1$ factors. We begin by establishing how regularity, intermediate-subfactor lattices, and Weyl groups transfer across the commuting square under relative commutant and irreducibility conditions. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization, via a novel factorization theorem, of the unitary normalizers of the upper inclusion when the lower inclusion is regular. Applying these findings to crossed-product inclusions induced by discrete groups, we introduce a relative eigenbasis property that preserves regular inclusions. Finally, we contrast this by proving that a relative weak mixing condition on the group action forces the crossed-product inclusion to be singular.

papers.title: Kähler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
papers.abstract: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a Kähler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We descend according to a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via ill-curvature-conditioned, or lack thereof, landscapes. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a function, pluriharmonic or real. Using Yau's Liouville theorem, we get a small eigenvalue blow-up effect under nontrivial background interaction, geometric invariance of the endomorphism constant, and almost low rank assumptions. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but large eigenvalues can be a local condition and hold empirically on open sets even in generalized Kähler cases due to lower bounds on the Ricci potential. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric modality, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.

papers.title: Spectral and Isoperimetric Bounds on Flat Tori
papers.abstract: We record several elementary relations between spectral and isoperimetric parameters of a flat torus $\mathbb{T}_Λ= \mathbb{R}^n/Λ$ and the covariance structure of a fundamental domain $K$ for the lattice $Λ\subset \mathbb{R}^n$. For every measurable fundamental domain $K$ and nonzero vector $ξ$ in the dual lattice $Λ^*$, we observe the sharp directional variance estimate \[ \left\langle \operatorname{Cov}_K ξ,ξ\right\rangle \geq \frac{1}{12}. \] This yields a lower bound on the torus spectral gap $λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ (equivalently, the length of the shortest nonzero dual vector $λ_1(Λ^*)$) in terms of the maximal covariance of $K$: \[ λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ) = 4π^2 λ_1(Λ^*)^2 \geq \frac{π^2}{3\left\|\operatorname{Cov}_K\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}. \] Analogous sharp results are obtained for the isoperimetric profile and the Cheeger constant $D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ using an old argument of Hadwiger. In particular, when the Voronoi cell $K_Λ$ of a lattice with $\det Λ= 1$ is isotropic, the recent resolution of the Slicing Problem by Klartag and Lehec implies that \[ D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_1(Λ^*) \geq c > 0, \] where $c > 0$ is a universal constant independent of dimension $n$; this may be thought of as a positive resolution of the Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits conjecture for all flat tori. While there are lattices $Λ$ and corresponding Voronoi cells $K = K_Λ$ for which no dimension-independent converse inequality to the spectral-gap bound above can hold, we show that under a certain sectional tiling hypothesis, this inequality is in fact an equivalence (up to numerical constants).

papers.title: Twisted Conjugacy and the Construction of Induced Centrosymmetric Alternant Codes
papers.abstract: This paper presents a construction of induced centrosymmetric alternant codes based on the automorphism structures inherited from Generalized Reed-Solomon (GRS) codes. We introduce a twisted conjugacy relation naturally arising from projective semilinear transformations and establish its connection with ordinary conjugacy in the corresponding projective semilinear coset. By means of the Shintani norm, we show that, in the quadratic extension case, all admissible transformations inducing centrosymmetry have a trivial Shintani norm and therefore belong to a unique conjugacy class in the semilinear coset. We further characterize the explicit forms of these transformations and establish a transport theorem describing how twisted conjugation acts on the supports and multipliers of GRS codes. These results provide an algebraic framework for constructing and analyzing induced centrosymmetric alternant codes.

papers.title: Critical avalanche tails in the one-dimensional anisotropic Bak--Sneppen model
papers.abstract: We study avalanche ranges in the anisotropic Bak-Sneppen model on $\mathbb Z$. In exponential coordinates, the right endpoint $X_t$ of an avalanche started at the origin has a nonlinear jump evolution whose tails satisfy a closed triangular system. Write $m(t)=\mathbb E[X_t]$ and let $t_c$ be the threshold for finite $m(t)$. Below $t_c$, the endpoint has exponential moments and $m(t)\sim 2/(t_c-t)$. At criticality it is finite almost surely, but $\mathbb P(X_{t_c}\geq k)\geq ck^{-1/2}$ and $\mathbb E[X_{t_c}^{1/3}]=\infty$. We propose two approaches for the critical estimates. First, a simple compensation argument, based on an extremal inequality for decreasing probability masses, yields a $k^{-2/3}$ lower bound. This already proves equality of the susceptibility and infinite-avalanche thresholds. We then exploit the additional fact that the exact evolution preserves geometric mixtures for the tails, which sharpens the bound to $k^{-1/2}$. Finally, by freezing the grafting law at criticality, we prove that the avalanche is infinite with positive probability for every $t>t_c$.

papers.title: From algebraic orthogonality to RAAG embedding obstructions in hierarchically hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We extend the Kim--Koberda obstruction arguments for embeddings of right-angled Artin groups (RAAGs) to a class of hierarchically hyperbolic groups (HHGs). To this end, we isolate algebraic conditions on HHGs relating domain orthogonality to the decomposition and commutation of group elements. Under these conditions, we obtain a clique-graph obstruction to RAAG embeddings into such HHGs using the \emph{expanded core graph}, which we introduce as a counterpart of both the extension graphs of RAAGs and the disjointness graphs of curves on surfaces. When the HHG structure has rank at most two, the expanded core graph itself gives a complete embedding criterion.

papers.title: The universal cover of the second-type locus of a cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the surface of second-type lines on a general cubic fourfold has fundamental group of order two. Its universal cover, constructed by Huybrechts, is obtained by considering the two ramification points of the Gauss map along each second-type line.

papers.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
papers.abstract: We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.

papers.title: Analytical Evaluation of Signature 2 Ramanujan-Type Series via Elementary Transformations and Companion Harmonic Expansions
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit analytical evaluation of the known rational Ramanujan-type series for $1/π$ of signature $2$. Focusing on the singular moduli $k_r$ for $r \in \{2, 3, 4, 7\}$, we show that these invariants and their underlying elliptic identities follow from elementary transformations of complete elliptic integrals of the first and second kind. Using this framework, we derive two companion families of rational harmonic Ramanujan-type series for the reciprocal of $π$ involving higher-degree polynomials

papers.title: Flexibility of the isometric immersion system in arbitrary dimension and codimension and the energy scaling of prestrained thin films
papers.abstract: We prove that, for a given $C^{r,β}$-regular Riemann metric posed on a $d$-dimensional domain, every short immersion into the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{d+k}$, can be uniformly approximated by exact isometric immersions of regularity $C^{1,α}$ for any $α<α_0=\min\{\frac{r+β}{2}, \frac{1}{1+d(d+1)/k}\}$. Our theorem recovers several previously known results as special cases. The novelty thereof lies in providing a unified flexibility statement for arbitrary dimensions $d$ and codimensions $k$, while also treating the so far uncharted range $k\in (1, \frac{d(d+1)}{2}-d+1)\setminus \{d\}$, where no corresponding general result was previously available. Our threshold flexibility exponent $α_0$ agrees with that previously obtained for the closely related Monge-Ampère system. As an application, we prove a new estimate in the quantitative immersability of thin prestrained films, setting the scaling exponent of the infimum of non-Euclidean energies in presence of an arbitrary prestrain metric, and in the limit of the film's vanishing thickness, at $\frac{4α_0}{α_0+1}$.

papers.title: WarpMPC: Large-Batch MPC on GPU via ADMM with Unrolled $LDL^\top$ Factorization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces numerical optimizations for maximizing throughput on GPU when solving large batches (10,000 to over 100,000) of sequential quadratic programming (SQP) iterations, where all problems have the same structure. The optimizations are implemented in a toolbox WarpMPC for model-predictive control (MPC) in JAX and Warp. Based on the insight that all MPC problem instances in a batch share the same sparsity in time, cost, and constraints, we propose unrolling sparse linear factorizations and solves, which dominate alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) solver runtime. We avoid memory access bottlenecks and wasting computations via optimized memory layout, padding-reducing segmentation of the unrolled factorization, and dependency level scheduled backsolves, additionally accelerating sensitivity computation. We achieve throughputs of 8,000 to 250,000 SQP iterations per second on nonlinear cartpole, quadrotor, and humanoid robot benchmarks, outperforming baselines by 3$\times$ to 25$\times$. We illustrate practical usefulness by synthesizing a dataset and training a neural network approximation of an MPC in under 5 minutes that stabilizes a nano quadrotor in hardware experiments.

papers.title: Local linear convergence of the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm for semidefinite programming
papers.abstract: Primal-dual first-order methods are widely used for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP), but their ability to compute highly accurate solutions is not explained by global convergence theory alone. We study the local convergence of the primal--dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method for SDP. We first show that PDHG converges linearly, uniformly for all starting points near a KKT point, if and only if the KKT mapping is metrically subregular at that point. We then show that PDHG eventually converges linearly whenever the limit KKT point is strictly complementary, even with multiple solutions. The asymptotic rate admits a bound computable from the eigenvalues of the linearized PDHG map and matching the observed rates in our experiments. As a byproduct of the analysis, strict complementarity implies metric subregularity. Finally, we prove that PDHG can converge sublinearly even when started arbitrarily close to a solution, which cannot happen for linear programming. Numerical experiments support the theory and exhibit SDP instances on which PDHG struggles to reach high accuracy.

papers.title: The Quantum Pendulum of Turbulent Flow: Decaying turbulence as a thermal state of an integrable system
papers.abstract: We present a theory of decaying turbulence in which the statistics of a classical flow becomes quantum mechanics in loop space. The loop functional plays the role of a wave function, and the Navier-Stokes equation makes it evolve linearly, with the viscosity as Planck constant. Turbulence at infinite Reynolds number is defined by a discretized loop equation on polygons with $N$ sides and a renormalization. It has an exact manifold of decaying solutions, the Euler ensemble; each is a singular point of the deterministic equation, which does not select their weights. We interpret this instability as the source of spontaneous stochasticity: thermal noise only triggers a diffusion of the momentum loop over the Euler states, and neither its amplitude nor the temperature of the fluid enters the statistics. In a stochastic model of this diffusion equal weights are proved to be the attractor. As a fermion trace, the partition function and the vorticity correlations become Gibbs averages of two quantum pendulums with the Mathieu Hamiltonian. The energy spectrum is a chain of explicit quadratures. It falls as $k^{-7/2}$ at large $k$; at $kL=\sqrt{2}$, with $L=\sqrt{\tildeν(t+t_0)}$, its slope diverges as a double logarithm, so the decay at a fixed wave number is singular at a finite time and the vorticity correlation oscillates. At small $k$ there are two solutions, for a quenched and an annealed orientation of the plane of the loop: $k^{-1}\log(1/kL)$ and $k^{-2}/\log(1/kL)$. The energy and its dissipation depend on the size of the system logarithmically in the first and almost linearly in the second, and the energy decays with an index of 1.1-1.2 and about 1.45. The reduction to the quantum pendulum is formally verified in Lean 4 in a forthcoming paper. The theory rests on stated physical hypotheses; its comparison with simulations and experiment is left to a separate paper.

papers.title: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
papers.abstract: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where the learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard, but their fixed, ad hoc prescriptions can be suboptimal. We propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating sampling-clock speed as the control, so a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in diffusion time and a leading-order Euler error surrogate defines the allocation objective. To solve the resulting high-dimensional deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized Gaussian-policy formulation that turns schedule learning into continuous-time reinforcement learning. We prove ART-RL is equivalent to ART at optimality: the mean of the optimal Gaussian policy solves ART. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor-critic updates. Experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation show that ART-learned schedules, when plugged into existing samplers by changing only the timestep grid, consistently improve sample quality over strong baselines at matched budgets. The learned schedules also exhibit broad generalizability, transferring without retraining across sampling budgets, data sets, solvers, pipelines, and representation spaces.

papers.title: On perturbations that preserve the connectivity properties in tree percolations
papers.abstract: We consider a general bond percolation on an infinite locally finite tree, where the edge retention probabilities $p_e$ are replaced by $\min\{1,q_{|e|}p_e\}$, where $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of positive perturbation factors and $|e|$ denotes the distance between the edge $e$ and the root. If the original percolation model admits infinite clusters, it is of interest to investigate under which perturbations $0<q_n\le 1$ this connectivity property is preserved. Conversely, if the original percolation does not admit infinite clusters, we are led to study the stability of such a property under perturbations satisfying $q_n\ge 1$. In both cases, under minimal assumptions on the original model, we show that the percolative behaviour is stable against certain quantitative non-trivial perturbations. We also discuss an application of our results to the Erdős similarity conjecture for Cantor sets.

papers.title: Axes of null Cartan normal helices with applications to isophotic and silhouette curves in Minkowski space-time
papers.abstract: We study null Cartan curves in Minkowski space-time $\E$ that are normal helices with respect to C-constant normal fields $V=λT+μN+νB_2$, whose components in the Cartan frame are constant. If $κ_3$ has no zeros, the constant vectors $W$ for which $\ip{V}{W}$ is constant correspond to common solutions of two linear differential equations, of orders four and at most two. Hence they form a space of dimension at most two, $B_2$ is never an axis field, and the normal helices with any other axis field $V$ and prescribed $κ_3$ are obtained by two quadratures, explicitly for $V=λT\pm B_2$. For null Cartan helices, $V$ admits an axis if and only if one of three explicit linear conditions on $(λ,μ,ν)$ holds; then $\ip{V}{W}=0$, and the axes are spanned by the invariant null lines and spacelike plane of the boost--rotation group generating the helix. For fields with $μν\neq0$ we obtain a Riccati criterion and determine all fields moving in a fixed plane; for fields $λT+N$ we find non-helical curves with two linearly independent axes, unlike in dimension three. Finally, we introduce a normalized Darboux frame for null curves on timelike hypersurfaces and characterize the isophotic and silhouette curves with C-constant normal.

papers.title: Higher cotangent cohomology for Stanley-Reisner rings
papers.abstract: Inspired by work of Altmann and Christophersen, we study the graded pieces of the cotangent cohomology $T^i_{S_{\mathcal{K}}}$, $i\geq 3$ of the Stanley-Reisner ring $S_{\mathcal{K}}$ associated to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$. We prove a localization formula allowing one to reduce to the case of negative weights. Our results give a complete description of $T^3$ and $T^4$ in terms of the topology of $\mathcal{K}$ whenever $\mathcal{K}$ is a flag complex. As an application, we give a sufficient criterion for the vanishing of $T^3$ for simplicial spheres, classify two-spheres that have vanishing $T^3$, and show that the boundary complex of the dual associahedron has vanishing $T^3$. Our results make use of the arborescent resolutions considered by Hancharuk, Laurent-Gengoux, and Strobl. We give an alternative and self-contained treatment of these resolutions that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Multi-Stage Stochastic Optimization and Reinforcement Learning Approaches for Dynamic Inspection of Infrastructure Systems
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic inspection problem for infrastructure systems in which we route and schedule multiple vehicles to monitor components that are subject to heterogeneous stochastic failures. Inspection decisions determine which components the vehicles serve first and thus affect how failures propagate to neighboring components. We formulate the problem as a multi-stage stochastic mixed-integer program that jointly optimizes routing and scheduling under exogenous and decision-dependent uncertainty. We develop a stochastic dual dynamic integer programming (SDDiP) algorithm based on a stage decomposition of the multi-stage model and show that it converges finitely to the optimal value. In parallel, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) approach that learns assignment policies from simulated system dynamics. On instances built from the road and storm-sewer networks of Sioux Falls, SDDiP proves optimality where the extended formulation of the same model leaves large gaps. On larger instances, RL with a routable-assignment certificate often finds cheaper policies than SDDiP under a short computational budget, whereas SDDiP finds cheaper policies and bounds on their quality with more time. Moreover, modeling failure propagation and decision-dependent transition probabilities reduces the realized cost when these mechanisms are present. These comparisons guide the choice between optimization and policy learning for inspection planning under failure risk.

papers.title: On the class-breadth conjecture for $p$-groups
papers.abstract: The class-breadth conjecture of Leedham-Green, Neumann and Wiegold states that the nilpotency class of any $p$-group is at most $b(G) + 1$, where $\displaystyle{b(G) = \max_{g\in G}\log_p[G:Z_G(g)]}$ denotes the breadth of a group $G$. While several counter-examples to this conjecture have been found for $p = 2$, it is still open in general for $p > 2$. This article is dedicated to the general case $p > 2$ of the conjecture.

papers.title: Beyond the probabilistic scaling for NLS on the ball
papers.abstract: We construct probabilistic strong solutions to the cubic Schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional ball with radial initial data, which is a significant improvement of a result by Bourgain--Bulut. These solutions lie in the supercritical regime with respect to the probabilistic scaling introduced by Deng--Nahmod--Yue. We achieve this result through gauge transformations, without renormalization, combined with a refined modulation analysis using random averaging operators.

papers.title: A Dynkin condition for manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: We propose a Dynkin-type condition for smooth Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We show that this condition implies bi-Lipschitz equivalence with a Bakry-Émery weighted Riemannian manifold obtained via a time change. As a consequence, we obtain various results, including a local doubling property as well as lower bounds on the Neumann spectral gap and logarithmic Sobolev constant. The local doubling property also yields a new precompactness theorem for manifolds with boundary.

papers.title: A counterexample to a basis conjecture of Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen
papers.abstract: Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen conjectured that certain rank inequalities characterize bases consisting of elementary vectors in the row space of a matrix whose nonzero entries are algebraically independent. We give a $4\times6$ counterexample: all the inequalities hold, but the four elementary vectors form a minimally dependent family. A construction using two planes in a common three-dimensional subspace explains the dependence and gives a second counterexample pattern with only four prescribed zeros. We also prove that the proposed criterion is valid over every field when the number of columns exceeds the row rank by at most one. A direct-sum extension gives counterexamples of size $m\times(m+2)$ for every $m\ge4$. Thus the minimum column excess permitting a counterexample is exactly two in every such rank.

papers.title: Rigidity and equidistribution of random walks by diffeomorphisms near the conservative regime
papers.abstract: We consider a random walk on a closed manifold $M$ driven by a probability measure $μ$ on the set of $C^2$-diffeomorphisms. Provided $μ$ has compact support, satisfies certain gap, pinching, and ergodicity conditions, and is weak-$*$ close to volume-preserving, we prove $M$ carries exactly one atom-free stationary probability measure $Υ_μ$. It has finite high-dimensional Riesz energy and coincides with volume in the volume-preserving setting. Moreover, for every $x\in M$, the $n$-step distribution $μ^{*n}*δ_{x}$ converges to $Υ_μ$ unless $x$ is trapped in a finite $μ$-invariant set. Our result applies to a variety of situations: bi-expanding random walks on surfaces, non-linear perturbations of Zariski-dense random walks on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, on cocompact lattice quotients of $\mathrm{SO}(2,1), \mathrm{SO}(3,1)$, or on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$.

papers.title: Well-Balanced Schemes for Hyperbolic Kinetic Relaxation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel class of well-balanced numerical schemes for hyperbolic systems of balance laws in 1D using the kinetic relaxation framework. Kinetic relaxation methods approximate nonlinear hyperbolic systems via a linear system of transport equations where nonlinearities are relegated to the source term. While these methods simplify the Riemann problem, they fail to preserve the discrete steady-state solutions of the original system because of the modified source term. We propose two distinct strategies to achieve the well-balanced property: a modified Finite Volume (FV) approach using well-balanced reconstruction operators and a well-balanced Semi-Lagrangian (SL) approach based on characteristic backtracking. Both methods ensure that the steady solutions of the original system remain invariant during the transport and projection steps. We demonstrate the efficacy of these schemes with first-, second-, and third-order accuracy using palindromic splitting techniques. Numerical results for Burgers' equation, the Shallow Water Equations with bathymetry, and the Euler equations with gravitational potential confirm that our relaxation schemes maintain steady states to machine precision while capturing complex transient dynamics.

papers.title: Solving Linear and Integer Programs Faster Using Data
papers.abstract: We study how much a linear program (LP) or an integer program (IP) can be compressed when solved repeatedly over a fixed feasible region with varying objective coefficients. We provide a framework that compresses LP and IP formulations with guarantees on the probability of preserving optimality, using either an uncertainty set for the cost vector or historical samples. Our framework exposes a tunable tradeoff between compression and the probability of recovering an optimal solution. We characterize the minimum dimension of affine reformulations preserving the full optimizer set over a given cost region and provide sample-based learning algorithms with fast-rate guarantees, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption for LPs. With high confidence over the training data, the learned reformulation preserves the optimizer set for an independent test cost with probability at least $1-ρ-\widetilde{O}(d^\star_ρ/n)$, where $ρ$ bounds the excluded probability mass and $d^\star_ρ$ is the retained region's decision-relevant dimension. Existing data-driven approaches to LP and IP reduction do not, to our knowledge, learn a single low-dimensional affine reformulation with a prescribed probability of preserving the full optimizer set. Experimental results show substantial improvements over the compared baselines in accuracy, sample efficiency, and computational speed.

papers.title: A discrepancy dichotomy for 1-factorizations of signed complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given a signing $σ\colon E(K_{n,n})\to\{-1,+1\}$ of the complete bipartite graph, when does $K_{n,n}$ admit a $1$-factorization in which every perfect matching has discrepancy bounded below by a positive absolute constant? Unlike the complete-graph case resolved by Ai, He, Im, and Lee, the bipartite setting carries an unavoidable obstruction: any balanced one-sided signing---one whose edge signs depend on a single bipartition class, with the two labels split as evenly as possible---forces every perfect matching to have discrepancy at most $1/n$. We prove that this is essentially the only obstruction: For every $0<\varepsilon\leq1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every signing of $K_{n,n}$ either (i) admits a $1$-factorization in which every perfect matching has discrepancy at least $\varepsilon/53$, or (ii) is $\varepsilon$-close, in normalized Hamming distance, to a balanced one-sided signing. The linear dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to an absolute factor. A key ingredient is a rank-one stability argument: if the density of rank-two $2\times 2$ switching patterns is small, then the sign matrix is close in Hamming distance to a rank-one sign matrix.

papers.title: Rare events of small-noise Doob conditioned processes
papers.abstract: Doob fixed-time conditioning enables the sampling of rare trajectories of Markov processes by modifying the drift so that reaching a prescribed target at a given time is guaranteed. We study the statistics of this conditioned path ensemble through the moment generating function in the weak-noise large deviation regime. Since the Doob drift is rarely available in closed form, we reinterpret the conditioned ensemble as the original process post-selected on the terminal constraint, thereby avoiding explicit construction of the Doob transform. This viewpoint then yields an optimal-control representation for the leading exponential contribution to the generating function, expressed as a variational principle with terminal boundary conditions set by the Doob end-point constraint. We illustrate the framework with two analytical examples and with an application to heat dissipation under Doob-controlled dynamics in a minimal model of biomolecular folding.

papers.title: Higher-Rank Connections and Deformed Schrödinger Operators
papers.abstract: We study the connection problem for a class of linear differential equations of order $N$ closely related to the Baxter equation of the quantum Toda chain. The space of solutions is $N$-dimensional and several linearly independent solutions decay at each singularity, leading to a rich structure of boundary value problems. We derive the weakest quantization conditions compatible with decaying behavior at both singularities, and formulate these conditions in terms of the associated monodromy data. In doing so, we prove the quantization conditions predicted by the topological string/spectral theory duality for a family of deformed Schrödinger equations. More generally, our results point to a hierarchy of spectral problems interpolating between the minimal conditions studied here and the maximally decaying boundary conditions of the $N$-particle quantum Toda chain.

papers.title: Manin's conjecture for semi-integral curves and $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness
papers.abstract: We explore log Manin's conjecture for integral points and its connections to $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness. We prove log Manin's conjecture for Campana rational curves and for $\mathbb A^1$-curves on split toric varieties. Our arguments combine the Cox ring description of the moduli space of rational curves with Batyrev's heuristic-type counting arguments. As our proofs are geometric in nature, they give a geometric explanation of the mysterious leading constant for Campana points proposed by Chow--Loughran--Takloo-Bighash--Tanimoto.

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a Hilbert space
papers.abstract: The cloud of a metric space $X$ consists of all metric spaces at finite Gromov--Hausdorff distance from $X$, with spaces at zero distance identified. We prove that the cloud of every real Hilbert space $H$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $H$.

papers.title: Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift
papers.abstract: We study a class of discrete-time random walks in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose conditional drift decays polynomially in time and grows polynomially with the distance from the origin to the current position. This class is related to several models of self-interacting random processes. We determine the asymptotic behavior of the walk under the assumption that its increments have moments of order $p$ for some $p>2$. In the linear case, where the drift depends linearly on the current position, we establish a phase transition in the convergence in distribution of the normalized process to Gaussian limits. In the nonlinear case, we identify three distinct regimes separated by a critical line and show that the normalized process exhibits qualitatively different behaviors in each regime, including convergence in distribution to a Gaussian law, convergence to a non-Gaussian limit given by the stationary distribution of a stochastic differential equation, and almost sure localization on a hypersphere.

papers.title: Intrinsic Curvature Energy Estimates for Strongly Stable CMC Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish an intrinsic square-root curvature-energy estimate for two-sided strongly stable CMC hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ for $3\leq n\leq 5$. By means of a weighted Hölder closure, we control a supercritical curvature norm in terms of the $L^2$ norm of the traceless second fundamental form, from which the pointwise bound follows via Moser iteration. In dimensions $n=3$ and $4$, the estimate holds without any scale restriction on the mean curvature. In regions of finite Morse index, this bound restricts points with low principal curvatures to neighborhoods of at most as many centers as the index, and yields an upper bound on the total diameter of separated degeneration sets in terms of their curvature energy and the index.

papers.title: Irregular SLE(4) martingales and isomonodromic deformations
papers.abstract: We consider non-Fuchsian monodromy preserving deformations on a Riemann sphere. The associated isomonodromic deformation parameters on this surface comprise the positions of the singularities, together with the Birkhoff (spectral) invariants owing to the presence of irregular singularities. Our first main result is the derivation of the Loewner evolution of these isomonodromic deformation parameters. Using this result, we construct martingale observables for Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE(4)) processes in the presence of double poles. Geometrically, the expressions contain the pre-Schwarzian and Schwarzian of the Loewner evolution, arising from conformal covariance of the observable. Furthermore, we characterize these SLE(4) observables uniquely in terms of confluent BPZ equations of a CFT with central charge c=1.

papers.title: Uniqueness of synchronized stationary equilibria in the Kuramoto mean field game
papers.abstract: The Kuramoto mean field game describes a population of oscillators which, above a critical value of the interaction parameter, form synchronized Nash equilibria. We show that these synchronized equilibria are unique, up to rotations, for each value of the parameter. Moreover, the unique equilibrium depends smoothly on the interaction parameter, and converges smoothly to the uniform distribution when the parameter approaches its critical value. These statements are direct consequences of our main technical result: the self-consistency map is strictly concave, as was previously conjectured by Carmona, Cormier, and Soner. In the proof, we decompose the second derivative of the self-consistency map as the sum of two moments, and prove that each of them is negative by using symmetrization arguments to exploit hidden monotonicity and skewness properties of the equilibria.

papers.title: From Schrodinger Bridge to Optimal Transport over Sub-Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the least-energy way to reshape a probability distribution when motion is constrained to a horizontal subbundle, i.e., optimal transport and distribution steering in sub-Riemannian geometry. It is well-known that the deterministic sub-Riemannian optimal transport problem can be complicated by the non-smooth geometry. To obtain a smooth and numerically tractable formulation, we introduce small noise that aligns with the geometry and study the associated Schrödinger bridge problem. We discuss the case where the given marginals can have compact support or have sub-Gaussian tails. Under bracket-generating hypotheses, we obtain smooth, strictly positive transition densities and a forward--backward characterization of the optimal bridge, which acts as a convex selection principle among potentially many deterministic optima. This leads to a practical Sinkhorn-type algorithm with geometric constraints and we discuss it convergence in both regimes. We show that as the noise level vanishes, the unique Schrödinger bridge minimizers converge to a minimizer of the deterministic sub-Riemannian optimal transport problem. In the case of full support regime, our result illustrates that, the existence and characterization of the unique Schrödinger bridge, Sinkhorn convergence and the convex selection principle is possible only after quantifying the smoothness and positivity of the transition density. We demonstrate with a benchmark Heisenberg group.

papers.title: A Spectral Framework for Closed-Form Relative Density Estimation
papers.abstract: We propose a closed-form spectral framework for relative log-density estimation in linearly parameterized probabilistic models, including unnormalized and conditional models. This is achieved by representing the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as an integral of weighted chi-squared divergences, converting KL estimation into a family of least-squares problems. We derive an explicit spectral formula based only on first- and second-order feature moments, yielding closed-form estimators of both divergences and log-density potentials for fixed features. The framework extends to a broad class of $f$-divergences and can be combined with kernelization or feature learning with neural networks (with then only a closed form for the last layer). We prove convergence guarantees for the resulting estimators and empirically compare them on synthetic data with optimization-based variational formulations, including logistic and softmax regression for normalized conditional models.

papers.title: On a PDE-based material parameter identification problem with contact constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the identification of a scalar coefficient in a PDE-based parameter estimation problem with contact constraints. The considered problem can be used as an idealized model of a membrane under forces, constrained by a barrier or indenter. More generally, it serves as a benchmark for the analysis of more complex contact problems and the development of corresponding reconstruction algorithms. In this paper, we discuss both the forward and inverse parameter estimation problems, as well as uniqueness and non-uniqueness issues caused by the contact constraints. Furthermore, we consider the design and implementation of reconstruction approaches which we test on numerical examples, illustrating both uniqueness and non-uniqueness as well as parameter identifyability.

papers.title: A Diffeological Construction of Singer's Universal Connection
papers.abstract: We provide a rigorous construction of I.M. Singer's universal connection, a natural connection on a bundle of paths associated to any manifold, using the theory of diffeology. Furthermore, we generalize the universal connection to the diffeological setting, which enables the reconstruction of diffeological principal bundles with connections from their holonomy representations, extending known bundle-reconstruction results into diffeology. In particular, any two diffeological bundle-connection pairs with conjugate holonomy representations must be isomorphic as bundles, with the isomorphism taking horizontal paths to horizontal paths. Finally, we show that reconstruction and holonomy are functorial and, for a fixed diffeological group $G$, form an adjoint equivalence between the category of smooth homomorphisms from based loop groups into $G$ and the category of pointed diffeological principal $G$-bundle-connection pairs, extending to the diffeological setting the known equivalences for manifolds and Lie groups.

papers.title: Reentrant value fields as delayed coupled reaction-diffusion systems on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We describe a dynamical system in which a symbolic field is coupled to a geometric field via a bipartite Hilbert-Schmidt kernel.
