Furthermore, we give a multilinear extension of the Christ--Kiselev theorem, establishing strong variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations for a general multilinear operator.

papers.title: Ranking Statistical Experiments via the Linear Convex Order and the Lorenz Zonoid: Economic Applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel ranking of statistical experiments, the linear-Blackwell (LB) order, which can equivalently be characterized by (i) the dispersion of the induced posterior and likelihood ratios in the sense of the linear convex order, (ii) the size of the Lorenz zonoid (the set of statewise expectation profiles), or (iii) the variability of the posterior mean. We show that the LB order provides a necessary and sufficient criterion for comparing experiments uniformly across decision problems with quasi-concave payoffs and principal-agent problems with separable payoffs.

papers.title: On the Algebraic Independence of $E$- and $G$-Functions, I: A $p$-adic Criterion
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and let $f_1(z),\ldots, f_m(z) \in K[[z]]$ be power series such that, for every $1 \leq i \leq m$, $f_i(z)$ is a solution to a differential operator $\mathcal{L}_i \in E_p[\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}z]$, where $E_p$ denotes the field of analytic elements. Suppose that $K$ is totally ramified over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and that for every $1 \leq i \leq m$, the operator $\mathcal{L}_i$ has a strong Frobenius structure and satisfies the maximal order multiplicity (MOM) condition at zero. Under these assumptions, we show that $f_1(z),\ldots, f_m(z)$ are algebraically dependent over $E_p$ if and only if there exist integers $a_1,\ldots, a_m$, not all zero, such that $f_1(z)^{a_1} \cdots f_m(z)^{a_m} \in E_p.$ The main consequence of this result is that it provides a general criterion for studying the algebraic independence of a broad class of $G$-functions and certain $E$-functions over the field of analytic elements.

papers.title: Compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We study properties of compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties. In particular, we prove a comparison theorem, in a stable range, with compactly supported syntomic cohomology, which is built from compactly supported Hyodo-Kato and ${\mathcal B}^+_{\rm dr}$-cohomologies. We derive from that a (limited version of a) fundamental diagram.

papers.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
papers.abstract: Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether \[ S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}} \] converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erdős and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].

papers.title: $P$-trivial MMP, Zariski decompositions and minimal models for generalised pairs
papers.abstract: We develop an inductive method for generalised pairs (g-pairs) without the NQC assumption. It is based on $P$-trivial MMPs, whose steps are trivial with respect to a given nef divisor $P$. For klt g-pairs, if $P$ is numerically equivalent to an effective divisor, we perturb the boundary so that any MMP on $K_X+B+M+αP$ is $P$-trivial for $α\gg0$. For lc g-pairs, the components with coefficient one cannot be perturbed, so we use induction on lc centres. If $K_X+B+M-P$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor, then local Cartier indices control the coefficients under divisorial adjunction, and we prove a special termination. This includes the case $P=0$, where $K_X+B+M$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor. As applications, we prove that a projective lc g-pair $(X,B+M)$ of dimension $3$ has a minimal model if $K_X+B+M$ birationally has a Nakayama-Zariski decomposition with nef positive part and either $K_X+B+M\equiv D\geq0$ or $M\equiv D\geq0$. We also prove this for klt g-pairs in arbitrary dimension. In dimension $4$, the last condition can be replaced by the log abundance of the nef data. For usual pairs, this is a theorem of Birkar and the author.

papers.title: On statistical and causal models associated with acyclic directed mixed graphs
papers.abstract: Causal models in statistics are often described using acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs), which contain directed and bidirected edges and no directed cycles. This article surveys various interpretations of ADMGs, discusses their relations in different sub-classes of ADMGs, and argues that one of them---the noise expansion (NE) model---should be used as the default interpretation. Our endorsement of the NE model is based on two observations. First, in a subclass of ADMGs called exogenously bidirected graphs (which retain most of the good properties of directed acyclic graphs and bidirected graphs), the NE model is equivalent to many other interpretations, including the ordinary Markov and nested Markov models. Second, the NE model for an arbitrary ADMG is exactly the union of the observed margins of NE models on its exogenously bidirected expansions. This property is referred to as completeness, as it shows that the model does not commit to any specific latent variable explanation. In proving the nested Markov property, we also develop an ADMG-based theory for causality and its complete characterization via the potential outcome calculus. Finally, we compare the NE model with the closely related but different interpretation of ADMGs as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with latent variables that is commonly used in the literature. We argue that the ``latent DAG'' interpretation is mathematically unnecessary, makes obscure ontological assumptions, and discourages practitioners from deliberating over important structural assumptions.

papers.title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.

papers.title: Projected gradient methods for nonconvex and stochastic smooth optimization: new complexities and auto-conditioned stepsizes
papers.abstract: We present a novel class of projected gradient (PG) methods for minimizing a smooth but not necessarily convex function over a convex compact set. We first provide a novel analysis of the constant-stepsize PG method, achieving a unified iteration complexity for finding an approximate stationary point for convex and nonconvex problems. We then develop an "auto-conditioned" projected gradient (AC-PG) variant that achieves the same iteration complexity without requiring the input of the Lipschitz constant of the gradient or any line search procedure. The key idea is to estimate the Lipschitz constant using first-order information gathered from the previous iterations, and to show that the error caused by underestimating the Lipschitz constant can be properly controlled. We then generalize the PG methods to the stochastic setting, by proposing a stochastic projected gradient (SPG) method and a variance-reduced stochastic gradient (VR-SPG) method, achieving new unified complexity bounds in different oracle settings. We also present auto-conditioned stepsize policies for both stochastic PG methods and establish comparable convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Transfer Learning for High-dimensional Quantile Regression with Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Information from related source studies can often enhance the findings of a target study. However, the distribution shift between target and source studies can severely impact the efficiency of knowledge transfer. In the high-dimensional regression setting, existing transfer approaches mainly focus on the parameter shift. In this paper, we focus on the high-dimensional quantile regression with knowledge transfer under three types of distribution shift: parameter shift, covariate shift, and residual shift. We propose a novel transferable set and a new transfer framework to address the above three discrepancies. Non-asymptotic estimation error bounds and source detection consistency are established to validate the availability and superiority of our method in the presence of distribution shift. Additionally, an orthogonal debiased approach is proposed for statistical inference with knowledge transfer, leading to sharper asymptotic results. Extensive simulation results as well as real data applications further demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed procedure.

papers.title: Cohomological VC-density: Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: The concept of Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) density is pivotal across various mathematical fields, including discrete geometry, probability theory and model theory. In this paper, we introduce a topological generalization of VC-density. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal{X}$ a family of closed subspaces of $Y$. For each $p \geq 0$, we define a number, $\mathrm{vcd}^{p}_{\mathcal{X}}$, which we refer to as the degree $p$ VC-density of the family $\mathcal{X}$. The classical notion of VC-density within this topological framework can be recovered by setting $p=0$. Our definition of degree $p$ VC-density extends to higher orders as well. For $p \geq 0$, $q \geq 1$, we define the degree $p$, order $q$ VC density $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$ of $\mathcal{X}$, which recovers Shelah's notion of higher order VC-density for $q$-dependent families when $p=0$. Our definition introduces a completely new notion when $p > 0$. We examine the properties of $\mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p$ (as well as $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$) when the families $\mathcal{X}$ are definable in structures with some underlying topology (for instance, the Euclidean topology for o-minimal structures over $\mathbb{R}$, the analytic topology over $\mathbb{C}$, or the étale site for schemes over arbitrary algebraically closed fields). Our main result establishes that in any model of these theories \[ \mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p \leq (p+1) \dim X, \] and more generally for any $q \geq 1$ \[ \mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}} \leq (p+q) \dim X. \] We give examples to show that our bounds are optimal. We also present combinatorial applications of our higher-degree VC-density bounds, deriving higher degree topological analogs of well-known results such as the existence of $\varepsilon$-nets and the fractional Helly theorem.

papers.title: On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy
papers.abstract: In the first part of the manuscript, we establish several consistency results concerning Woodin's HOD hypothesis and large cardinals around the level of extendibility. First, we prove that the first extendible cardinal can be the first strongly compact in HOD. Second, answering a question in \cite{CFH}, we prove that the first supercompact cardinal can be the first strongly compact, non supercompact, of HOD. We extend a former result of Woodin by showing that under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible cardinal is $C^{(1)}$-supercompact in HOD. We also show that the first cardinal-correct extendible may not be extendible, thus answering a question by Gitman and Osinski \cite[\S9]{GitOsi}. In the second part of the manuscript, we discuss the extent to which weak covering can fail below the first supercompact cardinal $δ$ in a context where the HOD hypothesis holds. Answering a question of Cummings et al. \cite{CumFriGol}, we show that under the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis there are many singulars $κ<δ$ where $\mathrm{cf}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(κ)=\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ and $κ^{+\mathrm{HOD}}=κ^{+}.$ In contrast, we also show that the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis is consistent with $δ$ carrying a club of $\mathrm{HOD}$-regulars cardinals $κ$ such that $κ^{+\mathrm{HOD}}<κ^{+}$. Finally, we close the manuscript with a discussion about the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis and $ω$-strong measurability.

papers.title: Equivalence Relations on Vertex Operator Algebras, II: Witt Equivalence and Orbifolds
papers.abstract: When can two strongly rational vertex operator algebras or 1+1d rational conformal field theories (RCFTs) be related by topological manipulations? For vertex operator algebras, the term "topological manipulations" refers to operations like passing to a conformal extension or restricting to a conformal subalgebra; for RCFTs, topological manipulations include operations like gauging (or orbifolding) a finite part of a generalized global symmetry or interpolating to a new theory via a topological line interface of finite quantum dimension. Inspired by results in the theory of even lattices and tensor categories, we say that two strongly rational vertex operator algebras are Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their modular tensor categories are Witt equivalent. Two RCFTs are said to be Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their associated 2+1d topological field theories can be separated by a topological surface. We argue that Witt equivalence is necessary for two theories to be related by topological manipulations. We conjecture that it is also sufficient, and give proofs in various special cases. We relate this circle of ideas to the problem of classifying RCFTs, and to lore concerning deformation classes of quantum field theories. We use the notion of Witt equivalence to argue, conditional on a mild technical hypothesis, that all of the finite symmetries of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model are invertible. We also sketch a "quantum Galois theory" for chiral CFTs, which generalizes prior mathematical literature by incorporating non-invertible symmetries; we illustrate this non-invertible Galois theory in the context of the monster CFT $V^\natural$, for which we produce two Fibonacci lines. Finally, we discuss $p$-neighborhood of vertex operator algebras, which is a special topological manipulation related to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbifolding.

papers.title: Markov-Nash equilibria in mean-field games under model uncertainty
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a framework for mean-field Markov games under model uncertainty. In this framework, a state-measure flow describing the collective behavior of a population affects the given reward function as well as the unknown transition kernel of the representative agent. The agent's objective is to choose an optimal Markov policy in order to maximize her worst-case expected reward, where worst-case refers to the most adverse scenario among all transition kernels considered to be feasible to describe the unknown true law of the environment. We prove the existence of a mean-field equilibrium under model uncertainty, where the agent chooses the optimal policy that maximizes the worst-case expected reward, and the state-measure flow aligns with the agent's state distribution under the optimal policy and the worst-case transition kernel. Moreover, we prove that for suitable multi-agent Markov games under model uncertainty the optimal policy from the mean-field equilibrium forms an approximate Markov-Nash equilibrium whenever the number of agents is large enough.

papers.title: Classification of real nodal orders
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study properties of nodal orders defined over arbitrary base fields. In particular we give a classification of complete real nodal orders.

papers.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.abstract: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While a standard probabilistic proof uses matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose an elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity: any 1-sub-Gaussian distribution with variance 1 yields the same sufficient target dimension as the Gaussian distribution. We then extend the analysis to sparse projections, with data-dependent sparsity conditions on the pairwise differences of the points, and we quantify the cost of sparsity on the target dimension. A complementary lower bound shows the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision Lloyd's Algorithm for k-means Clustering
papers.abstract: As low-precision arithmetic becomes more widely available on modern hardware, we develop mixed-precision variants of Lloyd's algorithm for k-means clustering, with a family of mixed-precision kernels for Euclidean distance computation as the main ingredient. These kernels are guided by rounding-error analysis and use a simple reliability test to decide whether the expanded distance formula can be evaluated safely with low precision or a higher-precision correction by the direct distance formula is required. Thus, most distance computations can be carried out with low precision, while high-precision arithmetic is used selectively when cancellation may lead to a loss of accuracy. We evaluate the proposed methods on large-scale distance-computation benchmarks, synthetic clustering problems, and image-segmentation tasks. The experiments verify that the mixed-precision kernels on GPUs can substantially improve performance while retaining accuracy and convergence behavior of higher-precision baselines. In particular, our implemented distance computation in CUDA achieves speedups of up to $4\times$ over the \texttt{PyTorch} baseline that evaluates the expanded formula in FP64 on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, with overall maximum relative errors of order $10^{-3}$, while providing increased numerical robustness in cancellation-prone calculations. The resulting mixed-precision kernels show efficiency for clustering and image segmentation, although the observed gains depend on factors such as feature dimension, and number of clusters. The mixed-precision kernels offer a favorable trade-off between performance and accuracy for clustering, and suggest that similar ideas may be beneficial for other distance-based machine learning methods.

papers.title: On completed homology and a conjecture of Venkatesh
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a CM field and $Π$ a regular algebraic cuspidal cohomological representation of $\mathbf{G}=\operatorname{PGL}_2/F$. A conjecture of Venkatesh describes the structure of the contribution of $Π$ to the homology of the locally symmetric spaces associated to $\mathbf{G}$. We investigate this conjecture in the setting of $p$-adic homology with $p$ a totally split prime. Along the way, we elaborate on the relations between Venkatesh's conjecture and completed homology, the Taylor-Wiles method and the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence. Our main result is a `big $R=T$' theorem in characteristic 0, from which we deduce a variant of the $p$-adic realisation of Venkatesh's conjecture, conditional on various natural conjectures and technical assumptions.

papers.title: On Bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: Recently, Özarslan and Elidemir (2023) introduced a methodology for constructing two-variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one-variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. The primary objective of the paper is to introduce novel class of two-variable biorthogonal polynomials namley bivariate Jacobi Konhauser polynomials. We investigate several fundamental properties of these polynomials including their biorthogonality property, operational formula, generating function, and integral representation. Furthermore, We inverstigate their images under the Laplace transform, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Mittag Leffler (JKML) function and obtain the similar properties for them.

papers.title: Quantitative asymptotics for polynomial patterns in the primes
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative estimates for averages of the von Mangoldt and Möbius functions along polynomial progressions $n+P_1(m),\ldots, n+P_k(m)$ for a large class of polynomials $P_i$. The error terms obtained save an arbitrary power of logarithm, matching the classical Siegel--Walfisz error term. These results give the first quantitative bounds for the Tao--Ziegler polynomial patterns in the primes result. The proofs are based on a quantitative generalised von Neumann theorem of Peluse, a recent result of Leng on strong bounds for the Gowers uniformity of the primes, and analysis of a ``Siegel model'' for the von Mangoldt function along polynomial progressions.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and unbounded drift
papers.abstract: We consider controlled SDEs with measurable coefficients, a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient and an $L_d$-drift. In this framework we investigate the relationship among value functions, PDEs, and operator semigroups. First, for a cost with an infinite time horizon on a bounded domain, we identify the value function as an $L_{d_0}$-viscosity solution to an HJB equation and we establish quantitative regularity estimates. The constant $d_0 \in (d/2, d)$ only depends on the space dimension $d$, the ellipticity constants of the diffusion coefficient and the $L_d$-bound of the drift. To illustrate applications of these results, we provide a uniqueness theorem under an additional assumption on the diffusion coefficient, showing a stochastic representation, and we discuss stability of value functions. Second, we consider a cost with a finite time horizon, terminal and running terms, assuming an $L_{d + 1}$-drift. We show that the value function indexed over the terminal cost is a nonlinear semigroup on $C_b (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we establish a regularization by noise effect, which shows that the semigroup regularizes lower semicontinuity to local Hölder continuity. We also establish quantitative regularity estimates for the semigroup that are local in time and global in space. Lastly, under an additional $L_{d + 2, loc}$-assumption on the drift, we relate the semigroup to a parabolic PDE, showing that the associated value function is an $L_{d + 1}$-viscosity solution. Our proofs of the regularity of the value functions, the $C_b$-Feller property of the semigroup and its regularization by noise effects are based on a strong Markov selection principle and analytic estimates for linear diffusions that were recently established by N. V. Krylov in a series of papers. We highlight that our method covers frameworks without uniqueness of the controlled SDEs, as well as the associated PDEs.

papers.title: Nontrivial Massey products on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the bigraded quasi-isomorphism type of the bigraded, bidifferential algebra of forms on a compact Kähler manifold generally contains more information than the de Rham cohomology algebra with its real Hodge structure. More precisely, on any closed Riemann surface of genus at least two, there is a nontrivial ABC-Massey product. Furthermore, starting from dimension three, there are simply connected projective manifolds with a nonzero ABC-Massey product of three divisor classes. In particular, compact Kähler manifolds are generally not formal in the sense of pluripotential homotopy theory.

papers.title: A sharper observability for diffusion equations in $\mathbb R^N$
papers.abstract: We establish that for any small constant $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a nontrivial equidistributed set (with an unbounded complement) such that the observability cost in the short time $(0,T)$ of diffusion equations over $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ can be improved to a sharper exponential form of $Ce^{\varepsilon/T}$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $T$.

papers.title: Fractional Calculus Operator Emerging from the 2D Biorthogonal Hermite Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we introduce a method to construct two variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. By using this new technique, we define 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and we investigate several properties of them such as biorthogonality property, operational formula and integral representation. We further inverstigate their images under the Laplace transformations, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function and obtain the similar properties for them. In order to establish new fractional calculus, we add two new parameters and consider 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function. We introduce an integral operator containing the modified bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function in the kernel. We show that it satisify the semigroup property and obtain its left inverse operator, which corresponds to its fractional derivative operator.

papers.title: On the enumeration of signatures of XOR-CNF's
papers.abstract: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_m$ over a set of variables $V$, a truth assignment $\mathbf{a} : V \to \{0, 1\}$ generates a binary sequence $σ_\varphi(\mathbf{a})=(C_1(\mathbf{a}), \ldots, C_m(\mathbf{a}))$, called a signature of $\varphi$, where $C_i(\mathbf{a})=1$ if clause $C_i$ evaluates to 1 under assignment $\mathbf{a}$, and $C_i(\mathbf{a})=0$ otherwise. Signatures and their associated generation problems have given rise to new yet promising research questions in algorithmic enumeration. In a recent paper, Bérczi et al. interestingly proved that generating signatures of a CNF is tractable despite the fact that verifying a solution is hard. They also showed the hardness of finding maximal signatures of an arbitrary CNF due to the intractability of satisfiability in general. Their contribution leaves open the problem of efficiently generating maximal signatures for tractable classes of CNFs, i.e., those for which satisfiability can be solved in polynomial time. Stepping into that direction, we completely characterize the complexity of generating all, minimal, and maximal signatures for XOR-CNFs.

papers.title: The transversal game
papers.abstract: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.

papers.title: On the role of dense ideals on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and associated $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets
papers.abstract: This article is a continuation of the work done in [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289] on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and concerns in addition the generalized version of Arbault sets, namely, $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets that is generated from this collection. A special class of ideals, namely, non-$snt$ ideals was introduced in 2023 ($snt$ stands for ``strongly non translation invariant") which was found to be effective in understanding ``Eggleston's dichotomy". Here we introduce another new class of ideals $\mathcal{H}$, a subclass of non-$snt$ ideals. We are able to establish a (new) necessary and sufficient condition for a $P$-ideal to be dense in Theorem 2.8 using the condition used to define the class $\mathcal{H}$ from which it follows that $\mathcal{H}$ coincides with dense $P$-ideals. Furthermore the important fact is established that the class of non-$snt$ ideals strictly contains the class of dense $P$-ideals. Subsequent investigation leads us to Theorem 2.14 which establishes the novelty of $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups for ideals coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$ and arbitrary arithmetic sequences showing that these are not even Arbault sets. Before all these, we also present a correct and revised proof of the main result of [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289], namely Theorem 3.8 (which had a gap in the proof). Finally we extend the results of [Das et al., Bul. Sci. Math. 179 (2022), 103157] for generalized version of Arbault sets and primarily show that for each ideal coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$, the class of $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets not only properly contains the class of classical Arbault sets but also a large subfamily of sets of absolute convergence while being contained in the class of weak Dirichlet sets.

papers.title: Inverse Gram Matrix Methods for Prioritization in Analytic Hierarchy Process: Explainability of Weighted Least Squares Optimization Method
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Inverse Gram Matrix (IGM) methods to prioritize Pairwise Reciprocal Matrices (PRMs) in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The IGM methods include Pseudo-IGM, Normalized-IGM, and Lagrangian-IGM. Interestingly, the proposed IGM methods achieve the minimum Weighted Least Squares (WLS) error. Since clarity, explainability, usability, and verification of the closed-form solutions of WLS appear to be incomplete in the literature, comprehensive mathematical proofs, detailed computational demonstrations, and intensive simulation verification to extend the prior studies are offered in this study. After a simulation of one million random PRM instances was performed to verify the equivalence of the IGM methods, another simulation of ten thousand random PRM instances was performed to verify that any one of the proposed IGM methods is the exact closed-form solution to the WLS optimization problem. The proposed IGM methods under the WLS framework provide the promising alternatives to Saaty's Eigenvector method in AHP. The open-source R package igm4ahp, along with its user manual, tutorials, and simulation datasets, is publicly available on GitHub and permanently archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: A variational Free Boundary Ricci flow on Surfaces with Boundary
papers.abstract: We study a Ricci flow on a compact surface with boundary arising as the L2-gradient flow of the Liouville functional with its natural Neumann boundary condition. Geometrically, this boundary condition preserves the geodesic-curvature density H dσ. In the regime in which the total scalar curvature satisfies 0 < C_0 < 4π, a scale invariant normalised Liouville functional is monotone, and bounded below. In our first result, we use its dissipation to show that every compact blow-up limit is homothetically shrinking with constant positive scalar curvature. We then treat a rotationally symmetric disc with H_0 > 0 and C_0 > 0, in which case every noncompact limit is ruled out via singularity analysis and a noncollapsing theorem. Consequently, the normalised flow fully converges smoothly to the unique spherical cap determined by the initial area and the preserved boundary data, yielding our second result. Additionally, we also study the regime in which C0 is nonpositive. In this case standard PDE arguments prove full smooth convergence of the normalised flow towards a metric with constant nonpositive scalar curvature.

papers.title: Aspherical Lagrangian submanifolds, Audin's conjecture and cyclic dilations
papers.abstract: Given a closed, oriented Lagrangian submanifold $L$ in a Liouville domain $\overline{M}$, one can define a Maurer-Cartan element with respect to a certain $L_\infty$-structure on the string homology $\widehat{H}_\ast^{S^1}(\mathcal{L}L;\mathbb{R})$, completed with respect to the action filtration. When the first Gutt-Hutchings capacity of $\overline{M}$ is finite, and $L$ is a $K(π,1)$ space, we show that $L$ bounds a pseudoholomorphic disc of Maslov index 2. This confirms a general form of Audin's conjecture and generalizes the works of Fukaya and Irie in the case of $\mathbb{C}^n$ to a wide class of Liouville manifolds, which includes low degree smooth affine hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$. In particular, when $\dim_\mathbb{R}(\overline{M})=6$, every closed, orientable, prime Lagrangian 3-manifold $L\subset\overline{M}$ is diffeomorphic either to a spherical space form, or $S^1\timesΣ_g$, where $Σ_g$ is a closed oriented surface.

papers.title: A biregular classification of smooth quotients of abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify smooth projective surfaces that are quotients of abelian surfaces by finite groups. We also record the orbifold boundary associated to a quotient map and describe its structure explicitly in the case of augmented irregularity one.

papers.title: Faster Algorithms for Structured Linear and Kernel Support Vector Machines
papers.abstract: Many machine learning problems are quadratic programs, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs). A general quadratic program has input size $Θ(n^2)$, and assuming the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH), no $O(n^{2-o(1)})$ time algorithm exists when the objective matrix is positive semidefinite (Backurs, Indyk, and Schmidt, NeurIPS'17). SVMs, however, are given by $n$ data points of dimension $d$, often much smaller than $n$, and have only $O(1)$ equality constraints. In this work, we design the first nearly-linear time algorithm for solving quadratic programs whenever a low-rank factorization of the quadratic objective matrix is given, the number of linear constraints is small, the coefficients of the objective and some optimal solution are bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(n)$, and some feasible point has all entries between $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and $\mathrm{poly}(n)$. For linear SVM on $d$-dimensional data, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $\widetilde O(nd^{(ω+1)/2}\log(n/ε))$ when $(d+1)^{ω-1}\le n$ and the data points have norms at most $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and margin at least $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$, where $ω<2.258$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Its output satisfies the equality constraint only approximately. For Gaussian kernel SVM, when $d=O(\log n)$, the squared dataset radius is $o(\log n/\log\log n)$ and the dual variables lie in a box $[0,R]^n$ with $R\le\mathrm{poly}(n)$, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $n^{1+o(1)}$ for any accuracy $ε\ge 1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$. We also prove that, assuming SETH, when the squared dataset radius is $Ω(\log^2 n)$, $Ω(n^{2-o(1)})$ time is required on some inputs to reach error $\exp(-Θ(\log^2 n))$ for the program without the bias term. This improves upon the prior best lower bound in both the dimension $d$ and the squared dataset radius.

papers.title: Stationarity with Occasionally Binding Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of multivariate threshold autoregressive models, known as censored and kinked structural vector autoregressions (CKSVAR), which are notably able to accommodate series that are subject to occasionally binding constraints. We develop a set of sufficient conditions for the processes generated by a CKSVAR to be stationary, ergodic, and weakly dependent. Our conditions relate directly to the stability of the deterministic part of the model, and are therefore less conservative than those typically available for general vector threshold autoregressive (VTAR) models. Though our criteria refer to quantities, such as refinements of the joint spectral radius, that cannot feasibly be computed exactly, they can be approximated numerically to a high degree of precision.

papers.title: Optimizer's Information Criterion: Dissecting and Correcting Bias in Data-Driven Optimization
papers.abstract: In data-driven optimization, the sample performance of the obtained decision typically incurs an optimistic bias against the true performance, a phenomenon commonly known as the Optimizer's Curse and intimately related to overfitting in machine learning. We develop a general approach that we call \emph{Optimizer's Information Criterion (OIC)} to correct this bias. OIC generalizes the celebrated Akaike Information Criterion from the evaluation of model adequacy, used primarily for model selection, to objective performance in data-driven optimization, which is used for decision selection. Our approach analytically approximates and cancels out the bias that comprises the interplay between model fitting and downstream optimization. As such, it saves the computational need to repeatedly solve optimization problems in cross-validation, while operating more generally than other bias approximating scheme. We apply OIC to a range of data-driven optimization formulations comprising empirical and parametric models, their regularized counterparts, and furthermore contextual optimization. Finally, we provide numerical validation of the superior performance of our approach under synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Cartesian Gray-Monoidal Double Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we present cartesian structure for symmetric Gray-monoidal double categories. To do this we first introduce locally cubical Gray categories, which are three-dimensional categorical structures analogous to classical, locally globular, Gray categories. The motivating example comprises double categories themselves, together with their functors, transformations, and modifications. A one-object locally cubical Gray category is a Gray-monoidal double category. Braiding, syllepsis, and symmetry for these is introduced in a manner analogous to that for 2-categories. Adding cartesian structure requires the introduction of doubly-lax functors of double categories to manage the order of copies. The resulting theory is algebraically rather complex, largely due to the bureaucracy of linearizing higher-dimensional boundary constraints. Fortunately, it has a relatively simple and compelling representation in the graphical calculus of surface diagrams, which we present.

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: On Iwasawa invariants of modular forms with reducible and non-$p$-distinguished residual Galois representations
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be the ordinary $p$-stabilization of the weight-one Eisenstein series, where $χ$ is odd and $χ(p)=1$. Under a Gorenstein hypothesis on the cuspidal Hecke algebra, we prove a factorization of the even branches of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function of $f$ by evaluating a cup product of cyclotomic units via local reciprocity. The odd branches follow from the Eisenstein specialization formula of Fukaya and Kato with a minor modification for the exceptional character considered here. We then obtain results on the $μ$- and $λ$-invariants. On the algebraic side, we compute the Selmer characteristic ideals at $f$ and the Iwasawa invariants of the higher-weight specializations. For every nontrivial twist of $f$, the ordinary characteristic ideal is generated by the corresponding $p$-adic $L$-function. On the untwisted branch it has one additional factor, the cyclotomic augmentation parameter. Imposing the strict local condition at $p$ removes this factor. For higher-weight specializations coming from newforms of level prime to $p$, Kato's divisibility then gives the cyclotomic main conjecture after inverting $p$.

papers.title: An Algebraic Approach to the Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Goldbach Conjecture using p-adic analysis and algebraic methods, requiring no knowledge of prime gaps or distribution. For $a \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{P}_a$ be the set of primes up to $a$. We prove that if a counter-example $2a$ exists, there is a monic polynomial $\mathcal{G}_-(z) \in \mathbb{Z}[z]$ where $\mathcal{G}_-(2a) = 0$. Applying Hensel's Lemma, we then show this polynomial structure forces each prime $p_i \in \mathcal{P}_a$ to satisfy $2a = p_i^{α_i} + p_i$ for a unique $α_i \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$. This produces a contradiction for $a > 4$ since each $2a - p_i > 1$ requires each $α_i > 0$ and the primorial, $a\#$, to satisfy $a\# \mid 2a$, which is impossible since $2a < a\#$ for all $a > 4$.

papers.title: Multiply Robust Causal Mediation Analysis with Continuous Treatments
papers.abstract: In many applications, researchers are interested in the direct and indirect causal effects of a treatment or exposure on an outcome of interest. Mediation analysis offers a rigorous framework for identifying and estimating these causal effects. For binary treatments, efficient estimators for the direct and indirect effects are presented by Tchetgen Tchetgen and Shpitser (2012) based on the influence function of the parameter of interest. These estimators possess desirable properties such as multiple-robustness and asymptotic normality while allowing for slower than root-n rates of convergence for the nuisance parameters. However, in settings involving continuous treatments, these influence function-based estimators are not readily applicable without making strong parametric assumptions. In this work, utilizing a kernel smoothing approach, we propose an estimator suitable for settings with continuous treatments inspired by the influence function-based estimation strategy. Our proposed approach employs cross-fitting, relaxing the smoothness requirements on the nuisance functions and allowing them to be estimated at slower rates than the target parameter. Additionally, similar to influence function-based estimators, our proposed estimator is multiply robust and asymptotically normal, allowing for inference in settings where parametric assumptions may not be justified.

papers.title: Adventures in Multi-Omics I: Combining heterogeneous data sets via relationships matrices
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose a covariance based method for combining partial data sets in the genotype to phenotype spectrum. In particular, an expectation-maximization algorithm that can be used to combine partially overlapping relationship/covariance matrices is introduced. Combining data this way, based on relationship matrices, can be contrasted with a feature imputation based approach. We used several public genomic data sets to explore the accuracy of combining genomic relationship matrices. We have also used the heterogeneous genotype/phenotype data sets in the https://triticeaetoolbox.org/ to illustrate how this new method can be used in genomic prediction, phenomics, and graphical modeling.

papers.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Training artificial neural networks predominantly relies on offline, gradient-based backpropagation algorithms. In contrast, biological circuits process and retain information through decentralized, continuous-time adaptation. In this work, we explore an online, gradient-free learning methodology by formulating the tuning of synaptic weights as a closed-loop trajectory tracking problem driven by model-free control principles. Rather than performing global optimization across static parameters, decentralized controllers adjust synaptic interactions in real-time using solely local input-output tracking errors. We present an exploratory benchmark neural architecture, whose purpose is to assess the dynamic resilience of the proposed approach, particularly in tracking target outputs and adapting to abrupt non-stationarities and structural perturbations (such as topological changes or dynamic dropout) without requiring offline retraining. This empirical preliminary study provides a proof-of-concept for control-theoretic learning paradigms and outlines the foundation for scalable, dynamically evolving connectome frameworks.

papers.title: Long time decay for global solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in the critical Sobolev--Gevrey space $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, $a>0$. We first prove local well-posedness, together with a global existence criterion and a blow-up criterion for the maximal solution. Our main result is that every global solution $u\in C\big([0,+\infty),\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)\big)$ satisfies $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}}\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$. The proof combines the classical decay of global solutions in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ with an analyticity estimate for small data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ and Fourier-analytic product laws in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces. As consequences, we obtain the decay rate $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^s}=o\big(t^{-\frac{s-1/2}{2}}\big)$ for every $s\ge\frac12$, and the stability of global solutions under small perturbations of the initial data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}$.

papers.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
papers.abstract: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusiński-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global Lê cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

papers.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3α+ 2β= π$
papers.abstract: An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(α,β,γ)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3α+ 2β= π$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $α$, $β$, or $α+β$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α,β,α+β)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α, α, 2β)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape. By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3α+ 2β= π$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2α,β,α+β)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $β$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price
papers.abstract: Comparing AI models across resource budgets yields quality-resource frontiers relating error to latency, parameter count, training compute, and energy. Offset power laws summarize such frontiers, but their fitted parameters reveal neither the price-independent geometry nor the manner in which trade-offs extend across several resource channels. This paper addresses both gaps by developing a differential theory in which this structure is made explicit. Each frontier admits a price-independent plane-curve representation relating the effective number of active resource channels, $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = s^2/κ$ (squared slope over curvature), to the remaining log-error depth, $ΔS = \ln(\varepsilon/\varepsilon_{\infty})$. This representation separates intrinsic shape from the scale and origin of the resource axis. Complete monotonicity and divisibility yield differential inequalities and frontier bounds. When each of $N$ resources contributes one active channel, the theory gives the parameter-free operating rule $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1$ in delivered units and derives minimax resource prices $λ^{\star}_i = α_i/(N+1)$ with an exact worst-case regret of $\ln(N+1)$ nats. The results make it possible to interpret measured frontiers and compare resource costs without hand-chosen exchange rates. The theory is evaluated on 117 published frontiers and implemented in the open-source package nn-rank, which derives prices from measured quality and cost, ranks candidates, and reports supported choices and minimax regret: https://github.com/ABrain-One/nn-rank

papers.title: Error Analysis of Deep Learning
papers.abstract: This review examines deep learning theory through the lens of error decomposition, systematically addressing approximation, statistical, and optimization errors. We trace the development of error analyses from bounds on individual error components to frameworks that account for all three. Using nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz Method as dual running examples, we demonstrate how these analyses apply across fundamentally different loss structures. We then review representative analyses in scientific machine learning, generative learning, reinforcement learning, representation learning, and large language models, showing how learning errors affect solutions, distributions, and predictions through problem-specific arguments. Throughout, we clarify which error components are controlled, how they are combined, and what assumptions are needed to obtain guarantees for trained networks.

papers.title: Covariance Cells And Star Products
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, a localized preparation is described not only by a point in phase space but also by a covariance cell specifying its finite resolution. We study balanced Gaussian cells on a linear symplectic space and show that they are equivalent to compatible complex structures and positive Lagrangian polarizations. Their parameter space is the Siegel symmetric space. Using the Koopman-von Neumann representation of classical mechanics, we describe the linearized transport of Gaussian amplitudes along a reference motion. Each covariance cell determines a separated star product whose antisymmetric part is fixed by the symplectic form and whose symmetric part is fixed by the covariance. This product is related to the Moyal product by Gaussian smoothing. Quadratic Hamiltonians act through their classical Poisson derivations within a fixed cell algebra exactly when they preserve the cell; squeezing transformations instead relate the algebras associated with different cells. Fronsdal's star-polarization construction yields a module whose cyclic element is the Gaussian density of the cell. Its completion is the corresponding Bargmann-Fock space, naturally embedded in the space of classical Koopman amplitudes. Koopman transport carries this Fock space to that of the transported cell. No Planck constant is introduced: the deformation parameter is a classical resolution scale, and physical observables remain commuting multiplication operators.

papers.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $χ^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Methods for Generalized Lipschitz Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a convex optimization problem, where the upper bound on the subgradient norm depends on the objective function. We establish a lower bound on the number of iterations required by any first-order method to find an approximate solution to the problem. Furthermore, we present two near-optimal algorithms that can match the lower bound up to logarithmic factors. The first algorithm is a projected GD with a carefully designed stepsize schedule which incorporates warm-up and decay phases. The second algorithm is scalar-stepsize clipped AdamW which extends the near-optimal guarantees to the stochastic setting, where only a noisy unbiased estimator of the subgradient is available.

papers.title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

papers.title: Strengthening Compact Vehicle Routing Formulations through Arc-Flow Aggregation and Refinement
papers.abstract: Arc-flow formulations can provide strong relaxations for mixed-integer program formulations of vehicle routing problems, but the associated networks may be prohibitively large. We study the setting in which multiple arc flow relaxations may be applied, and introduce a dual-guided aggregation and refinement framework that constructs substantially smaller arc-flow formulations while recovering the LP bound of the original networks. Dual information is used both to identify states that can be aggregated without weakening the bound and to guide node disaggregation. We show that the resulting procedure converges finitely to the arc-flow bound of the full arc-flow formulation. The framework retains the original decision variables, allowing cutting planes to be added directly in the original variable space. Moreover, it produces an explicit MILP formulation without relying on column generation or pricing to determine the arc-flow relaxation bound. We apply our approach to the vehicle routing problem with time windows for which we define two arc flow relaxations, as well as two families of cutting planes over the original variable space. Computational experiments show that strong bounds can be obtained using substantially aggregated networks. The resulting root bounds are competitive with those obtained by the branch-and-price solver RouteOpt, while retaining a formulation that can be solved directly by a general-purpose MILP solver.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $ρ\gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(μ_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is \(μ_L\)-stable and \(L\)-Gieseker-stable. The corresponding object \(E_{C,A}^{\vee}[1]\) for \(d<g-1\), or \(E_{C,A}\) for \(d>g-1\), is stable in the adjacent chamber, as its reduction. These results connect dimension estimates for Brill-Noether loci with stability and wall-crossing on abelian surfaces.

papers.title: Hochschild Cocycle and Universality of Merge
papers.abstract: The Hopf algebra Markov chain dynamical system, on the Hopf algebra of non-planar binary forests, that models the action of Merge on workspaces in Chomsky's Minimalist Model of syntax, satisfies a universal property, determined by the fact that the Merge operation is a Hochschild 1-cocycle. This universal property has an interpretation in terms of models of the syntax-semantics interface, as it shows that, if the side of semantics possesses a sufficiently rich compositional structure, then that structure is uniquely induced by the syntactic Merge, once the semantic values of lexical items and syntactic features are assigned. We illustrate how this universality works by showing, in particular, full compatibility of this Hopf algebraic formulation with Heim-Kratzer semantics.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
papers.abstract: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.

papers.title: On cover exacting cardinals
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goldberg about cover exacting cardinals. Concretely, we show that if $κ$ is $ω_1$-strongly compact, then no cardinal $λ>κ$ is $γ$-cover exacting for some cardinal $γ$.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part III: Oracle Complexity of Monotone Variational Inequalities with $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Operators
papers.abstract: We consider monotone variational inequalities in which the Jacobian norm of the operator $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is bounded by an affine function of the norm of the operator itself: $\|DF(z)\|\le L_0+L_1\|F(z)\|$. The main case is the problem on the whole space, that is, finding a zero of $F$. We assume that a solution exists and that an upper bound $R$ on the distance from the starting point to the solution is known. Neither strong monotonicity nor cocoercivity is assumed. Global Lipschitz continuity is not assumed either: for $L_1>0$, the Jacobian norm may grow together with the norm of the operator. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the number of oracle calls sufficient to find a point $\hat z$ with $\|F(\hat z)\|\le\varepsilon$. For $L_0R/\varepsilon\ge1$, both bounds are, up to logarithmic factors in $L_1R$, of order $1+L_0R/\varepsilon+(L_1R)^{6/5}$. The upper bound is attained by a deterministic extragradient-type method, and the lower bound holds for arbitrary randomized methods. The same bounds are obtained for the Minty gap on the ball of radius $R$, where $L_0R/\varepsilon$ is replaced by $L_0R^2/η$. In addition, we show that for a variational inequality on a bounded set the numbers $L_0,L_1$ and the diameter of the set are not sufficient: a uniform complexity bound requires additional information, for example, an upper bound on the norm of the operator at the solution.

papers.title: Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, let $T\subseteq V$, and let $F\subseteq E$. We call $F$ semi-cutting for $T$ if $d_{G}(u,w)<d_{G\setminus F}(u,w)$ for every two distinct terminals $u,w\in T$. We prove the sharp bound $|F|\ge |T|-1$. The argument is structural: semi-cutting sets are first identified with edge transversals of all shortest terminal-terminal paths, and the bound then follows from a contraction step, a terminal-deletion lemma, and a lexicographic induction on $(|T|,|V|)$.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $η\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $η$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $η=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
papers.abstract: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific. Maternal and Perinatal Health scored lowest (28.0%), followed by Dental and Oral Health (38.5%) and Behavioral Health (44.4%), while Long-Term Services and Supports (82.8%) and Experience of Care (67.8%) scored highest. State performance correlated strongly with national benchmarks (r = 0.77, approximately), so rates should be read against each measure's benchmark. Domain was the strongest predictor, and the model explained 31.2% of variance. Because of heteroscedasticity and influential observations from mixing bounded and utilization measures, estimates are descriptive. Quality improvement should be targeted by domain, prioritizing maternal health, behavioral health network adequacy, and dental provider participation.

papers.title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown $m$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{M}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is $F=f\circΠ_{\mathcal{M}}$, where $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the nearest-point projection onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $f:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}^p$ is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For $p\ge m$, under our geometric and sampling conditions, $n$ independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order $n^{-2/(m+4)}$ and integrated squared prediction error at the $m$-dimensional nonparametric rate $n^{-4/(m+4)}$, up to logarithmic factors. In a scaling regime with fixed intrinsic dimension, model and scale parameters, and ratio of manifold volume to the $m$-th power of its reach, the required sample size grows polynomially in $D+p$, and computation is polynomial in $n$, $D$ and $p$. Numerical experiments on curves with non-monotone links and surfaces with vector-valued responses compare observed convergence rates with the theoretical bounds; a Langevin dynamics example tests prediction of hitting probabilities under an approximate manifold-index model.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, I: the mass matrix and the polygon model
papers.abstract: A canonical metric $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ on $S^n \setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$, where $\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}=(p_1,\ldots,p_{\ell})$ and $n \ge 3$, is a metric conformal to the round metric that is complete, scalar-flat, and asymptotically flat at each puncture $p_i$. For $n=3$ these metrics are the Brill--Lindquist time-symmetric initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and their ends carry ADM masses. In this paper we study the masses, through the mass matrix, as functions on the conformal moduli space $M_{\ell}(S^n)$. The mass matrix $η=(η_{ij})$ is a symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and vanishing row sums (these matrices form the space $H_{\ell}$), and it determines the \emph{normalized ADM mass} at the $i$-th end via $\hat{\mathfrak{m}}_i=\sum_{j\ne i}e^{η_{ij}}$. We prove that the mass map $Ξ\colon M_\ell(S^n)\to H_{\ell}$ is a homeomorphism onto its image. On the other hand, the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_\ell(S^n)$ is homeomorphic to the moduli space of those equilateral $\ell$-gons in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$ whose sides, extended to infinity, end at distinct points (the Gauss map). By a theorem of Kapovich--Leeb--Millson and Balser, every polystable configuration is the Gauss image of such a polygon, and the Gauss map identifies the space of all equilateral $\ell$-gons with a natural compactification of $M_\ell(S^n)$. In particular, the mass matrix has an explicit description in terms of the pairwise vertex distances of the polygon. The mass matrix diverges as punctures collide. The degeneration, its renormalization, and the resulting compactification of the moduli space are the subject of a sequel to this paper.

papers.title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

papers.title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{ω^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
papers.abstract: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by Itô stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path. Each notion is characterized by a differential condition that is necessary and sufficient for contraction under mild hypotheses. Relations between contraction notions and an associated incremental input-to-state stability result are also established. As an illustration, we apply the established theory to analyze noise-induced synchronization and quantify its robustness with respect to parameter perturbations.

papers.title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

papers.title: Asymptotic radial symmetry of $p$-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers on the disk
papers.abstract: We solve the minimizer case of Brezis's Open Problem~2.3 for every fixed $p>2$.
