Andruskiewitsch and F. Dumas in \cite{AD}. We characterize a subgroup $\mathbb L$ stabilizing two one-dimensional vector spaces and obtain two semidirect product decompositions of it. This subgroup contains all super-automorphisms and its structure motivates our main result. Precisely, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}\mathcal B=\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$, where $\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$ denote, respectively, the groups of inner automorphisms and super-automorphisms of $\mathcal B$. We also characterize the nilpotent elements of $\mathcal B$ and prove that every nonzero nilpotent has nilpotency index two. Furthermore, we give a geometric interpretation of three distinguished families of nilpotent elements. After degree truncation and projectivization, two of these families yield projective linear subspaces, while the third yields quadratic Veronese varieties of arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: Minimax Estimation of Discrete Distributions under Hockey-stick Divergence
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of estimating a discrete distribution with respect to the hockey-stick divergence from independent samples. We provide non-asymptotic upper and lower bounds on the minimax expected loss in terms of the alphabet size, the number of samples, and the divergence parameter. The upper bounds are achieved by add-constant estimators, while the lower bound is derived via a Bayes risk argument. Both upper bounds and lower bounds reveal a transition between polynomial and exponential regimes as the parameters of the problem vary.

papers.title: A simplified temporal logic completeness proof
papers.abstract: A temporal logic discussed in the author's book "Logics of Time and Computation" is given a simpler proof of semantic completeness, eliminating some flaws in the original.

papers.title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

papers.title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and Bétermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of Bétermin--Šamaj--Travěnec [SAM 2023].

papers.title: Boundary regularity, finiteness and stability of energy-maximizing vortex patches
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for energy-maximizing vortex patches of the 2-D incompressible Euler equations in a bounded Jordan domain. These results resolve Turkington's free-boundary regularity question throughout the full range of admissible parameters. For bounded convex domains, we further prove that the set of energy maximizers is finite at each prescribed patch area. When the domain is smooth, the number of maximizers is uniformly bounded over all admissible patch areas, and every maximizer is Lyapunov stable in $L^p$ for any $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: The structure of varieties with nef anticanonical divisor in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a regular projective variety with nef anticanonical divisor over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $f:X\to A$ be a surjective morphism to an abelian variety. We prove that there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $f': X\times_AA' \to A'$ admits a Zariski locally trivial structure. If moreover $-K_X\equiv D$ for some semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D$, then $-K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}D$, and there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $ X\times_AA' \cong X_0\times A'$ where $X_0$ is the fiber over the identity $0\in A'$.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Cholesky with Error Guarantees
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators increasingly support low-precision formats such as 8-bit floats and integers to speed up machine learning. We show that a Cholesky factorization in which both GEMM and TRSM are implemented using the fixed-point Ozaki 1 scheme satisfies the same backward error bounds as the standard floating-point Cholesky factorization, and that the same holds for a Cholesky factorization computed using a low-precision MicroScaled GEMM. We then use our error analyses to construct an adaptive precision Cholesky factorization that exploits low-precision formats while respecting a prescribed element-wise error bound, as long as the factorization succeeds. We test it in two settings. First, we use it to choose the number of Ozaki 1 slices at each iteration, with SYRK/GEMM and TRSM emulated in INT8 fixed-point arithmetic to attain double-precision accuracy. Second, we use it to build a low-precision Cholesky preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method (PCG), in which SYRK/GEMM take low-precision inputs and accumulate in high precision, with the input format selected adaptively for each panel; if the factorization breaks down, diagonal perturbation still yields a valid preconditioner, at the cost of the error bound guarantees. On an NVIDIA GH200, the adaptive Ozaki 1-based factorization is up to 29% faster than a right-looking Cholesky using a fixed slice count of 7, and up to 69% faster than one using cuBLAS' Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP), while maintaining the same error guarantees. For PCG, FP8 factorizations with diagonal perturbation form effective preconditioners on the 13 tested SuiteSparse matrices, reducing the number of PCG iterations by up to $12\times$ over CG on the same matrix diagonally scaled by powers of two. For synthetic matrices with arithmetic spectra, and geometric spectra with $κ\le 10^4$, FP8 preconditioners also reduce the number of CG iterations.

papers.title: Inequality-Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode Control
papers.abstract: We present COSMIC (Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode for Inequality Constraints), a continuous-time solver for inequality-constrained optimization. COSMIC couples primal gradient-flow dynamics with multiplier dynamics derived from sliding mode control laws on a manifold defined by the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister function. We prove that COSMIC's trajectories reach this manifold in finite time from any primal initial point, after which the dynamics reduces to the gradient flow of a logarithmic barrier function. This yields a control-theoretic interpretation of barrier methods while allowing infeasible initialization. For strongly convex problems, we further establish exponential convergence to the minimizer. To address the numerical stiffness that arises in discretization, we develop a modified discrete-time algorithm. We validate COSMIC across various machine learning applications, demonstrating its ability to solve optimization problems accurately while scaling effectively to high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: A discontinuous time to collision feedback: well posedness, regularity of the collision-time map, and residual stability of its Hamilton Jacobi approximations
papers.abstract: We analyze a finite-horizon time-to-collision map generated by an optimal-velocity prediction with bounded measurable leader acceleration and a feedback law that uses this map. The prediction describes nominal motion without the additional collision-avoidance feedback. Its first-contact geometry can produce discontinuities of the capped collision time at grazing, so smooth-feedback theory does not apply globally. For a prescribed leader--follower pair, we prove existence of Filippov solutions and exclusion of contact with negative relative velocity for every solution; a zero-speed touch is not excluded. Under explicit nondegeneracy hypotheses, trajectories cross the grazing set and uniqueness persists through the crossing. On the domain of transversal first contacts, the collision-time map is locally Lipschitz, continuously differentiable in the state, and differentiable in time outside a common null set. We quantify its sensitivity to the transversality margin and to jumps of the forcing. Characteristic and coarea arguments give boundary-plus-interior residual estimates for Hamilton--Jacobi approximations. An endpoint/age change of variables yields a stability coefficient controlled by flight time and terminal normal velocity, without inverse-transversality blowup. The estimates imply convergence conditional on vanishing continuum loss and pointwise identification under the stated trace and regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments on thirteen prescribed forcing profiles investigate boundary-error transport, sampling effects, and regularity predictions; a separate first-contact experiment numerically demonstrates post-threshold sensitivity sign changes. The guarantees concern the exact feedback and value-function approximation. Learned-feedback safety and convergence of a training algorithm remain open.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

papers.title: Maximal dissipativity for the Dirichlet operator associated to the dynamical $Φ^4$ model on the plane
papers.abstract: We consider the Dirichlet/Kolmogorov operator associated with the stochastic quantization of the $Φ^4$ model on the plane whose domain is restricted to the space of smooth cylindrical functions. We prove that its closure is maximally dissipative in $L^p$. Our result implies the so-called $L^p$-uniqueness of the Dirichlet operator for every $1\le p<\infty$. In particular, essential self-adjointness and Markov uniqueness follow. The key ingredient is an estimate for the linearized equation for the dynamical $Φ^4_2$ model. The proof is based on techniques from singular SPDE theory and the stopping time argument introduced by Kunick and Tsatsoulis.

papers.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
papers.abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
papers.abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

papers.title: The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
papers.abstract: We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}ξ_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1π,\;\frac1π+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/π$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|ξ_0|^{2+δ}<\infty$ for some $δ>0$.

papers.title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests, cycles and complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. We disprove the Bialostocki--Dierker asymptotic conjecture for forests by constructing trees for every sufficiently large edge count whose ratio of zero-sum to two-color Ramsey numbers has lower limit at least $554/553>1$. For powers of two $q\ge2$, we characterize all $s,k\ge1$ satisfying $R(K_{s,kq},\mathbb Z_q)=s+kq$ and prove $R(mK_{q,q},\mathbb Z_m)=2qm+m/\gcd(m,q)-1$ for every $m\ge2$. The packing upper bound combines Caro's transfer inequality with our spanning result and sharpens earlier bounds when $\gcd(m,q)\ge4$. The formula also gives exact values for counterexamples to Caro's defect conjecture, whose failure was already implicit in earlier work of Caro and Caro--Provstgaard. For every integer $m\ge2$ and every multiple $\ell$ of $m$ with $\ell\ge100m^3$, we also prove $R(C_\ell,\mathbb Z_m)=\ell+m/\gcd(m,2)-1$ for the cycle $C_\ell$ on $\ell$ vertices, determining the eventual value left by the bounds of Chi and He for even moduli $m\ge4$.

papers.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
papers.abstract: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

papers.title: Derived invariance of holomorphic two-forms and homological motives of stably holomorphically symplectic varieties
papers.abstract: Let $Φ:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb C$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $Θ^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $Φ$. We prove that $Θ^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove that being stably holomorphically symplectic is a derived invariant, where a smooth projective variety is called stably holomorphically symplectic if it is a direct factor of a smooth projective holomorphic symplectic variety. For derived-equivalent varieties in this class, we construct an isomorphism of rational homological motives as unital algebra objects. In particular, their graded rational cohomology algebras are isomorphic compatibly with the Hodge structures.

papers.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences. For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class. The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.

papers.title: Integer Programming Parametrized by Imbalanced Circuit Packing
papers.abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

papers.title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete approximation of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise $(-A)^αdW$, $0\leα<1/4$, below the critical roughness threshold $α=1/4$. Through the Cole--Hopf transformation, the nonlinear equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation with spatially correlated multiplicative noise, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a scale-invariant regularized inverse Cole--Hopf transformation. The convergence analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with strict positivity and uniform inverse-moment bounds for the exact transformed solution. Under an initial approximation condition and a weak-$L^4$ tail assumption on the transformed initial datum, we obtain the spatial strong convergence rates arbitrarily close to $1/2-2α$ and a temporal rate of order $1/2$, up to a logarithmic correction. For $0\leα<1/4$, the spatial rate is essentially sharp within the spectral Galerkin framework, the temporal rate is independent of the roughness parameter $α$, and we prove a converse estimate showing both the necessity of the initial approximation condition and the weak-$L^4$ tail of the initial datum.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A companion project on Lean v4.35 imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.06.

papers.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
papers.abstract: Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying constraint families, and each candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, as in classical lot-sizing, network-design, and facility-location formulations. We prove that when an evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, methods that observe only bounds need of order $k^w$ evaluations to find a hidden group of $w$ families in the worst case. A prediction missing $e$ members reduces this to $Θ(k^e)$ through a staged search that need not know $e$. The orders extend to several groups, prices, and growing evaluation costs. We study two predictors: a lookahead at an optimal LP dual, which vanishes on groups whose families share no variable, and language models reading the model, verified by the staged search in JointDW. Such groups appear in three of ten MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved and in all 59 benchmark instances. Given the coefficients of constructed models with up to 16 families, one language model names a true group first in 249 of 252 answers. On the benchmark instances, decompositions chosen by language models from the text solve faster than those of GCG's detector.

papers.title: Relative cohomology and base-change
papers.abstract: In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.

papers.title: Operator Fejér-Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial $F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)[x]$ positive semidefinite on $K$ admits a certificate in the operator quadratic module generated by $S$, with weighted degree at most $\operatorname{deg} F+c_S$. Here, $c_S$ depends only on $S$ and is independent of both $F$ and the coefficient Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, which may be infinite-dimensional. In contrast to the scalar case, natural matrix preorderings admit no uniform degree bound over compact semialgebraic subsets of the real line. We construct positive semidefinite quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees tend to infinity as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap remains bounded below. Conversely, uniform degree bounds hold for interval unions in a fixed compact interval when the component and gap lengths are bounded below by positive constants. Our proofs develop two techniques. The first is a quadratic reduction principle that reduces the problem of obtaining degree bounds for arbitrary-degree operator polynomials to the quadratic case, with a fixed additive increase in degree. The second uses a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil to transfer positivity on unions of intervals to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér-Riesz theorem provides certificates. We also obtain operator-valued Fejér-Riesz factorizations on unions of circular arcs, rational certificates with a fixed denominator on unbounded semialgebraic sets, and a characterization of the sets whose natural operator preorderings admit degree-preserving certificates.

papers.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.

papers.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

papers.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior
papers.abstract: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevič region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining rows have a Toeplitz pattern. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand, first reaching the full Karpelevič region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$ for $n\ge3$. Reproducing every complete stochastic spectrum, with multiplicities, requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. For a boundary arc whose endpoints have orders $q<s$ as roots of unity, the least $m$ needed to attain the whole arc is $0$ for $q=1$ and $\left\lceil\frac12\left\lfloor n/q\right\rfloor\right\rceil$ for $q\ge2$. For a Karpelevič boundary arc whose nonreal points between the endpoints first occur as stochastic eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, fixing any one of these eigenvalues fixes the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ with that eigenvalue. For these arcs and $m\ge1$, our family attains either the whole arc or only its endpoints. Further results describe the smaller eigenvalue regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.

papers.title: Countable unions of intervals without Riesz spectra
papers.abstract: We prove that every set $S = \bigcup_{n = 0}^{\infty} [ t_{2 n + 1} , t_{2 n} )$, where $t_0 > t_1 > \cdots > 0$ and $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} t_n = 0$, admits no Riesz spectrum, that is, no system of exponentials is a Riesz basis for $L^2 ( S )$. Up to a reflection and a null set, this class contains the example of Kozma, Nitzan, and Olevskii (2023). Moreover, combining with the result of Kozma and Nitzan (2015), we show that a bounded countable union of pairwise disjoint intervals of positive length whose endpoints have exactly one accumulation point admits a Riesz spectrum if and only if it is a finite union of intervals up to a null set.

papers.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
papers.abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

papers.title: A discontinuous Galerkin method for biharmonic Dirichlet control problems with patch reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-33}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

papers.title: On the Characterization Problem for Krull Monoids with Homocyclic Class Group
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a central problem in the factorization theory of Krull domains in which every class contains a prime divisor. It is well-known that the system of length sets depends on the class group only and the question is whether this system carries enough information to recover the underlying class group. We give an affirmative answer for all homocyclic class groups $C_n^r$. More precisely, let $D$ be a Krull domain with class group $C_n^r$, with $n, r \in \mathbb N$, and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. If the system of length sets $\mathcal L (C_n^r)$ is equal to a system of length sets $\mathcal L (G)$, for any finite abelian group $G$ with $\mathsf D (G) \ge 4$, then $G \cong C_n^r$. The central tools are cross numbers of (minimal) zero-sum sequences over the class group.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.abstract: We consider an attractor $Λ$ of a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbf M^d$ with a trapping neighborhood $U$ and an extendable continuous invariant splitting $T_{\overline U}\mathbf M^d=E\oplus F$. Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures on $Λ$ that satisfy Pesin's entropy formula and have negative Lyapunov exponents on $E$ and positive exponents on $F$. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures, and the corresponding sets of asymptotically hyperbolic points are covered, modulo Lebesgue null sets, by the basins of at most countably many such measures. We give necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of ergodic SRB measures with these exponent signs in terms of derivative growth and orbit statistics, and characterize the relationship between physical measures, strongly observable measures, physical-like measures and such SRB measures. We also construct examples with unique hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
papers.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

papers.title: Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $ε$-Nash equilibrium property is established.

papers.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $Σ$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,Φ)$ with $(E,Φ)\cong(E,-Φ)$. Using the non-abelian Hodge correspondence, we show that the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $η\mapsto-η$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.title: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all bounded definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. These beautiful pairs are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields. We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields -- considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$.

papers.title: Provable Method of Moments for Cryo-EM
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional volume in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) from noisy tomographic projections acquired at unknown viewing rotations, drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. We show that, in a spherical-shell representation satisfying an explicit shell-separation condition, the first three moments generically determine the underlying real volume up to its intrinsic global $\mathrm{O}(3)$ ambiguity. The proof is constructive and yields a frequency-marching procedure that successively recovers the volume. Consequently, consistent recovery in the high-noise regime has sample complexity $n=ω(σ^6)$, where $n$ is the number of observations and $σ^2$ is the noise variance. Numerical experiments validate the constructive recovery scheme under finite sampling and additive noise, and indicate that direct third-moment optimization can succeed beyond the structural assumptions required by the constructive proof.

papers.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing and quantitative transversality on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on spetral designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
papers.abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{λ,μ}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities ($λ\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $μ\in\mathbb{R}$). Furthermore, we provide explicit expressions for cocycles generating these spaces.

papers.title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
papers.abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent mean zero random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$ that need not be identically distributed. Let $S_n$ denote the sum, $Σ=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\ne0$, and let $G\sim N(0,Σ)$. Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}Σ}{\|Σ\|}, \qquad v(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(Σ^2)}{\|Σ\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions $r(Σ)\le C_Σv(Σ)$ and $v(Σ)\ge6$, we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(Σ)}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The approximation error thus tends to zero when $r(Σ)=o(n)$, even if $p$ grows faster than $n$. We also provide an example showing that the order $r(Σ)/n$ is sharp in general. The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof combines Esseen smoothing, truncation, covariance partitioning, moment matching, frame/lattice estimates, a second-order endpoint expansion and comparison estimates expressed in terms of the covariance matrices.

papers.title: Strong transport noise prevents self-intersection in 2D fluid-structure interaction
papers.abstract: We consider the interaction of a viscous incompressible fluid with a flexible elastic shell occupying the boundary of the fluid's domain in two space dimensions. The shell is modelled by a visco-elastic linearised beam equation. It is an open problem in fluid-structure interaction, if a self-intersection of the structure can be excluded in the long run. We show that by adding a physically well-motived and sufficiently strong transport noise in the structure equation, the self-intersection does not occur before any given end-time with any prescribed probability smaller than 1.

papers.title: Inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson structures from vector field samples
papers.abstract: We present a method for the data-driven inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson dynamical systems from vector-field samples, in which the Hamiltonian and the underlying Poisson tensor are estimated jointly rather than assuming the structure is known. The Hamiltonian is represented as a linear combination of random feature maps with fixed random internal weights, so its estimation is a linear regression problem for any given Poisson structure. We treat three cases of increasing generality: a known Poisson tensor, an unknown constant invertible (symplectic) structure matrix, and Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson structures, with structure matrix linear in the state. In the constant case, the Hamiltonian and structure matrix are recovered jointly from an eigenvalue problem that avoids the trivial zero solution due to the scaling symmetry of Hamiltonian systems. For Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson systems we alternate between an initial Hamiltonian estimate from a generalized eigenvalue problem for an approximate first integral, and a constrained nonlinear least-squares fit of the structure constants that enforces the Jacobi identity and, for affine structures, the cocycle condition, via continuation in a penalty parameter. Orthogonal matching pursuit selects a compact, well-conditioned subset of random features. Because the learned Hamiltonian is a sum of single-feature terms, the model admits an explicit Poisson/symplectic splitting integrator, which we use to validate the learned systems via long-time Poincare sections. We demonstrate the approach on the four- and five-dimensional Lorenz-86 model and a six-dimensional Kirchhoff rigid-body system, recovering Hamiltonians, structure constants and Casimir invariants to high accuracy, and showing the inferred Poincare sections converge to the correct invariant-tori topology as the number of random features increases.

papers.title: Strictly positive optimal Hardy weights on manifolds and graphs via Green potential
papers.abstract: Consider a subcritical functional $Q$ associated with a $p$-Schrödinger operator defined on a domain $Ω$ in a noncompact Riemannian manifold. Employing the supersolution construction, we obtain a family of strictly positive-critical Hardy weights for $Q$. The construction is based on the Green potential $G_f$, with a strictly positive charge $f$ such that $G_f$ vanishes at infinity. An interesting new feature of this family, depending on a parameter $0\leq \varepsilon\leq 1$, is the transition from positive-criticality to null-criticality at $\varepsilon=0$. Furthermore, we prove an analogous result on graphs.

papers.title: Boundary Collisions and Weak Excitation in LQR Policy-Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: Closed-loop stability concerns all initial states, whereas an LQR cost evaluates only the directions excited by a prescribed initial-state distribution. We study how this distinction affects Euclidean policy-gradient flows. For every nonzero deficient covariance rank, we construct relatively open families of controllable data and open sets of stabilizing initial gains whose exact gradient trajectories reach the stability boundary in finite optimization time. The state Gramian can remain positive definite at every time before collision. By separating the cost contribution of a critical mode, we obtain a local collision criterion based on direction attraction and motion toward the stability boundary. Adding excitation of strength $\varepsilon$ yields matching $Θ(\sqrt\varepsilon)$ bounds on the local minimum stability margin for trajectories that would otherwise collide. For a class of single-input, corank-one systems, these bounds hold over the entire trajectory without a common compact-set assumption. Numerical examples further illustrate the dynamics and scaling laws.

papers.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
papers.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

papers.title: Congruences for Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts
papers.abstract: In recent work, authors defined $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ to be the number of overcolored partition $k$-tuples wherein both even and odd parts are colored with $r$ and $s$ colors, respectively. This function generalizes the overcubic partition $k$-tuples studied by Chacon and Sellers. The present work gives a uniform framework for studying congruences for $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ modulo odd primes. For example, we prove that, for $n\ge 1$, \begin{align*} \bar{b}_{4,2}^4(5n)\equiv 0\pmod{5}. \end{align*}

papers.title: Recursive Paintboxes and the Martin Boundary of the Hoffman Rooted-Tree Graph
papers.abstract: We determine the Martin boundary of the Hoffman graph on unlabelled non-plane rooted trees and classify the central measures on its path space. Every boundary point is minimal, and the boundary is parametrized by deterministic recursive paintboxes up to equality of their finite sampling laws. The probabilities of sampling trees whose root has a single child determine the root branch masses and their associated boundary points, and characterize convergence on the boundary. Under any central measure, the successive tree shapes converge almost surely to a random boundary point whose law is the unique mixing measure in the extremal decomposition. For recursive Ewens trees, this limit is represented by a random paintbox with independent Poisson--Dirichlet splits at its vertices, and the mixing measure has no atoms. This applies in particular to the uniform recursive-tree law and Fulman's rooted-tree Plancherel law.

papers.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
papers.abstract: We implement a program of constructing a reflectionless measure on a Widom set with a nontrivial singular continuous component of Nazarov-Volberg and Yuditskii. The construction is an induction that based on two types of operations: splitting point mass and inserting bands. Each operation is realized by multiplying the Cauchy transform of the measure by some explicit multipliers. We provide necessary estimates on measures and the Green functions after each operation.

papers.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
papers.abstract: In their studies of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola--Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems $S'$ and $S'_T$, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension $T$ of Peano arithmetic ($\mathrm{PA}$), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in $T$, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a $T$-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's $S'$ is the case $T=\mathrm{PA}$. More generally, for consistent $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when $T$ proves every true $Π^0_1$ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$ by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if $T$ is $Σ^0_1$-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

papers.title: Selberg sieve weights and sign changes of Kloosterman sums. II. Square-free moduli with at most four prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $\operatorname{Kl}(1;q)$ denote the normalized Kloosterman sum modulo $q$. We prove that, for each sign, there are $\gg X/\log X$ square-free moduli $q\in(X,2X]$ with at most four prime factors for which $\operatorname{Kl}(1;q)$ has that sign. The proof combines the Selberg sieve with equidistribution and mean-square estimates for Kloosterman sums; the uniform estimate for shifted sieve weights established in Part I controls the contribution of moduli having small prime factors.

papers.title: Selberg sieve weights and sign changes of Kloosterman sums. I. Uniform asymptotics for shifted weights
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for smoothed correlations of divisor sums with independently shifted quadratic cutoff functions. With $Y$ denoting the averaging scale, $R$ the divisor cutoff, and $g$ a fixed smooth averaging weight, the error is $O_g(Y/(\log Y)^2)$, uniformly for $Y^{1/5}\leq R\leq Y^{1/3}$ and shifts $s,u\in[0,1/2]$, including coincident shifts. The main term is an explicit bilinear form in the first and second derivatives of the cutoff functions. The proof uses a fixed zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta-function to evaluate the relevant Mellin integrals by successive contour shifts and residue calculations. We also obtain a mean-square estimate for differences of shifted divisor sums, which is used in Part II to control small prime factors in the study of sign changes of Kloosterman sums.

papers.title: Principal component error in high-dimensional factor models
papers.abstract: In a statistical factor model, principal components (or eigenvectors) of a sample covariance matrix serve as estimates of principal directions, the true drivers of co-movement of a collection of observed variables. We write the often substantial error in these estimates as a sum of two interpretable terms, which we show have almost sure asymptotic limits as the number of variables grows with sample size bounded. This scenario is commonplace in financial economics, genomics, machine learning and signal processing. Out-of-subspace error measures the distance from an estimate to the subspace spanned by population factor exposures. It can be expressed in terms of data, providing an estimable floor for asymptotic error. In-subspace error is driven by a rotation error within that subspace, which arises from the fixed sample size of the latent factor returns and cannot be estimated from data alone. We illustrate our error analysis with a three-factor simulation of the US public equity market, showing the dependence of the magnitude of the error and its components on dimension and sample size. In that simulation, out-of-subspace error dominates. Researchers who rely on principal component analysis to estimate factor models can use our results to quantify errors in model-based predictions and attributions.

papers.title: The Powers-Størmer-Ogata inequality for operator monotone functions
papers.abstract: We show that for any positive operator monotone function $f$ the inequality $\int_{[0,\infty)} f(t) \, \mathrm{d} \left\lVert E^{Δ_{\varphi,ψ}}(t) ξ_ψ\right\rVert^2 + f'_\infty \varphi(1-s(ψ)) \geq \frac{f(1)}{2} \Bigl( \varphi(1) + ψ(1) - \lVert \varphi - ψ\rVert \Bigr)$ holds, where $\varphi, ψ\in \mathcal{M}_{*,+}$ are two normal positive linear functionals on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$, and $Δ_{\varphi,ψ}$ is the associated relative modular operator. Choosing $f(t) = t^s$ with $s \in [0,1]$, the Powers-Størmer-Ogata inequality is recovered.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: Product structures and decompositions of $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the decomposition and product theory of $Γ$-symmetric spaces, where $Γ$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. These results lead to the local classification of semisimple Riemannian $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces of nontrivial type. Furthermore, we identify notable phenomena specific to $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spaces: the existence of distinct product structures and that of an example with the trivial infinitesimal isotropy representation.

papers.title: Positive biorthogonal curvature on $S^2$-bundles over closed surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct an explicitly one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics with positive biorthogonal curvature on $S^2\times T^2$, answering a question raised by Bettiol. The method also yields metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on every smooth oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. Since $π_1(S^2\times T^2)=\mathbb Z^2$ is not virtually free, these examples separate positive biorthogonal curvature from positive isotropic curvature at the level of fundamental groups.

papers.title: Network recovery from aggregated relational data: alignment and resolution
papers.abstract: We prove that labeled edge probabilities can be recovered uniformly from complete aggregated relational data (ARD) at a given community composition if and only if the sum of trait alignment and partition resolution diverges. We study a two-community logistic network with fixed known weak signal and $K$ trait groups of size $m$. If $b_k$ is the difference between the two community counts in group $k$, alignment $Λ=\|b\|_2^2/m$ measures separation in the mean counts. Resolution $ρ=K/m^2$ measures the information that accumulates across groups through joint count fluctuations. Without knowing $b$, the full count likelihood gives a mean squared error bounded by $Ce^{-c(Λ+ρ)}+O((Km)^{-2})$ under bounded-energy activity perturbations. At exact group balance and zero activity, the minimax risk is $\exp\{-Θ(ρ)\}$ as $ρ\to\infty$. Uniform recovery over all globally balanced community assignments holds exactly when $ρ\to\infty$. At zero activity, when the community assignment is uniform over all balanced assignments, the optimal mean squared error averaged over assignments and networks vanishes exactly when $K\to\infty$. The population count law identifies every edge probability, and full adjacency permits uniform recovery throughout the model.

papers.title: Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the combinatorial object $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ which counts the colored overpartition $k$-tuples wherein both even and odd parts occurs with $r$ and $s$ colors, respectively. We establish several congruences which extends the results of Chacon and Sellers for infinite families of $r,s$ and $k$. In particular, we prove divisibility properties for $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)$ modulo prime $p$ and derive new congruences modulo powers of $2$. The techniques involved to obtain our results rely on theta function identities and modular forms.

papers.title: The direct moving plane method for weak solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop the method of moving planes entirely in the weak formulation for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in the singular range $1<p\leq2$. We first establish a small region principle for antisymmetric functions and apply it to prove radial symmetry and monotonicity of nonnegative weak solutions of fractional $p$-Laplacian equations in a bounded domain. We also consider the nonlocal quasilinear Lane--Emden equation $(-Δ)^s_pu=u^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. In the Sobolev critical case, we establish radial symmetry, monotonicity, and precise asymptotic behavior at infinity for finite-energy weak solutions. Under a suitable decay condition, we also obtain radial symmetry for the full range $q>p-1$. Our proofs rely on integral estimates derived directly from the weak formulation, thereby extending the moving plane approach of Chen and Li (Adv. Math. 2018: 735-758) from the pointwise $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ setting to weak solutions.

papers.title: A Full-Sequence Quantitative Gap Between the Chromatic and Cochromatic Numbers of a Random Graph
papers.abstract: The cochromatic number $ζ(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the least number of parts in a partition of $V(G)$ into cliques and independent sets, so $ζ(G)\leχ(G)$. Erdős and Gimbel asked whether $χ(G_n)-ζ(G_n)\to\infty$ with high probability for $G_n\sim G(n,1/2)$. Heckel answered this affirmatively for about $95\%$ of all integers $n$ and conjectured that the natural order of the difference along the full sequence is $n/(\ln n)^3$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$ through all integers, $χ(G_n)-ζ(G_n)\ge0.063\,n/(\ln n)^3$ with high probability. The failure probabilities are summable, so under any coupling of the graphs $G_n$ the bound holds almost surely for all sufficiently large $n$. The proof counts partitions of the vertex set into classes of five consecutive sizes, each class declared independent or complete. The two choices per class outweigh the entropy lost by restricting the class sizes, so the expected number of such partitions is large already at a number of classes that lies order $n/(\ln n)^3$ below the first-moment lower bound for the chromatic number, uniformly in the rounding phase. A second-moment argument, which controls all overlaps between two such partitions, including whole shared classes and large intersections of unequal classes, bounds the probability that such a partition exists from below. Vertex-exposure concentration, together with a coloring of the leftover vertices, then raises this to high probability at a cost of $o(n/(\ln n)^3)$ extra classes.

papers.title: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation and Retry Feedback in LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language model providers are compute constrained, and a common response to congestion is to degrade service: route queries to smaller models, cut reasoning budgets, or shorten context windows. A user who receives an unsatisfactory answer either retries, adding load while the system is busy, or abandons, possibly as churn. We model inference serving as a control problem in which service quality is the provider's decision. A two-regime fluid approximation with retries folded into the service rate gives closed-form trajectories and crossing times, so the dynamic program over quality tiers needs no simulation. We characterize a region in which a weaker tier uses less energy per task but more capacity per task, and show that in the fluid model reactive throttling to such a tier can keep the queue from draining. With heterogeneous customers the problem is a transportation problem with retry-inflated capacity coefficients; optimal routing follows a $cμ$-type index, and the dual of the capacity constraint gives the marginal cost of one more query by class and time. We illustrate the method on five instances calibrated to public benchmark data.

papers.title: On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category
papers.abstract: We develop an $\infty$-categorical framework for internal homotopy theory (truncations, homotopy groups, and Eilenberg-MacLane objects) of an accessible localization of an $\infty$-topos. For the motivic localization over a perfect field $k$, we show that a motivic space has trivial motivic $n$-truncation iff it has trivial Nisnevich $n$-truncation ($n\geq-2$), identifying internal $n$-Eilenberg-MacLane objects with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of groups when $n=1$ and strictly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of abelian groups when $n\geq2$. We further prove that a generically free Nisnevich group sheaf is strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff it is birational (which for the free group sheaf $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ holds iff $A$ is birational), whereas for an étale-weakly unramified sheaf of sets $A$, $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff $A$ is itself $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Non-birational, étale-weakly unramified motivic sheaves of sets (such as $\mathbb{G}_m$) thus generate (non-abelian) $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves that are not strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Combining this obstruction with essentially smooth base change, we prove that for a qcqs scheme $S$, $\mathcal{H}^{mot}(S)$ is an $\infty$-topos iff $S=\emptyset$. We also study relative truncation and connectivity under a localization. Over a qcqs scheme $S$, this identifies external $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings with internal motivic $n$-coverings via pullback along the localization unit, yielding a motivic $n$-Galois correspondence over $k$. For connective morphisms over $k$, we establish a higher $\mathbb{A}^1$-Van Kampen theorem and a Nisnevich-local-to-global $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-connectivity criterion; in particular, a $k$-scheme is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected iff it admits a Nisnevich cover by $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected schemes whose pairwise fiber products have $k$-points.

papers.title: Time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with a general external force in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-
abla_{x}φ\cdot 
abla_{v}f +  rac{1}{2}v \cdot 
abla_{x}φf$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.

papers.title: Stochastic partial differential equation model for environmental DNA dynamics in river environments
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a novel tool for quantifying the seasonal abundance of aquatic species in water bodies; however, its mathematical modeling is still at a germinating stage because of its mechanistic uncertainties. We propose a first-step mathematical and computational framework for the eDNA dynamics of migratory fish based on a novel stochastic partial differential equation model with a delayed source input. The model governs spatiotemporal eDNA concentration in rivers where the source comes from a stochastic differential equation for the migration dynamics of the fish. The affine nature of the model facilitates its theoretical analysis, including the guarantee of well-posedness and the closed-form derivation of the Laplace functional despite the proportionality coefficient of the multiplicative noise term being non-Lipschitz. We also propose a discretization scheme for the model that theoretically generates nonnegative numerical solutions. We finally apply the proposed model to eDNA concentration data sampled from midstream reaches of a river system and perform sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval
papers.abstract: Randomly initialized first-order iterative algorithms are simple, widely used, and empirically effective across many high-dimensional inference problems, yet their theoretical behavior remains far less understood than that of algorithms started from more elaborate, problem-specific initializations such as spectral initialization. This paper takes a step toward closing this gap by studying randomly initialized approximate message passing (AMP) for noiseless phase retrieval, a canonical nonconvex inference problem. We give a non-asymptotic, growing-horizon characterization of the AMP trajectory from random initialization, and show that it achieves both the information-theoretic weak recovery threshold $δ_{\rm weak}=1/2$ and the AMP strong recovery threshold $δ_{\rm str}\approx1.13$, matching the recovery thresholds established for spectrally initialized AMP. The key technical ingredients are twofold: (i) a non-asymptotic coupling that decomposes the AMP iterates as a signal component, a linear combination of independent Gaussian vectors, and an approximation error, and (ii) a second-order analysis of the Onsager correction error built around a non-asymptotic version of Bolthausen's condition. These allow us to analyze the $O_δ(\log n)$ steps required for weak recovery, and to faithfully track the asymptotic state evolution up to $n^{1/3}/\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps in the intermediate recovery regime $δ\in(δ_{\rm weak},δ_{\rm str})$, both beyond the $O(1)$-iteration horizon of classical AMP theory. Above the strong recovery threshold, AMP reaches any prescribed fixed recovery accuracy within $O_{δ,\varepsilon}(\log n)$ iterations. Both the coupling and the error analysis are developed for a broad class of generalized AMP dynamics and may be of independent interest for general single-index models.

papers.title: Counterexamples, Spectral Obstructions, and Deletion Stability for WOW-284
papers.abstract: WOW-284 is a Graffiti conjecture asserting that every connected graph of order at least three and girth at least five has minimum dual degree at most $-λ_{\min}(D)$, where $D$ is the distance matrix and the dual degree of a vertex is the average degree of its neighbors. We refute it with exact counterexamples on $38$, $39$, $40$, $42$ and $50$ vertices and study the structure of regular counterexamples. For a connected $k$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least five and diameter three, we prove that $δ^*(G)+λ_{\min}(D)=2k-2-\max_θ(θ+1)^2$, the maximum being over the nonprincipal adjacency eigenvalues, so strict failure is a spectral window condition. The closed window $|θ+1|\le\sqrt{2k-2}$ alone, without any diameter assumption, forces $|V(G)|<(k+2)(k^2+3)/6$ when $k\ge4$, and an integral excess matrix derived from the optimal polynomial sharpens this bound for diameter-three counterexamples. Every regular strict counterexample has degree at least six and diameter at most four, and in degree six it has at most $50$ vertices. Under vertex deletion, the Hoffman-Singleton graph remains a strict counterexample after the removal of any five vertices, while an explicit six-vertex deletion destroys strictness. A degree-$57$ Moore graph, if one exists, remains a connected strict counterexample after the removal of any $56$ vertices. Every strict counterexample has at least $15$ vertices, and an exhaustive search excludes orders up to $19$. The strict induced subgraphs of the Hoffman-Singleton graph of orders $36$ to $50$ are classified up to automorphism; among them are three further irregular counterexamples of order $40$.

papers.title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging
papers.abstract: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) underlies matrix factorisation tasks across many fields, with imaging applications demanding cost-efficient processing. Yet SVD algorithms are inherently sequential, constraining GPU throughput and limiting online deployment in imaging pipelines.
