This study introduces a fully parallelized matrix factorization framework for GPUs by enforcing matrix orthogonality on left singular vectors via Lie-parametrised algebra and recovering the remaining components through soft constraints. This asymmetric constraint design enables an efficient parallel decomposition with an orthogonal left factor, achieves high reconstruction fidelity and substantially accelerates computation relative to the exact SVD, with high throughput exceeding standard video frame rates. Performance is evaluated on multiple imaging tasks spanning complementary computational regimes: (1) an MNIST denoising benchmark at an intermediate scale with known ground truth, (2) Mueller matrix polarimetry for neurosurgical tissue characterisation, requiring massive batch processing of small matrices, and (3) spatio-temporal background subtraction for ultrasound localisation microscopy, requiring high-dimensional matrix separation. Across regimes and instruments, the proposed framework demonstrates robust domain transfer at various matrix scales and 2.6--67$\times$ speed-ups over the exact GPU SVD, and, unlike randomised SVD, accelerates large batches of small full-rank matrices. By prioritising downstream reconstruction fidelity over exact spectral recovery, the proposed SVD framework enables GPU-friendly matrix factorisation.

papers.title: The Liouville equation on Riemannian surfaces: the role of volume growth in classification and rigidity results
papers.abstract: We study the Liouville equation $-Δ_g u = e^u$ on a complete, connected, non-compact, boundaryless Riemannian surface $(M, g)$ with non-negative Ricci curvature. Assuming only some asymptotic lower bound on the solution, we establish classification results for both the solutions and the ambient manifold, discussing also their optimality. Our results reveal a close connection between the volume growth of the manifold and the classification of both the solutions and the underlying manifold.

papers.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
papers.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3214 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.481e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic points of the circle. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.

papers.title: A Direction Adaptation Evolution Strategy for Noisy Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.abstract: In noisy derivative-free optimization (DFO), methods based on the matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES) often mistakenly identify points with spuriously good function values, undermining selection and leading to unreliable search directions. To address this, we develop a novel direction adaptation evolution strategy (DAES) that targets the algorithmic phases prone to noise propagation, combining selected-population search with complexity analysis. Fixing the transformation matrix to the identity, DAES employs a structured direction-generation mechanism consisting of symmetric sampling, joint sorting--selection of noisy values, partitioning of all sampled directions into three ranked groups, and construction of a heuristic search direction. Along this direction, a noisy derivative-free sufficient descent condition with extrapolation is applied. Using a probabilistic angle condition preserved through our proposed framework, we obtain, to the best of our knowledge, the first high-probability evaluation-complexity bounds for a noisy MAES-type method across nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex objectives, under bounded noise. Finally, experiments on 230 BARON BCP problems across eight noise levels compare DAES with five DFO solvers, notably MADFO, showing greater robustness at intermediate-to-small budgets.

papers.title: Exterior power operations on relative K-theory
papers.abstract: We algebraically construct exterior power operations on higher relative algebraic K-groups and prove their desired properties such as the expected behaviour with respect to (tensor) products and composition. This builds on Grayson's description of relative K-groups in terms of explicit generators and relations and on work by Harris, the first author and Taelman for (absolute) K-groups. Among the new features in our approach is the observation that the product axiom in the classical notion of a lambda-ring is redundant.

papers.title: Kalman structure and observability for transport systems
papers.abstract: We study observability and controllability for constant-coefficient first-order hyperbolic systems on the real line when only part of the state is observed or controlled. Even when the Kalman rank condition holds, the usual \(L^2(\mathbb R)^N\)-observability estimate may fail because some components are detected only through the dynamics. We show that the Kalman structure determines the appropriate observability estimate. A component that becomes visible after \(k\) algebraic steps is measured at low Fourier frequencies with a weight of order \(|ξ|^{2k}\) in the Fourier variable. This yields a natural Kalman-adapted observation space for the system. Assuming that the transport matrix \(A\) is diagonalizable over \(\mathbb R\), we prove whole-line observability in this space for every positive time and derive exact controllability in the corresponding dual space. If, in addition, \(A\) has no zero eigenvalue and the observation set satisfies the one-dimensional bounded-gap condition, we establish localized observability whenever the observation time exceeds the natural characteristic travel-time threshold. Separately, in the whole-line setting, we extend the construction to transport matrices \(A\) with real spectrum and possible nontrivial Jordan blocks.

papers.title: K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras and iquantum groups with unequal parameters
papers.abstract: We present an equivariant K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras of type C with three parameters by taking advantage of Kato's exotic framework. This enables the derivation of an equivariant K-theoretic realization of affine iquantum groups of type AIII with three parameters. Additionally, in Appendix A, we provide an equivariant K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras of types B/C/F/G with two parameters, following Antor's recent work on affine Hecke algebras with two parameters.

papers.title: A note on uniform finiteness in weakly o-minimal expansions of groups
papers.abstract: For an $\aleph_0$-saturated weakly o-minimal expansion of an ordered group $\mathcal{M}$, it is shown that $\mathcal{M}^{\text{eq}}$ has uniform finiteness if and only if the collection of definable convex subgroups of $\mathcal{M}$ has uniform finiteness. If $\mathcal{M}$ expands an ordered field, then considering definable convex valuation subrings is sufficient. The results use a criterion of Johnson for uniform finiteness in $\mathcal{M}^{\text{eq}}$, [8]. In addition, it is shown that uniform finiteness in $\mathcal{M}^{\text{eq}}$ may fail for weakly o-minimal expansions of fields.

papers.title: Bellman-sufficient Information Complexity
papers.abstract: We introduce Bellman-sufficient information complexity for minimax analysis of sequential decision problems. A Bellman-sufficient state retains the history needed for the controlled recursion; an index $Y=χ(Ω)$ specifies which information the bounds charge. A log-penalized Bellman program gives the upper bound, and a Bellman--Fano comparison with an algorithm-dependent reference trajectory gives the lower bound. When admissibility, calibration, and growth conditions hold and the bounds match at a common localization scale, they yield an information-risk sandwich. UCB bounds the immediate decision loss through calibration and optimism, while AMS/EBO gives a robust relaxation of the AIR Bellman program. Our main application gives a negative answer to a widely studied form of the GP--UCB minimax-optimality question. For every $0<α<1/4$, we construct a fixed bounded continuous kernel with minimax regret $Θ(T^{1-α})$ along an infinite sequence of horizons. At those horizons, two globally calibrated GP--UCB rules incur linear regret under one fixed truth. A policy that applies action-index AMS to a predetermined finite set in each epoch attains the minimax order; EBO gives a dual interpretation. Many low-value directions inflate the global exploration multiplier even though ignoring them is inexpensive. Through the canonical RKHS feature map, the same construction gives a finite-horizon polynomial minimax gap for the specified maximal-information-calibrated LinUCB rule. A numerical experiment illustrates the mechanism.

papers.title: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
papers.abstract: We establish a unified operator-theoretic framework for understanding the results on the Weil quadratic form obtained by Yoshida (1992), Bombieri (2001, 2003), Connes--Consani (2023), and Connes--Consani--Moscovici (2025+) from the perspective of the screw function introduced in Suzuki (2023). An advantage of the approach via the screw function is that it provides a method to study the Weil quadratic form, which is originally defined in terms of distributions, by means of continuous functions and brings the theory of de Branges spaces into the analysis of the Weil quadratic form via the Fourier transform. Based on this framework, we formulate a conjecture stating that a self-adjoint operator whose eigenvalues are the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be obtained as the limit, as $a \to \infty$, of self-adjoint operators arising from nonlocal realizations of the first-order differential operator on the finite interval $[-a,a]$. All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis. This conjecture may be compared with the limit formula for the Riemann zeta function expressed in terms of zeta-regularized products proposed by Connes, Consani, and Moscovici, and it sheds new light on the spectral-theoretic interpretation of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: LEAF: A Learning-Enabled ADMM Framework for Accelerated Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose LEAF, a learning-enabled ADMM framework for accelerated convex optimization. The key idea is to approximate the Moreau envelope of the objective function using an Input Convex Neural Network (ICNN), resulting in a learned model that preserves convexity and smoothness. This leads to the proposed Moreau Envelope Learning ADMM (MEL-ADMM) and its splitting variant sMEL-ADMM. Unlike existing approaches that learn high-dimensional operators directly, LEAF learns a scalar-valued Moreau envelope, significantly reducing model complexity and improving data efficiency. The framework accommodates a broad class of convex problems with smooth and non-smooth objectives. By embedding convexity explicitly through the ICNN architecture, the proposed approach maintains high approximation accuracy while preserving key structural properties of the optimization problem. Both MEL-ADMM and sMEL-ADMM are developed with theoretical guarantees of convergence and feasibility under the learned model. Rigorous analysis shows that the proposed methods achieve convergence rates comparable to classical ADMM while reducing per-iteration computational cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate up to an order-of-magnitude speedup over state-of-the-art solvers while maintaining low optimality gaps

papers.title: New Codes from Cyclic and Negacyclic Codes of Even Length over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
papers.abstract: This paper uses theoretical results previously established in the literature to design search algorithms to find new linear codes over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ from cyclic and negacyclic codes of even length. As a result of these searches, we have found 2500 new cyclic codes and 730 negacyclic codes. These new codes exhibit improved parameters compared to previously known codes. Additionally, we have obtained binary quantum codes with good parameters from such $\mathbb{Z}_4$ codes.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis of the Finite Transposition Method for Backward Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a finite transposition method for the numerical approximation of backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs). Starting from the transposition formulation of BSDEs, we construct appropriate finite-dimensional transposition spaces and establish the existence and uniqueness of the corresponding finite transposition solutions. We prove the convergence of the proposed method under standard assumptions and derive convergence rates under additional Malliavin regularity assumptions. The proposed approach provides a variational approximation framework for BSDEs and may be viewed as a stochastic counterpart of the classical finite element method for partial differential equations. In addition, the conditional expectations arising in the resulting scheme can be evaluated explicitly, thereby facilitating its numerical implementation.

papers.title: Existence of ACM Bundles on Polarized Abelian Varieties
papers.abstract: We study arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay bundles on polarized abelian varieties of dimension at least two. We construct explicit indecomposable families in every rank, compute their cohomology, and establish wild representation type via the Fourier--Mukai correspondence. We also obtain slope-stable ACM bundles from simple semihomogeneous bundles, with ranks determined by the polarization type and rational slope.

papers.title: Filtering out Erratic Observables: Wormholes from Gauging Nonlocal Symmetries
papers.abstract: The wormhole contribution to the gravitational path integral may be interpreted as smooth remnant of correlations among the erratic large-$N$ behaviors of dual CFTs. In this work, we investigate this idea in (2+1)-dimensional gravity. We show that one-sided boundary gravitons are intrinsically incomplete in the sense that the associated observable algebra has a nontrivial center regardless of choices of boundary conditions. Based on asymptotic symmetries, we bootstrap a general Poisson bracket to construct completions of the boundary gravitons. In the simplest completion, the commutant of the boundary graviton observable algebra is given by an observable algebra of monodromy data which we interpret as an effective description of one-sided black holes. We show that, to describe Lorentzian multi-boundary wormholes, only the monodromy data with a positivity restriction is needed. The positivity restriction results in emergent erratic large-$N$ behaviors for some observables. We filter out the erratic observables by restricting to a subspace on which they act trivially. The monodromy observables generate nonlocal symmetries lack of corresponding local currents. We show that gauging the nonlocal symmetries is equivalent to filtering out the erratic observables. For one CFT, gauging the nonlocal symmetries at the quantum level removes all black hole states. Filtering the partition function of CFTs leads to an apparent ensemble averaging. For two CFTs, a Hilbert subspace describing wormholes survives after gauging global part of the nonlocal symmetries. The filtered partition function of the two CFTs is an ensemble average over quantum gates entangling the monodromy degrees of freedom of the two CFTs. The correlation between the erratic observables of the two CFTs is preserved, which contributes to the filtered partition function as a wormhole term.

papers.title: On small-step quarter plane lattice walks with a non D-finite univariate generating function
papers.abstract: We report on the status of the conjecture of Bousquet-Mélou and Mishna that the univariate counting generating function of a small-step quarter-plane lattice model is D-finite if and only if a particular group associated to the walk is finite. While the finite-group case is fully resolved, the infinite-group case remains incomplete. First we survey the known cases. By invoking asymptotics results from probability theory and a case analysis completed by Bostan, Raschel and Salvy (2014), we establish that the generating functions of 14 infinite-group models are not D-finite, and that for an additional 18 models the generating function for walks that end on an axis is not D-finite. We conclude with a discussion of limitations of asymptotic arguments to resolve the remaining cases.

papers.title: Monomial bases and canonical bases for quantum affine algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a monomial basis of a quantum affine algebra of simply-laced type, associated to the PBW basis of Beck-Nakajima. We show that there exists a simple algorithm of computing canonical basis in terms of the monomial basis. We dsicuss the relations of the canonical basis obtained from this PBW basis with Lusztig's canonical basis constructed by using the geometry of quivers.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Tensorial Model Reduction
papers.abstract: This work investigates a two-stage method for constructing projection-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs). Based on established tensorial ROM methodology, the proposed approach reduces dimensionality offline by encoding solution snapshots using a multi-linear Tucker factorization, so that a reduced basis which varies nonlinearly with PDE parameters can be rapidly constructed online and used in a Galerkin ROM. Two novel extensions of this strategy, tailored to the cases of structured PDEs and sparse parameter sampling, are presented: the construction of reduced bases orthonormalized with respect to a general discrete inner product, and the interpolation of encoded states via radial basis functions. Basic representation and ROM error estimates are presented demonstrating the validity of these modifications, and the approach is challenged on state-linear examples where monolithic-basis ROMs are known to struggle, including a realistic instance of Maxwell's equations in 3D. Results suggest that the proposed nonlinear basis ROM can effectively mitigate linear restrictions on Kolmogorov $n$-width while improving upon previous tensorial ROM technology, particularly in the highly nonlinear and data-limited regimes characteristic of practical use cases.

papers.title: On submersions with definite folds of manifolds with boundary into Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: Submersions with definite folds are submersions on manifolds with boundary whose restrictions to the boundary are definite fold maps. In this paper, we study differential-topological properties of manifolds with boundary admitting such maps into Euclidean spaces. When the target is $\mathbb{R}$, we obtain restrictions on the homeomorphism and diffeomorphism types of the source manifolds by using results for $m$-functions. For targets of dimension greater than one, we focus on the cases where the restrictions to the boundary are round fold maps or image simple fold maps, both defined by conditions on the singular value set. Then, we study the diffeomorphism types and Euler characteristics of manifolds admitting such maps. These results have applications to non-singular extensions of definite fold maps.

papers.title: G-birationally rigid cubic threefolds
papers.abstract: We classify pairs $(X,G)$ consisting of a (possibly singular) cubic threefold $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4$ and a finite subgroup $G\subset\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ such that $X$ is $G$-birationally rigid, i.e., $X$ is a $G$-Mori fiber space (over a point), and $X$ is not $G$-birational to any $G$-Mori fibre space that is not $G$-biregular to $X$.

papers.title: A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomena for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary.II
papers.abstract: This is a continuation of the research in [16]. Let $(\overline{M},g_{-1})$ be a closed geodesic $r_0$-ball in the hyperbolic space $(\mathbb{H}^n,g_{-1})$. Let $m\neq1$ be a positive constant. In this paper, we show that for $n\geq3$, starting from the metric $m g_{-1}$ on $\overline{M}$, with certain prescribed non-decreasing rotationally symmetric mean curvature and the fixed conformal class $[g_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}]$ on the boundary $\partial M$, the solution $g(t)$ to the normalized Ricci flow $(1.2)$ which is continuous up to the boundary, exists for all $t>0$, and converges locally uniformly in the interior $M$ of $\overline{M}$ to a complete hyperbolic metric as $t\to\infty$(see Theorem 1.1 for details). Under some additional conditions, we show the same conclusion holds for $n=2$.

papers.title: A Loewner-Nirenberg phenomenon for Ricci flow on compact manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that starting from a geodesic ball $\overline{B_{r_0}}(0)$ in $\mathbb{H}^n$, for $n\geq3$, with prescribed non-decreasing rotationally symmetric mean curvature and the fixed conformal class $[g_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}]$ on the boundary, the solution $g(t)$ to the normalized Ricci flow $(1.2)$ which is continuous up to the boundary, exists for all $t>0$ and converges locally uniformly in $B_{r_0}(0)$ to a complete hyperbolic metric as $t\to\infty$(see Theorem 1.2 for details). Moreover, the sectional curvature of $g(t)$ maintains less than $-1$ for $t>0$.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, which are non-graded counterparts of the Koszul dualities of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: Structural interpretability in SVMs with truncated orthogonal polynomial kernels
papers.abstract: Support vector machines (SVMs) can yield classifiers with similar predictive performance but different internal structures, particularly in the contributions of individual explanatory variables and their interactions. We introduce Orthogonal Representation Contribution Analysis (ORCA), a post-training methodology for SVMs constructed from tensor products of truncated Christoffel--Darboux kernels. The associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) admits a finite orthonormal polynomial basis in which the regularized component of the fitted decision function has an exact expansion. Squared expansion coefficients induce an additive decomposition of its squared RKHS norm. Based on this representation, normalized Orthogonal Kernel Contribution (OKC) indices quantify the fractions of the squared RKHS norm associated with total polynomial degrees, interaction orders, and input-variable contributions, both individually and through interactions of arbitrary order. ORCA summarizes these indices through joint structural maps, variable-specific displays, and comparisons of fitted classifiers. A controlled quartet of classification problems illustrates substantial structural differences under matched predictive performance. A double-spiral experiment compares five Jacobi kernels, while an application to the Vertebral Column data illustrates the method after cross-validated model selection. ORCA provides a quantitative characterization of the internal structure of fitted SVMs, revealing differences that may remain undetected by standard predictive performance metrics.

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.abstract: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

papers.title: LAD estimation of locally stable SDE
papers.abstract: We prove the asymptotic mixed normality of the least absolute deviation (LAD) estimator for a locally $α$-stable stochastic differential equation (SDE) observed at high frequency, where $α\in(0,2)$. We investigate both ergodic and non-ergodic cases, where the terminal sampling time diverges or is fixed, respectively, under different sets of assumptions. The objective function for the LAD estimator is expressed in a fully explicit form without necessitating numerical integration, offering a significant computational advantage over the existing non-Gaussian stable quasi-likelihood approach. We also give illustrative numerical results that support our theoretical finding.

papers.title: The Ferrers bound for spanning trees in bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Ehrenborg's conjecture that every connected bipartite graph $G$ with parts of size $m$ and $n$ has at most $\frac{1}{mn}\prod_{v\in V(G)} \operatorname{deg}(v)$ spanning trees, and that equality holds if and only if $G$ is a Ferrers graph.

papers.title: Every 3-connected $\{K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph of order at least 13 is Hamilton-connected
papers.abstract: A graph is split if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and an independent set. Let $K_{1,4}+e$ denote the graph obtained from $K_{1,4}$ by adding an edge between two leaves. Ryjáček et al. [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 134 (2019), 239--263] conjectured that every $4$-connected graph with minimum degree at least 6 that contains neither $K_{1,4}$ nor $K_{1,4}+e$ as an induced subgraph is Hamiltonian. They proved the conclusion for $5$-connected graphs with the same minimum degree bound. We prove that every $3$-connected split graph of order at least 13 that contains neither of these induced subgraphs is Hamilton-connected. Together with Dirac's theorem, this proves the conjecture of Ryjáček et al. for split graphs.

papers.title: RL unknotter, hard unknots and unknotting number
papers.abstract: We train a reinforcement learning agent to simplify hard unknot diagrams and pair it with a learned crossing selector to search for short unknotting sequences. Three examples found by the agent lead to an infinite family of prime two-bridge knots of unknotting number three whose connected sums with the figure-eight knot also have unknotting number three, and fifteen new unknotting upper bounds were found on the set of prime knots up to 13 crossings.

papers.title: Three heteroclinic orbits induce a countable family of equivalence classes of regular flows
papers.abstract: We solve the problem of topological classification for smooth structurally stable flows on closed four-dimensional manifolds, the non-wandering set of which contains exactly two saddle equilibria, and the wandering set contains isolated trajectories connecting these saddle equilibria (heteroclinic curves). In particular, we show that for a flow of the class under consideration on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, the number of heteroclinic curves is a complete topological invariant, while on the sphere $\mathbb S^4$, there exists a countably many equivalence classes with an arbitrary odd number $γ\geq 3$ of heteroclinic curves. These results contrast with a three-dimensional case, where under similar conditions there exists only finite set of equivalence classes for each number of heteroclinic curves.

papers.title: On the Stability Connection Between Discrete-Time Algorithms and Their Resolution ODEs: Applications to Min-Max Optimisation
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between the stability of discrete-time algorithms (DTAs) and continuous-time dynamical systems, in particular their $O(s^r)$-resolution ordinary differential equations (ODEs). We show that exponential stability of a common equilibrium transfers to the DTA whenever the one-step error is small relative to the distance to the equilibrium and the one-step Lyapunov decay. This condition is sharp in order, and one-step consistency alone is insufficient. The result is local and allows step-size-dependent ODEs and Lyapunov functions, covering $O(s)$-resolution ODEs whose decay rate vanishes as the step size tends to zero. Asymptotic stability is not inherited in general, but a comparison criterion and a checkable compatibility condition ensure it carries over for equilibria and compact sets. For resolution ODEs, joint regularity of the update map guarantees the required error bound. We apply the framework to two-timescale gradient descent ascent (TT-GDA), generalised extragradient, two-timescale proximal point, and (regularised) damped Newton, showing that for small step sizes and suitable parameters, every saddle point with invertible Hessian is locally exponentially stable for all but TT-GDA. For degenerate saddle points, the framework yields asymptotic stability and convergence rates.

papers.title: Functional central limit theorem for superdiffusive SDEs with stable noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a functional stable central limit theorem for a class of superdiffusive solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by an $α$-stable process.

papers.title: Max-Min Bilinear Completely Positive Programs: A Semidefinite Relaxation with Tightness Guarantees
papers.abstract: We study max-min bilinear completely positive (CP) programs and their associated min-max programs. We establish reformulations of these problems as linear optimization over the product of the CP cone and the copositive (COP) cone, namely, the COP-CP programs. A hierarchy of coupled Moment-SOS type semidefinite relaxations is proposed to solve these COP-CP programs. We show that this approach has asymptotic convergence under mild assumptions. Moreover, we use the coupled flat truncation conditions (FTCs) to certify tightness of semidefinite relaxations, and we give sufficient conditions for finite convergence of the hierarchy, under which the FTCs hold at every optimal solution of all sufficiently high-order relaxations. Numerical experiments are presented to show the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title: On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
papers.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed Kähler class $[ω]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal Kähler metric in $[ω]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $Δ$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $Δ$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $Δ$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[ω]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

papers.title: Real-Time Dynamic N-1 Screening: Identifying High-Risk Lines and Transformers After Common Faults
papers.abstract: Power system operators routinely perform N-1 contingency analysis, yet conventional tools provide limited guidance on which lines or transformers deserve heightened attention during fast post-fault transients. In particular, static screening does not reveal whether (1) the same faulted line repeatedly triggers severe downstream overloads, or (2) a specific transformer emerges as vulnerable across many distinct fault scenarios. This paper introduces a real-time dynamic N-1 screening framework that addresses this gap by estimating, for each counterfactual single-phase transmission fault, the probability of transient overcurrent on critical grid elements. The output is an operator-facing dashboard that ranks (a) faulted lines whose outages most frequently lead to dangerous transformer overloads, and (b) transformers that consistently overload across top-risk scenarios, both of which are actionable indicators for real-time situational awareness. The approach models post-fault electromechanical dynamics using a linear stochastic formulation of the swing equations with short-lived, fault-localized uncertainty, and combines analytic transient evaluation with cross-entropy based importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare but high-impact events. All N-1 contingencies are evaluated in parallel with linear computational complexity. The framework is demonstrated on the IEEE 118-bus system, where it reveals latent high-risk lines and transformers that remain invisible under deterministic dynamic or static N-1 analysis. Results show orders-of-magnitude computational speedup relative to brute-force Monte Carlo, enabling practical deployment within real-time operational cycles.

papers.title: Equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials of Thagomizer Matroids with a Hyperoctahedral Group Action
papers.abstract: We compute the equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig and inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of the thagomizer matroid $T_n=M(K_{1,1,n})$ under the action of the hyperoctahedral group $\Bn$. For $n\ge2$, this action identifies $\Bn$ with the full automorphism group of $T_n$. For every $n\ge0$, we give multiplicity-free decompositions of all coefficients of both polynomials into irreducible representations and prove that both coefficient sequences are strongly induced log-concave with respect to induction from $\Bn\times\Bn$ to $\B{2n}$. The formulas for Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials follow from the palindromicity of the equivariant $Z$-polynomial and the known equivariant formulas for the graphic matroids of cycle graphs under the action of $\Sn$. The inverse formula follows from Proudfoot's equivariant inversion identity. For $n\ge2$, we also obtain explicit formulas for both polynomials of $M(K_{2,n})$ under the inherited action of $\Bn$, again with multiplicity-free coefficients.

papers.title: Function-on-function nonlinear autoregressive model (F2NARX) for probabilistic surrogate modeling of stochastic dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally efficient surrogate models for predicting dynamical system responses is critical in many engineering domains, yet remains challenging due to the strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional mapping from external excitations and system parameters to system responses. This work introduces a novel Function-on-Function Nonlinear AutoRegressive model with eXogenous inputs (F2NARX), which reformulates the recently proposed $\mathcal{F}$-NARX method from a function-on-function regression perspective. The proposed framework substantially improves predictive efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. By combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression, F2NARX further enables probabilistic predictions of dynamical responses via the unscented transform in an autoregressive manner. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through case studies of varying complexity. Results show that F2NARX outperforms state-of-the-art NARX model by orders of magnitude in efficiency while achieving higher accuracy in general. The probabilistic prediction capability of F2NARX is further demonstrated by combining it with active learning for first-passage probability estimation, showing its potential for reliability-oriented applications.

papers.title: Log canonical thresholds at infinity
papers.abstract: The paper considers a global version of the notion of log canonical threshold for plurisubharmonic functions $u$ of logarithmic growth in $\mathbb{C}^n$, aiming at description of the range of all $p>0$ such that $e^{-u}\in L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$. Explicit formulas are obtained in the toric case. By considering Bergman functions of corresponding weighted Hilbert spaces, a new polynomial approximation of plurisubharmonic functions of logarithmic growth with control over its singularities and behavior at infinity (a global version of Demailly's approximation theorem) is established. Some application to tame polynomial maps are given.

papers.title: Elementary Quantum Gates from Lie Group Embeddings in $U(2^n)$: Spectral Geometry and Intrinsic Factorization Lengths
papers.abstract: We study intrinsic factorizations of quantum gates using determinant-one unitaries supported on arbitrary two-dimensional subspaces of $\C^N$, where $N=2^n$. For $U\in U(N)$ write $r=\operatorname{rank}(U-I)$. When $r\ge2$, we characterize all factors that lower the active rank by two through traceless compressions of the Cayley transform on $\Ran(U-I)$. For the ordered active eigenangles $\vartheta_j\in(0,2π)$, existence is equivalent to $\vartheta_1+\vartheta_2\le2π\le\vartheta_{r-1}+\vartheta_r$. For $U\in SU(N)$, combining this construction with eigenangle merging realizes the classical reflection-length formula in two-level form: $\ell^{SU}(U)=\max\{ν(U),r-ν(U)\}$, where $ν(U)$ is the positive eigenangle sum divided by $2π$. On the full-rank open set, the age indexes $N-1$ connected components with constant intrinsic length. We place these factorizations within the spectral description of the dictionaries formed by faithful $SU(2)$ and $U(2)$ embeddings. For $n\ge2$, these dictionaries are Haar-null of Hausdorff dimensions $N^2-N+1$ and $N^2-N+2$; the former is compact and the latter dense. Distances to compact sectors reduce to eigenvalue matching. Further results concern ambient minimality of embedded geodesics and a first-order sharp spectral bound on coherence production.

papers.title: Mutually c-Conjugate Potentials in Multimarginal Optimal Transport: Dual Representation and Stability
papers.abstract: We establish dual representation and stability results for multimarginal optimal transport (MOT) with bounded continuous costs. Our approach uses mutually $c$-conjugate potentials: each component is the largest function compatible with the dual constraint when the others are fixed. A single sweep of successive component updates produces such a family from any real-valued feasible family while preserving contact points. The resulting potentials are bounded and upper semicontinuous. On fixed compact metric spaces, normalization at fixed reference points yields a compact class of continuous potentials in the product uniform norm. This class is independent of the marginals and contains a dual maximizer for every marginal tuple. We prove its Lipschitz dependence on the cost in Hausdorff distance. Under uniform cost convergence and weak marginal convergence, transport values converge. The corresponding normalized optimizer sets are upper stable in the product uniform norm, without uniqueness assumptions. We also obtain value bounds in total variation and, for coordinatewise Lipschitz costs, Wasserstein distance. For coordinatewise Lipschitz reference costs, a power-growth condition on the dual objective gives one-sided Hölder estimates for optimizer sets under joint perturbations. On finite spaces, polyhedral structure yields linear growth and one-sided Lipschitz estimates with reference-dependent constants. On Polish spaces, total boundedness of the coordinate cost profiles in the uniform norm yields a compact normalized representation. For a fixed cost satisfying this condition, value continuity and upper stability of normalized conjugate optimizer sets hold under weak marginal convergence.

papers.title: Domino tilings of black-and-white Temperleyan cylinders
papers.abstract: We consider the dimer model in cylindrical domains $Ω_δ$ on square grids of mesh size $δ$ with two Temperleyan boundary components of different colors. Assuming that the $Ω_δ$ approximate a cylindrical domain $Ω$ as $δ\to 0$, we prove the convergence of height fluctuations to the Gaussian Free Field in $Ω$ plus an independent discrete Gaussian multiple of the harmonic measure of one of the boundary components. The limit of the dimer coupling functions on $Ω_δ$ is holomorphic in $Ω$ but not conformally covariant. Given this, we determine the limiting structure of height fluctuations from general principles rather than from explicit computations. In particular, our analysis justifies the inevitable appearance of the discrete Gaussian distribution in the doubly connected setup.

papers.title: Differential calculus on bigraded spaces and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: Koszul duality for superalgebras involves both the intrinsic super parity and the degree shift introduced by suspension. We study this duality while keeping the two gradings separate, using a $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z$-graded refinement of the commutativity convention of Deligne and Morgan. In this setting, the Koszul suspension preserves the parity degree and raises the independent weight by one. We realize the polynomial superalgebr $\mathcal O(k^{m|n})$ and its Koszul dual as function algebras on bigraded spaces and construct an isomorphism between their differential calculi of polyvector fields and mixed differential forms. For admissible quadratic Poisson structures, whose bivectors have bidegree $(0,2)$, this isomorphism descends to the differential calculi on Poisson cohomology and mixed Poisson homology. With respect to the corresponding mixed volume forms, Koszul duality preserves unimodularity and, in the unimodular case, identifies the induced Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structures on Poisson cohomology.

papers.title: Correcting quantum errors one gradient step at a time
papers.abstract: Probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) lets a recovery fail with some probability, in exchange for higher fidelity when it succeeds. Prior PAQEC code searches keep the codewords orthonormal with penalty terms and tune the code without its best recovery. We propose a gradient method with three new parts. First, the codewords move on the complex Stiefel manifold, so they are orthonormal at every step without penalties. Second, every code is trained against its best recovery, which we solve for at each step rather than learn. Third, a fast Petz recovery that we can differentiate even for symmetric codes gets the search close, and the exact semidefinite program finishes it. We train a single five-qubit code over generalized amplitude damping noise. At weak noise ($γ= 0.1$, $p = 0.05$) and equal success probability, it has $23$ times lower infidelity than the permutation-invariant code of prior work, and $9$ times lower than that work's numerically optimized code. At equal fidelity it succeeds $91\%$ of the time, against $76\%$ for the permutation-invariant code.

papers.title: On the future cover of a sofic shift
papers.abstract: The paper contains a new proof of the theorem by Krieger which establishes the canonicity of the future cover of a sofic shift. In addition the paper describes a method to produce new canonical covers from a given one, resulting in canonical covers related to, but generally different from the future cover.

papers.title: Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
papers.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

papers.title: Quadratic Mean-Field BSDEs and Exponential Utility Maximization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of real-valued mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with generators of quadratic growth in the control variable and the mean-field term. For bounded terminal conditions satisfying suitable structural regularity, we establish existence and uniqueness under two complementary quadratic regimes; the uniformly continuous path-dependent case additionally requires a uniform quadratic bound on the normalized generator. Our approach for these results combines Malliavin calculus with refined BMO and stability estimates, and bridges the gap between the quadratic BSDE results of [Ann. Probab. 45 (2017), pp. 3795--3828] and [Ann. Appl. Probab. 35 (2025), pp. 2128--2174]. Motivated by a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, we further extend our framework to terminal conditions without imposing continuity or Markovian structure on the terminal condition. Under a suitable smallness condition on the oscillation of the terminal value around its mean, the associated quadratic BSDE admits a unique solution in a suitable small solution class. We then apply the extended theory to solve a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, thereby extending the constrained exponential utility framework of Hu et al. [Ann. Appl. Probab. 15 (2005), pp. 1691--1712] to a mean-field setting.

papers.title: A General Theorem for Non-Simultaneous Hat Guessing Puzzles
papers.abstract: The prisoners and hats puzzle, or simply the hat puzzle, is a family of games in which a group of prisoners are each assigned a colored hat and are asked to guess the color of their own hat. Various versions of the puzzle arise depending on the number of prisoners, the number of possible hat colors, and the information available to them before and after the game begins. These puzzles are broadly classified according to whether the prisoners' declarations are made simultaneously or non-simultaneously. In this paper we present a general theorem concerning the existence of a winning strategy when the declarations are non-simultaneous. We also discuss the relationship between the construction of such strategies and the Axiom of Choice, as well as their connection to the simultaneous-declaration case.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Difference Equation and Affine Laumon Space III: Generalization to $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$
papers.abstract: In a series of papers, we have considered a non-stationary difference equation which was originally discovered for the deformed Virasoro conformal block. The equation involves mass parameters and, when they are tuned appropriately, the equation is regarded as a quantum KZ equation for $U_q\bigl(A_{1}^{(1)}\bigr)$. We introduce a $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ generalization of the non-stationary difference equation. The Hamiltonian is expressed in terms of $q$-commuting variables and allows both factorized forms and a normal ordered form. By specializing the mass parameters appropriately, the Hamiltonian can be identified with the $R$-matrix of the symmetric tensor representation of $U_q\bigl(A_{N-1}^{(1)}\bigr)$, which in turn comes from the 3D (tetrahedron) $R$-matrix. We conjecture that the affine Laumon partition function of type $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ gives a solution to our $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary difference equation. As a check of our conjecture, we work out the four-dimensional limit and find that the non-stationary difference equation reduces to the Fuji-Suzuki-Tsuda system.

papers.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
papers.abstract: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
papers.abstract: Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $ν\neqκ$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally. Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

papers.title: Test-Time Search in Neural Graph Coarsening Procedures for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
papers.abstract: The identification of valid inequalities, such as the rounded capacity inequalities (RCIs), is a key component of cutting plane methods for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP). While a deep learning-based separation method can learn to find high-quality cuts, our analysis reveals that the model produces fewer cuts than expected because it is insufficiently sensitive to generate a diverse set of generated subsets. This paper proposes an alternative: enhancing the performance of a trained model at inference time through a new test-time search with stochasticity. First, we introduce stochastic edge selection into the graph coarsening procedure, replacing the previously proposed greedy approach. Second, we propose the Graph Coarsening History-based Partitioning (GraphCHiP) algorithm, which leverages coarsening history to identify not only RCIs but also, for the first time, the Framed capacity inequalities (FCIs). Experiments on randomly generated CVRP instances demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in reducing the dual gap compared to the existing neural separation method. Additionally, our method discovers effective FCIs on a specific instance, despite the challenging nature of identifying such cuts.

papers.title: Linking numbers and triple linking numbers for periodic tangles
papers.abstract: Periodic tangles are 1-dimensional submanifolds in the 3-space with translational symmetry. In this paper, we define the linking numbers for singly, doubly, and triply periodic tangles using appropriate motifs and show that they are well-defined and invariant under link-homotopy. Furthermore, we extend the notion to the triple linking numbers for singly, doubly, and triply periodic tangles, and the higher order linking numbers for singly periodic tangles under certain assumptions.

papers.title: Adaptive direct search for blackbox optimization
papers.abstract: Two families of directional direct search methods have emerged in derivative-free and blackbox optimization (DFO and BBO), each based on distinct principles: Mesh Adaptive Direct Search (MADS) and Sufficient Decrease Direct Search (SDDS). MADS restricts trial points to a mesh and accepts any improvement, ensuring that none are missed, but at the cost of restricting the placement of trial points. SDDS allows greater freedom by evaluating points anywhere in the space, but accepts only those yielding a sufficient decrease in the objective function value, which may lead to discarding promising points. This work introduces a new class of methods, Adaptive Direct Search (ADS), which uses a novel acceptance rule based on the so-called punctured space, avoiding both mesh and sufficient decrease conditions. ADS enables flexible search while addressing the limitations of MADS and SDDS, and retains the theoretical foundations of directional direct search. Computational results in constrained and unconstrained settings highlight its performance compared to both MADS and SDDS.

papers.title: SDP bounds on the stability number via ADMM and intermediate levels of the Lasserre hierarchy
papers.abstract: We consider the Lasserre hierarchy for computing bounds on the stability number of graphs. The semidefinite programs (SDPs) arising from this hierarchy involve large matrix variables and many linear constraints, which makes them difficult to solve using interior-point methods. We propose solving these SDPs using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). When the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy for a given graph is intractable for the ADMM, we consider an intermediate-level relaxation of the hierarchy. To warm-start the ADMM, we use an optimal solution from the first level of the Lasserre hierarchy, which is equivalent to the well-known Lovász theta function. Additionally, we use this solution to determine which degree two monomials to add in the Lasserre hierarchy relaxation to obtain an intermediate level between 1 and 2. Computational results demonstrate that our approach yields strong bounds on the stability number, which are computable within reasonable running times. We provide {improved} bounds on the stability number of various graphs from the literature.

papers.title: Cardinalities of Ultraproducts of Finite Sets in ZF + DC
papers.abstract: Relative to an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent with ZF + DC that there exists an ultrafilter $U$ on $ω$ such that two infinite ultraproducts of finite sets, $\prod A_n / U$ and $\prod B_n / U$, have the same cardinality if and only if $0 < \lim_U |A_n|/|B_n| < \infty$. In particular, this holds in $W[U]$, where $W$ is the Solovay Model and $U$ is $[ω]^ω$-generic.

papers.title: Rectifying Conformity Scores for Better Conditional Coverage
papers.abstract: We present a new method for generating confidence sets within the split conformal prediction framework. Our method performs a trainable transformation of any given conformity score to improve conditional coverage while ensuring exact marginal coverage. The transformation is based on an estimate of the conditional quantile of conformity scores. The resulting method is particularly beneficial for constructing adaptive confidence sets in multi-output problems where standard conformal quantile regression approaches have limited applicability. We develop a theoretical bound that captures the influence of the accuracy of the quantile estimate on the approximate conditional validity, unlike classical bounds for conformal prediction methods that only offer marginal coverage. We experimentally show that our method is highly adaptive to the local data structure and outperforms existing methods in terms of conditional coverage, improving the reliability of statistical inference in various applications.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: Light Edge Fault Tolerant Graph Spanners
papers.abstract: There has recently been significant interest in fault tolerant spanners, which are spanners that still maintain their stretch guarantees after some nodes or edges fail. This work has culminated in an almost complete understanding of the three-way tradeoff between stretch, sparsity, and number of faults tolerated. However, despite some progress in metric settings, there have been no results to date on the tradeoff in general graphs between stretch, lightness, and number of faults tolerated. We initiate the study of light edge fault tolerant (EFT) graph spanners, obtaining the first such results. First, we observe that lightness can be unbounded if we use the traditional definition (normalizing by the MST). We then argue that a natural definition of fault-tolerant lightness is to instead normalize by a min-weight fault tolerant connectivity preserver; essentially, a fault-tolerant version of the MST. However, even with this, we show that it is still not generally possible to construct $f$-EFT spanners whose weight compares reasonably to the weight of a min-weight $f$-EFT connectivity preserver. In light of this lower bound, it is natural to then consider bicriteria notions of lightness, where we compare the weight of an $f$-EFT spanner to a min-weight $(f' > f)$-EFT connectivity preserver. The most interesting question is to determine the minimum value of $f'$ that allows for reasonable lightness upper bounds. Our main result is a precise answer to this question: $f' = 2f$. In particular, we show that the lightness can be untenably large (roughly $n/k$ for a $k$-spanner) if one normalizes by the min-weight $(2f-1)$-EFT connectivity preserver. But if one normalizes by the min-weight $2f$-EFT connectivity preserver, then we show that the lightness is bounded by just $O(f^{1/2})$ times the non-fault tolerant lightness (roughly $n^{1/k}$, for a $(1+ε)(2k-1)$-spanner).

papers.title: The infinitesimal subgroup of interpretable groups in some dp-minimal valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue our local analysis of groups interpretable in various dp-minimal valued fields, as introduced in [8]. We associate with every infinite group $G$ interpretable in those fields an infinite type-definable infinitesimal subgroup $ν(G)$, generated by the four infinitesimal subgroups $ν_D(G)$ associated with the distinguished sorts $K$, $\textbf{k}$, $Γ$ and $K/\mathcal{O}$. To show that $ν(G)$ is type-definable, we show that the resulting subgroups $ν_D(G)$ commute with each other as $D$ ranges over the four distinguished sorts. We then study the basic properties of $ν(G)$. Among others, we show that $ν(G_1\times G_2)=ν(G_1)\times ν(G_2)$ and that if $G_1\le G$ is a definable subgroup then $ν(G_1)$ is relatively definable in $ν(G)$. We also discuss possible connections between $\mathrm{dp\text{-}rk}(ν(G))$ and elimination of imaginaries.

papers.title: A generalized Schmidt's subspace theorem for algebraic points of bounded degree
papers.abstract: Schmidt's subspace theorem in terms of Seshadri constants for closed subschemes in subgeneral position has already been richly developed. Building upon this framework, we establish a Schmidt subspace theorem for algebraic points of bounded degree with respect to numerically equivalent ample divisors, attaining the optimal factor known to date and deriving a generalized weighted version. Also, we settle a long-standing conjecture in this field.

papers.title: $δ$-Poisson and transposed $δ$-Poisson algebras
papers.abstract: We study two new classes of Poisson-type algebras, namely, $δ$-Poisson and transposed $δ$-Poisson algebras. We show that these algebras are related to many interesting identities; in particular, they are related to shift associative algebras, $F$-manifold algebras, algebras of Jordan brackets, etc. We classify simple $δ$-Poisson and transposed $δ$-Poisson algebras and find their depolarizations. We study the Koszulity and self-duality of the $δ$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson operads. Bases of the free $δ$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson algebras generated by a countable set $X$ are constructed.

papers.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
papers.abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.

papers.title: ARMAr-LASSO: Mitigating the Impact of Predictor Serial Correlation on the LASSO
papers.abstract: We explore estimation and prediction accuracy for sparse linear models, focusing on scenarios where both predictors and errors carry serial correlations. We establish a clear link between predictor serial correlation and the performance of the LASSO, showing that even orthogonal or weakly correlated stationary AR processes can lead to significant spurious correlations due to their serial correlations. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach named ARMAr-LASSO (ARMA residuals LASSO), which applies the LASSO to predictors that have been pre-whitened with ARMA filters and lags of dependent variable. We establish oracle inequalities for the feasible estimator and assess its estimation, selection, and forecasting performance empirically. Our findings are supported by extensive simulations and an application to real-world macroeconomic data, which highlight the superior performance of the ARMAr-LASSO for handling sparse linear models in the context of time series.

papers.title: Shift associative algebras
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of algebras satisfying the identity $(xy)z=y(zx),$ named as shift associative algebras. Our research shows that these algebras are related to many interesting identities. In particular, they are related to anti-Poisson-Jordan algebras and algebras of associative type $σ$. We study algebras of associative type $σ$ to be Koszul and self-dual. A basis of the free shift associative algebra generated by a countable set $X$ was constructed. An analog of Wedderburn-Artin's theorem was established. The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $4$-dimensional shift associative algebras are given. In particular, we proved that the first non-associative shift associative algebra appears only in dimension $5$.

papers.title: Asymptotics of a Gauss hypergeometric function related to moments of symmetric square L-functions I
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for a special case of the Gauss hypergeometric function, which arises in the explicit formula for the second moment of Maass form symmetric-square $L$-functions.

papers.title: On proving an Inequality of Ramanujan using Explicit Order Estimates for the Mertens Function
papers.abstract: We intend to prove unconditionally that the Ramanujan's Inequality, \begin{align*} π(x)^2<\frac{ex}{\log x}π(x/e) \end{align*} for every real $x\geq e^{490}$, where $π(x)$ counts the primes up to $x$. We try to obtain an order estimate for $ψ(x)-x$ explicitly based on a point-wise power bound on the Mertens function $M(x)$, where $ψ$ is the second Chebyshev function. An asymmetric hyperbola decomposition of the logarithmically weighted Mertens sum and partial summation give an exact cancellation at the split point. Using the zero-free half-plane, $\Re (s)>7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function, we prove $|M(t)|\leq12000\,t^{213/235}$ for $t\geq e^{131}$ by averaged Perron inversion. The resulting bounds for $ψ$ and the prime counting function $π$ gives us our desired result. A separate argument using a classical zero-free region proves the asymptotic inequality.

papers.title: Harary's Sum and Integral Sum Graphs -- A Survey in detail
papers.abstract: Harary introduced the concepts of sum and integral sum graphs. A graph $G$ is a {\em sum graph} if the vertices of $G$ can be labeled with distinct positive integers so that $e = uv$ is an edge of $G$ if and only if the sum of the labels on vertices $u$ and $v$ is also a label in $G$. An {\em integral sum graph} is also defined just as sum graph, the difference being that the labels may be any distinct integers. This survey presents results obtained by different authors, in detail, on sum and integral sum graphs.

papers.title: Finding pure Nash equilibria in large random games
papers.abstract: Best Response Dynamics (BRD) constitute a family of strategy update rules designed to identify Pure Nash Equilibria (PNEs) in strategic games. In each iteration, a player is selected uniformly at random and adopts a best response strategy, maximising their payoff given the current strategies of the other players. If no improvement is possible for the selected player, another is chosen. The process terminates upon reaching a state where no player wishes to deviate, corresponding to a PNE. However, convergence is not guaranteed as either PNEs may not exist, or the dynamics may become confined within substructures of the game, which we call traps, that admit no PNEs. We investigate this behaviour in the context of random games with $N$ players, each choosing between two actions and receiving independently and identically distributed payoffs. The payoff distribution is permitted to have atoms, allowing for the possibility of ties. The induced dynamics define a class of random walks on the $N$-dimensional hypercube, where the landscape includes two types of absorbing sets: PNEs and traps. Our analysis encompasses BRD, simple random walks, and a broad class of nearest-neighbour processes. We prove that, with high probability, these dynamics reach a PNE before encountering any trap. Our results complete and generalise the ones by Amiet, Collevecchio, Scarsini and Zhong (2021), using a different approach.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: On Elliptical and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions, which play a major role when handling covariance matrices. Similarly to multivariate elliptical distributions, these form a large family of covariance distributions, encompassing, \textit{e.g.}, the Wishart or $t$-Wishart ones. Our first major contribution is to derive a stochastic representation for Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart matrices. This later enables us to obtain various key statistical properties of these distributions such as expectations, variances, and Kronecker moments up to any order. The stochastic representation provides an efficient method for generating random matrices from these distributions. Additionally, Elliptical Wishart distributions have a specific dependence structure - a random scale shared by all columns - which strongly influences their asymptotic behavior. Lastly, the practical relevance of Elliptical Wishart distributions, particularly the $t$-Wishart distribution, is demonstrated through a fitting experiment conducted on real electroencephalographic data. This experiment highlights their effectiveness in accurately modeling real covariance matrices.

papers.title: On Some Infinitary Logics
papers.abstract: We define a new class of infinitary logics $\mathscr L^1_{κ,α}$ generalizing Shelah's logic $\mathbb L^1_κ$ defined in \cite{MR2869022}. If $κ=\beth_κ$ and $α<κ$ is infinite then our logic coincides with $\mathbb L^1_κ$. We study the relation between these logics for different parameters $κ$ and $α$. We give many examples of classes of structures that can or cannot be defined in these logics. Finally, we give a different version of Lindström's Theorem for $\mathbb L^1_κ$ in terms of the $φ$-submodel relation.

papers.title: Ordinals and recursively defined functions on the reals
papers.abstract: We determine sufficient conditions under which certain recursively defined functions are well defined for all real inputs. Given a function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, call a decreasing sequence $x_1>x_2>x_3>\cdots$ "$f$-bad" if $f(x_1)>f(x_2)>f(x_3)>\cdots$, and call the function $f$ "ordinal decreasing" if there exist no infinite $f$-bad sequences. We prove the following result: Given ordinal decreasing functions $f,g_1,\ldots,g_k,s$ that are everywhere larger than $0$, define the recursive algorithm "$M(x)$: if $x<0$ return $f(x)$, else return $g_1(-M(x-g_2(-M(x-\cdots-g_k(-M(x-s(x)))\cdots))))$". Then $M(x)$ halts and is ordinal decreasing for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. The recursive algorithms $M$ and $M_n$ previously studied in the context of fusible numbers by Ericskon et al. (2022) and Bufetov et al. (2024), respectively, are special cases of this scheme. Moreover, given an ordinal decreasing function $f$, denote by $o(f)$ the ordinal height of the root of the tree of $f$-bad sequences. Then we prove that, for $k\ge 2$, the function $M(x)$ defined by the above algorithm satisfies $o(M)\le\varphi_{k-1}(γ+o(s)+1)$, where $γ$ is the smallest ordinal such that $\max\{o(s),o(f),o(g_1), \ldots, o(g_k)\} <\varphi_{k-1}(γ)$.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on solvable and perfect Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We described all transposed Poisson algebra structures on oscillator Lie algebras, i.e., on one-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; on solvable Lie algebras with naturally graded filiform nilpotent radical; on $(n+1)$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; and on $n$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $n$-dimensional algebra with trivial multiplication. We also answered one question on transposed Poisson algebras, posted in a paper by Beites, Ferreira and Kaygorodov. Namely, we found that the semidirect product of ${\mathfrak sl}_2$ and an irreducible module gives a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with non-trivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations, but without non-trivial transposed Poisson structures.

papers.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{τ_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $τ_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

papers.title: Discrete and Continuous Concentration of Measure: Geometric Obstructions, Predictive Gowdy Evolution, and Observable Limits
papers.abstract: We compare concentration in increasing dimension with geometric and metric--measure degeneration of compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. For vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy developments we establish an exact law for redistribution of normalized spatial volume, without imposing polarization. An explicit strict bound on the \emph{initial} spatially averaged wave-map energy guarantees divergence of the transverse circle length $L(τ)$. Under this expansion hypothesis, we classify \emph{all convergent distance-scaling regimes}: if $a_τL(τ)\to\ell$, the rescaled sections concentrate to a point for $\ell=0$, to the uniformly measured circle of circumference $\ell$ for $0<\ell<\infty$, while for $\ell=\infty$ their associated pyramids converge to the maximal pyramid. The classification applies to Ringström's generic non-polarized class, including nondegenerate true spikes, and requires no uniform geometric control at spike points. The argument compares orbit metrics with their initial values outside an exceptional set of probability at most $L(τ_0)/L(τ)$. The normalized Laplacian splits into periodic one-dimensional Schrödinger operators indexed by toroidal Fourier modes; its non-invariant sectors satisfy a uniform spectral gap $Λ_τ\ge cL(τ)^2$. Thus only torus-invariant modes persist at bounded spectral energy, with quantitative heat-semigroup and resolvent estimates. Separately, an initial-data perturbation criterion yields strictly monotone transfer toward a prescribed region in a relatively open low-velocity non-polarized class. Explicit high-velocity solutions exhibit contrasting point-collapse and unbounded-diameter geometries governed by the torus marking.

papers.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.

papers.title: The Brauer-Manin obstruction on algebraic stacks
papers.abstract: For algebraic stacks over number fields, we define their Brauer-Manin sets, Brauer-Manin pairings, and extend the descent theory of Colliot-Thélène and Sansuc. By extending Sansuc's exact sequence, we show the torsionness of Brauer groups of stacks that are locally quotients of varieties by linear groups. With mild assumptions, for stacks that are locally quotients or Deligne-Mumford, we show that the Brauer-Manin obstruction coincides with some other cohomological obstructions such as obstructions given by torsors under connected groups or abelian gerbes. For Brauer-Manin sets of these stacks, we show the properties such as descent along a torsor, product preservation are still correct. These results extend classical theories of those on varieties.

papers.title: Selective Inference for Survey-Weighted Generalized Linear Models: Growing Dimension and Average Marginal Effects
papers.abstract: This paper extends the $\ell_1$-penalized likelihood Selective Inference method to survey settings. We establish its asymptotic validity for generalized linear models with an increasing number of covariates and survey weights, allowing inference on pseudo-true parameters of possibly misspecified selected models. Moreover, we generalize the method to facilitate inference on nonlinear functionals, such as the average marginal effect in survey-weighted logit models. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated using simulated data and the 2020 Canadian Internet Use Survey.

papers.title: Lower bounds on the measure of the support of positive and negative parts of trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: The measure of the positivity set $\{ x \in [0; 2π] \mid f(x) > 0 \}$ of a trigonometric polynomial $f$ is bounded from below by the Motzkin density.
