We generalize the bound to polynomials in several variables and almost periodic functions. We then use these generalizations to extend known results on Taikov's problem.

papers.title: A Chebotarev Density Theorem over Local Fields
papers.abstract: We compute the $p$-adic densities of points with a given splitting type along a (generically) finite map, analogous to the classical Chebotarev theorem over number fields and function fields. Under some mild hypotheses, we prove that these densities satisfy a functional equation in the size of the residue field. This functional equation is a direct reflection of Poincaré duality in étale cohomology. As a consequence, we prove a conjecture of Bhargava, Cremona, Fisher, and Gajović on factorization densities of p-adic polynomials. The key tool is the notion of admissible pairs associated to a group, which we use as an invariant of the inertia and decomposition action of a local field on the fibers of the finite map. We compute the splitting densities by Möbius inverting certain p-adic integrals along the poset of admissible pairs. The conjecture on factorization densities follows immediately for tamely ramified primes from our general results. We reduce the complete conjecture to the existence of an explicit "Tate-type" resolution of the "resultant locus" over the integers and complete the proof of the conjecture by constructing this resolution.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on Galilean and solvable Lie algebras
papers.abstract: Transposed Poisson structures on complex Galilean-type Lie algebras and superalgebras are described. It is proven that the principal Galilean Lie algebras and superalgebras do not admit nontrivial transposed Poisson structures. We also prove that each complex finite-dimensional solvable Lie algebra of dimension greater than one admits a nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivation and a nontrivial ${\rm Hom}$-Lie structure, and that each complex finite-dimensional non-abelian solvable Lie algebra admits a nontrivial transposed Poisson structure.

papers.title: The Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures
papers.abstract: This paper surveys known results in the theory of transposed Poisson algebras and establishes some new results on this subject. A list of open questions for future research is also given, together with notes on the questions that have been answered.

papers.title: $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras
papers.abstract: A relation between $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras has been established. Some non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a certain Lie algebra (Witt algebra, the algebra $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$, the thin Lie algebra and a solvable Lie algebra with abelian nilpotent radical) have been done. In particular, we have developed an example of the transposed Poisson algebra with associative and Lie parts isomorphic to the Laurent polynomials and the Witt algebra. On the other side, it has been proved that there are no non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a Lie algebra part isomorphic to a semisimple finite-dimensional algebra, a simple finite-dimensional superalgebra, the Virasoro algebra, $N=1$ and $N=2$ superconformal algebras, or a semisimple finite-dimensional $n$-Lie algebra.

papers.title: Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles
papers.abstract: We prove global Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles, combining arguments from M.Ikawa (1982,1988) with more recent ones inspired by N.Burq, C.Guillarmou, and A. Hassell (2010) and O. Ivanovici (2010). This is to be contrasted with the loss in the smoothing estimate for the Schrödinger equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in the presence of a trapped geodesic.

papers.title: Archimedes' Angle Measure and The Fundamental Theorem of Trigonometry
papers.abstract: We aim to understand a distant conversation about a trigonometric principle. Although foundational to calculus, this principle and the basic concept of angle measure are often treated tacitly in both elementary and advanced accounts. The primordial idea of counting rotations makes one aware of the integers. In the same vein, Archimedes' measure of partial rotations hints at the completeness of the real numbers. By a less well-known implication, these ideas also lead to the complex numbers and to the Fundamental Theorem of Trigonometry. What does it all mean? And is it true?

papers.title: Conjugate Power Series of Ultralogarithm Branches
papers.abstract: We investigate multivalued solutions of the transcendental ultralogarithm equation $e^{aw} = 1 + a x e^{bw}$ for arbitrary real parameters $a > b > 0$. A sector-based conjugation criterion is formulated and rigorously proved, reducing the technical two-dimensional indexing of conjugate master-series expansions inside ($|x| < R$) and outside ($|x| > R$) the disk of convergence to a unified one-dimensional branch index $n \in Z$. For integer exponents, a logarithmic analog of Vieta's theorem is established. Using multi-channel phase hodographs, we analyze branch evolution across integer, fractional, and transcendental incommensurable ($a = π$, $b = e$) exponents. It is demonstrated that logarithmic stratification eliminates branch cuts of fractional powers, ensuring global stability of iterative root refinement near branch points without auxiliary sheet-selection parameters. Finally, using the Sagdeev pseudopotential method in plasma physics, we confirm the continuous preservation of branch numbering in the Lambert $W$ limit and the physical invariance of the indices $n = 0$ (subsonic regime) and $n = -1$ (supersonic regime).

papers.title: MRASLive: An online parameter estimation toolbox for time-dependent PDEs
papers.abstract: We present MRASLive, a toolbox for online parameter identification in time-dependent partial differential equations based on a model reference adaptive system (MRAS). Building on the MRAS proposed by Kaltenbacher and Nguyen (Inverse Problems 37(5) 2021) and its first numerical realization by the authors (Applied Mathematics for Modern Challenges 8 2026), the toolbox is designed for ease of use, utilising the user's weak form specification to prepare the data, the discretized MRAS and its solvers, and to verify the assumptions of MRAS's convergence theory semi-automatically.

papers.title: Taylor coefficients and duality for finite multiple T-values
papers.abstract: We express every normalized finite multiple $T$-value of positive even depth as the coefficient of $u^{p-1}$ in an explicit iterated integral built from $du$ and $du/\sinh u$. An analogous formula for odd-depth $S$-values, combined with reversal, gives a coefficient representation of $T_p(\mathbf{s})$ for every nonempty index $\mathbf{s}$. The coefficients involved are $p$-integral without a restriction on the weight. For indices $(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})$ with $\ell+m$ odd, we obtain an explicit Bernoulli convolution. It yields a prime-by-prime proof of $T_p(\{1\}^{\ell},3,\{1\}^{m})=T_p(\ell+1,1,m+1)$ for odd $\ell$, and the corresponding identity with an $S$-value for even $\ell$, whenever $p\ge5$ and $p>\ell+m+1$. This proves the finite assertion of the first family in Cheng and Zhao's duality conjecture. We also establish uniform depth-two identities, evaluate the boundary cases, and explain the obstruction to the same termwise argument for $(\{1\}^{\ell},4,\{1\}^{m})$.

papers.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. In a smallest counterexample we find a $4$-connected planar part containing four vertices of degree five. Their neighborhoods meet the boundary in at most one vertex. This allows us to apply the planar configurations of Blanché, Bonamy, and Bonichon and to realize the reduced graph as a minor of the original graph.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite plane-to-plane germs
papers.abstract: We show that the bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite holomorphic map germs $(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ admits continuous moduli, already among finitely determined polynomial germs of corank one and degree five. The moduli come from a new invariant of finite germs: for two tangent branches of the critical set whose images are tangent, the limit of the ratio of the norms of the images of nearby points is preserved by bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence. For germs $(F,H)$ with quasihomogeneous components the invariant is computed from the height functions of $F$ and $H$: it is given by the moduli of the values of the height function of the component of lower weighted degree at the roots of a weighted Wronskian. As a first application we obtain a continuous invariant for the germs $(Y^3+3tYX^4+X^6,\,X^N)$, $N\ge7$, built from the Henry--Parusiński family.

papers.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
papers.abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we derive formulas involving finite sums and generating functions. The arguments use images and fibers, homomorphisms between functional digraphs, and isomorphism types of iterates. A common construction decomposes weighted allocations of fibers into trees and cycles, yielding determinant expressions for several generating functions. Colored functional digraphs provide further formulas. As a by-product, for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$, we derive an inclusion--exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$.

papers.title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
papers.abstract: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

papers.title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal. As a further consequence, the Durfee square side length of a uniformly chosen partition of $n$ has the same distribution as $1$ plus a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables.

papers.title: Spectral coincidence and generalized Hua inversion in rings and Banach algebras
papers.abstract: For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inverses with Harte-quasinilpotent remainders, without Noetherianity. This gives input-core coincidence under intertwining. If the central subring is Noetherian, every Harte-quasinilpotent element also has separated left and right powers. For common-core data in the finite-central class, the candidate is a strict output inverse exactly when the residual parallel sum is Harte-quasinilpotent. In the Banach setting, uniform input spectral gaps characterize continuity of the core and candidate along convergent input pairs, with intertwining and quasinilpotent input remainders at every term and at the limit. The output gap is equivalent when the residues of the sequence and limit are also quasinilpotent. Exact defect identities give local estimates on augmented inverse data. At an exactly intertwined base with invertible coefficient operators, we determine the feasible first-order defect space and its sharp norm constant, with a norm-specific matrix calibration.

papers.title: Minimal time of null-controllability of the multi-dimensional singular Grushin equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the null-controllability of the multi-dimensional Grushin equation with an inverse-square potential on cylinders. In the critically degenerate case, we compute the minimal time of null-controllability from vertical strips, obtaining an explicit formula depending on the distance of the strip to the singular set and on the strength of the singular potential. To do so, after a Fourier and spherical harmonic decomposition of our control system, we use the moments method for radial problems to construct controls on annuli. For this purpose, we prove a uniform spectral gap and uniform localization estimates for the eigenfunctions of the infinite family of radial operators that arise. We then reduce the control zone using spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method. In the weakly degenerate case, we prove null-controllability in arbitrarily small time from any open set. This is done using the transmutation method and quantitative observability estimates for radial waves, which yield a cost of null-controllability from annuli for the Fourier components of our system that is uniform with respect to the frequency. We conclude again with spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method.

papers.title: PSK: A Matrix-Free Single-Loop Method for K-Level Physics-Based Control
papers.abstract: Physics-based control is central to robot learning, but differentiating through implicit physics steps typically requires Hessian or Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) linear solves; we ask whether gradient steps suffice. Each simulation step minimizes an energy under many contact and collision constraints. Without constraints, we view control over $K$ steps as $K$-level optimization with strongly convex lower levels, recast as one min--max problem. Our Penalized Single-loop $K$-level method (PSK) uses only gradients and a projection, updates all levels in parallel, and reaches an $ε$-stationary control in $O(ε^{-3})$ iterations, with a $K$-independent exponent but a $K$-dependent constant. Contact-rich constraints, however, typically violate a constraint qualification (CQ). We replace each constraint by a smooth wall that acts on a band of constant width. Under mild assumptions that need no CQ, every exact solution of the banded lower levels is then feasible and banded Fritz--John, and PSK keeps the $O(ε^{-3})$ complexity. Without a CQ that is uniform in the band width, however, a shrinking band loses the $K$-independent exponent: with width $ε$ and fixed $K\geq2$, deterministic zero-respecting methods need $Ω(ε^{-(K+3)/4})$ calls on a hard instance whose control dimension grows with $1/ε$. We prove our assumptions for smoothed kinematic and dynamic multi-robot navigation among segment obstacles. In navigation experiments, PSK, tuned per case, reaches every goal with sixteen levels and, at equal time, reaches a lower loss than tuned unrolling in 17 of 18 cases, while implicit differentiation is lower in 10.

papers.title: Associahedra are 8-colourable
papers.abstract: Determining the chromatic number of associahedra is a long-standing open problem. Tan [arXiv:2611.05323] recently proved that associahedra are 12-colourable, which is the first constant upper bound. This paper adapts Tan's argument to show that associahedra are 8-colourable.

papers.title: Invariance of Arens module actions on the norm dual of a Riesz-normed f-algebra
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

papers.title: A Quantitative Kuratowski Theorem
papers.abstract: Suppose that a graph $G$ contains exactly $k$ different subdivisions of a $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$. We prove that in this case the crossing number of $G$ is at most $\binom{3k+7}{2}$ (and, when $k\le 2$, it is at most $k$).

papers.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
papers.abstract: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network. We identify the dynamical symmetry group of ensembles of Boolean networks that average over random interaction topologies: for networks with $N$ nodes, it is the $N$-dimensional hyperoctahedral group, generated by node-flips and node-label permutations. These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. We also show that input-label permutations constitute a hidden gauge freedom of the dynamics. The Zyklenzeiger symmetry of Boolean functions follows directly from the node-flips of the hyperoctahedral group together with this gauge freedom. Boolean networks related by the hyperoctahedral group have isomorphic state-space networks and form its orbits, and Burnside's lemma gives the number of these orbits for any fixed network topology. It provides a symmetry reduction of the analysis of Boolean network dynamics and explains why the Boolean functions of evolved networks fall into Zyklenzeiger classes, and why these classes split in finite networks.

papers.title: A new approach to Turán inequalities for classical orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $f,g\in C^{2}\left( a,b\right) .$ In this paper we investigate properties of the function% \[ v_{g}\left( f\right) \left( x\right) =-\frac{f^{2}\left( x\right) }{g\left( x\right) }\frac{d}{dx}\frac{g\left( x\right) f^{\prime}\left( x\right) }{f\left( x\right) }% \] where $f:\left( a,b\right) \rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is a solution of the second order differential equation $f^{\prime\prime}+pf^{\prime}+qf=0.$ Criteria for the monotonicity of $v_{g}\left( f\right) $ are given which depend on the coefficients $p$ and $q$. It is shown that for classical orthogonal polynomials $p_{n}\left( x\right) $ the Turán inequalities are equivalent to the non-negativity of the functions $v_{g}\left( p_{n}\right) $ for a suitable function $g.$ This allows new and simple proofs of classical and recent Turán inequalities.

papers.title: Constructive and computational methods for extremal and near-extremal box colorings
papers.abstract: We investigate extremal and near-extremal 2-colorings of three-dimensional grids without monochromatic axis-parallel boxes. Our approach focuses on the parameter $ρ(a,b)$, defined to be the minimum number of monochromatic rectangles in a 2-coloring of an $a\times b$ grid. We determine $ρ(a,b)$ for several small grids and use these values to obtain upper bounds on the number of layers that can be stacked to form an $a\times b\times c$ grid without creating a monochromatic box. Explicit constructions and computational certificates show that these bounds are attained for several cases, including grids of dimensions $5\times5\times100$, $5\times6\times75$, and $6\times6\times75$. For the grid of dimension $5\times7\times c$, we construct a box-free coloring with $c=50$, while our counting bound gives $c\leq 52$. This gap suggests that the counting bound may not always be sharp. We also investigate the largest $n\times n\times n$ cube admitting a box-free 2-coloring. We found box-free colorings of the $n$-cube for $n\leq 10$, and colorings of the $11\times11\times11$ cube with only eight monochromatic boxes. On the other hand, we show that every 2-coloring of the $21\times21\times21$ cube contains at least 21 monochromatic boxes. Thus the largest box-free cube has side length between 10 and 20, inclusive. We conclude with conjectures and open problems.

papers.title: Ramsey Numbers of Most Even-Linked Double Stars
papers.abstract: For $n \geq m$, the linked double star $S_c(n, m)$ is the graph formed by taking two disjoint stars $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{1, m}$ and linking their centers with a path on $c$ vertices. In this paper, we investigate the Ramsey numbers of even-linked double stars, that is, where $c = 2p$ for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. Determining the Ramsey numbers of the $p = 1$ case (classical double stars) is a longstanding open question; the $p = 2$ case was resolved by Burr and Erdős in 1976, and Liu and Chen made progress for general even-linked double stars in 2026. We extend Burr and Erdős' formula for $p = 2$, proving that the Ramsey number of $S_{2p}(n, m)$ is given by \[r(S_{2p}(n, m)) = \max(2n + 2p - 1, n + 2m + 3p - 1),\]when $m \geq p -2 \geq 0$. Our upper bound argument hinges upon the existence (or nonexistence) of an object that we call a polarized pair. We also establish a matching lower bound that applies for all $n, m, p \geq 2$, and as such, we conjecture that this formula applies for all even-linked double stars where $p \geq 2$.

papers.title: Conic Frames, Cosine Measure, and Gaussian Frames
papers.abstract: Conic combinations play an important role across mathematics in areas such as optimization, non-negative matrix factorization, and sparse coding. Frames which span their underlying space using only conic combinations, known as positive spanning sets or conic frames, are of special interest in derivative free optimization. In particular, sets with large cosine measure, a measure of how spread out the vectors are, are favored. We focus on the asymptotics of the cosine measure of Gaussian frames and present tail bounds in a variety of regimes.

papers.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect and Odd Perfect Sequences of Unbounded Length over the Unit Quaternions
papers.abstract: We give a recursive construction, with closed-form index functions, of perfect and odd perfect periodic autocorrelation sequences over the eight simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ in every length $2^n$. The sequences are built, as in the recursive perfect array construction of Blake, from \emph{twisted periodic extensions}: a short sequence continued with period $M$ up to a right factor $u\in\Qe$. Over roots of unity the twists cannot be regenerated by a one-dimensional recursion, consistently with Mow's conjecture; over $\Qe$ we show that no single sequence of length $M\not\equiv0\pmod 4$ carries a twist $\pm i,\pm j$ or $\pm k$ either, but that \emph{pairs} of sequences whose $i$- and $(-i)$-twisted autocorrelations are complementary do. These $i$-pairs behave exactly like Golay pairs: they double under interleaving with a right factor $j$ in place of a sign, every Golay pair of length $n$ gives an $i$-pair of length $2n$, and they exist in length $6$ where no Golay pair exists. An $i$-pair of length $M$ interleaves to an odd perfect sequence of length $4M$, and a perfect and an odd perfect sequence of length $M$ interleave to a perfect sequence of length $4M$ with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$. The $i$-pairs of length $2^t$ are $x^{(t)}_{r,a}=j^{w_t(r,a)}$, where $w_t(r,a)$ counts the changes in the bit string formed by $r$ and the binary digits of $a$, and the odd perfect sequence of length $2^{t+2}$ is $y^{(t)}_{2a+r}=j^{w_t(r,\,a\bmod 2^t)}\, i^{(1-2r)\lfloor a/2^t\rfloor}$. The construction also gives odd perfect sequences over $\Qe$ in every length $24\cdot2^s$ and perfect sequences in every length $6\cdot4^s$.

papers.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
papers.abstract: We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture". Given a symmetric monoidal category with suitable symmetry, we develop a categorical framework by introducing a notion of twisted factorization homology and studying its categorical action. We show that the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted local systems can be realized as a twisted factorization homology. Using metaplectic factorizable Satake we further prove that the metaplectic Hecke action naturally fits into our categorical framework. Combining these results, we obtain the desired spectral action.

papers.title: Braid monodromy and the Cartwright--Steger surface
papers.abstract: Building on the Livne-like construction of Cartwright, Koziarz and Yeung, we construct a closed smooth 4-manifold with a map to the two-sphere whose generic fiber has genus 109 and whose four exceptional fibers are determined by explicit braid and permutation data. A pencil of four-pointed spheres realizes the same global braid monodromy and makes the covering holomorphic. We show that the contraction of its thirty-six exceptional curves is the Cartwright-Steger surface, hence our smooth construction gives a topological description of this complex surface.

papers.title: On the boomerang spectrum of the APN power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$
papers.abstract: We study the boomerang spectrum of the almost perfect nonlinear power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$, where $q$ is an odd prime power with $q\equiv1\pmod6$. The connection of Pal and Stănică between boomerang entries and $(-1)$-differential entries reduces the problem to counting roots of a single equation. We determine the complete contribution from nonzero parameters in $\F_q$. For parameters outside $\F_q$, we obtain a quintic over $\F_q$ in terms of the parameter's trace and norm, with a separate formula when the trace is zero. We exclude the entry four when $q\equiv1\pmod{12}$ and characterize its occurrence when $q\equiv7\pmod{12}$ through a repeated-root parametrization and a residual cubic. We also evaluate the first nonsubfield moment and an aggregate quadratic-character sum, and prove a Weil bound for each nonzero trace. Explicit secant and residual-cubic formulas express the second, third, and fourth falling-factorial moments as finite sums. Once the size-four frequency is known, these moments recover all remaining frequencies through a nonsingular five-dimensional system. A closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.

papers.title: Sharp fill-in inequalities and rigidity for spin initial data sets
papers.abstract: We prove sharp fill-in inequalities for compact spin initial data sets satisfying the dominant energy condition. The inequalities relate the spacetime mean curvature of the boundary to its hyperspherical radius and stable one-systole. Equality characterizes spacelike graphs of constant boundary height over round Euclidean balls and, in the systolic case after passing to the universal cover, over products of a round disk with Euclidean space. We also prove rigidity under comparison with strictly convex Euclidean domains, using normalized boundary metrics. The proofs use a modified Dirac operator with a chiral boundary condition.

papers.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
papers.abstract: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

papers.title: Nonsmooth Convex and Strongly Convex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons
papers.abstract: We study nonsmooth convex and strongly convex optimization problems using only noisy pairwise comparisons: each query specifies two points and returns a single binary response indicating which point has the smaller function value, subject to noise. We distinguish two observation models: Stochastic Order Oracles, which compare two evaluations of the same random loss, and Preference Oracles, whose conditional response mean is a transfer function of the objective difference. For Stochastic Order Oracles, we prove that no comparison-based algorithm can guarantee vanishing expected suboptimality in general, even when sample losses are convex and Lipschitz and the mean objective is strongly convex. Under a normalized probit calibration, we recover convergence and establish matching upper and lower rates for convex and strongly convex objectives. For Preference Oracles with a linear response model, the binary response $O \in \{\pm1\}$ satisfies $\E[O\mid y,z]=λ(f(y)-f(z))$, with $λ>0$. In dimension $d$, we obtain an upper bound of $\widetilde (d^{3/2}/(λ\sqrt N))$ and establish, to our knowledge, the first minimax lower bound of $Ω(d/(λ\sqrt N))$, matching the optimal budget $N$ exponent, for both convex and strongly convex nonsmooth objectives. Beyond exact linearity, we analyze a simple projected comparison method for nonlinear transfer functions and establish convergence rates that depend on how accurately these functions can be approximated by a linear model near zero. Our analysis requires neither oddness nor twice differentiability of the transfer function.

papers.title: On the number of elite primes
papers.abstract: A prime $p$ is elite if all sufficiently large Fermat numbers $F_n=2^{2^n}+1$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$. Let $E(x)$ be the number of elite primes up to $x$. The best published bounds are $E(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{3/2}$ unconditionally and $E(x)\ll x^{5/6}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), both due to Just. Just and Pollack remarked, without a written proof, that sorting primes by the exact power of $2$ dividing $p-1$ should give $x/(\log x)^{2-\varepsilon}$ and $x^{3/4+\varepsilon}$. We give complete proofs of slightly sharper statements: $E(x)\le(16+o(1))x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$ unconditionally, and $E(x)\ll x^{3/4}(\log x)^{1/2}$ under GRH. We also recall, with short proofs, known facts about the period of $(F_n\bmod p)$ that go back to Aigner: every elite prime $p$ satisfies the defining condition from the index $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p 2)$ onwards, and the period is even unless $p\in\{3,5\}$. Finally, we show under GRH that, when the moduli involved are at most $x^{1/3}$, the set of primes bounded by the sieve argument has size $\asymp x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$. This indicates that the remaining factor $\log\log x$ cannot be removed by this method alone. All theorems of the paper have been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the Brun--Titchmarsh inequality and two standard consequences of GRH as explicit hypotheses.

papers.title: Symbolic Powers and Asymptotic Invariants of Invariant Ideals in Determinantal Rings
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the coordinate ring of a bounded-rank locus of generic, symmetric, alternating, or Hankel matrices. Thus $A$ is the quotient of a polynomial ring by a generic determinantal, symmetric determinantal, generic Pfaffian, or Hankel determinantal ideal. In each case there is a nested family of rank primes ${\mathfrak p}_1\supset {\mathfrak p}_2\supset\cdots\supset{\mathfrak p}_q$ and a standard-monomial basis whose shapes are diagrams with parts at most $q$. We isolate the common properties of these four straightening theories and use them to give a uniform treatment of products $D_σ={\mathfrak p}_{σ_1}\cdots{\mathfrak p}_{σ_s}$ in the quotient ring $A$, extending analogous results over suitable polynomial rings. In all four cases the shape $σ$ must have parts of size at most $q$. We determine their primary decompositions and associated primes in the rank-$q$ quotient, compute all symbolic powers with respect to the full set of associated primes, and prove that their symbolic Rees algebras are finitely generated. In the generic, symmetric, and alternating cases the respective symbolic Rees algebras are also normal, and Cohen--Macaulay. We also determine the asymptotic resurgence $\widehatρ$ and Waldschmidt constants of these ideals and prove they are related by $\widehatρ(D_σ)=α(D_σ)/\widehatα(D_σ)$.

papers.title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field. Finally, we compute the tropical $E_6$-Grassmannian and its 60 classes of toric degenerations. This is an extended abstract for a forthcoming paper.

papers.title: Positivity and Boundedness of Solutions to the Guyon-Lekeufack Volatility Model with General Kernels
papers.abstract: We study nonnegativity of the volatility in the continuous-time Guyon-Lekeufack model, in which volatility is an affine function of the convolution of past returns with a kernel $K_1$ and the square root of the integral of past squared returns weighted by a kernel $K_2$. We show that, when volatility is nonnegative and $K_1$ admits a resolvent of the first kind, uniform boundedness of integrals of $K_2$ with respect to this resolvent yields a deterministic upper bound for the asset price, which is then a bounded martingale on every finite time interval. This result is the counterpart of the strict local martingality criterion for negative volatility in Guyon, Jeannin and Jourdain (2026, Corollary 2.6(ii)). We also derive such bounds for popular stochastic volatility models when the Brownian motions driving the asset price and volatility have correlation $-1$. We give sufficient conditions for nonnegative volatility with a completely monotone return convolution kernel $K_1$, and necessary conditions when $K_1$ and $K_2$ are respectively $M$- and $N$-exponential kernels. For $M=1$, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition.

papers.title: The Deepest Pairs of Points Are Not as Deep as Conjectured
papers.abstract: Given any finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, Neumann-Lara and Urrutia \cite{NLUr88} proved in 1988 that there is always a pair such that every circle through the two points encloses a positive fraction of all points. While Edelsbrunner et al.\ \cite{EHSS89} showed that the fraction is at least $\sfrac{1}{2} - \sfrac{1}{\sqrt{12}} = 0.211\ldots$, Urrutia \cite{Urr02} conjectured that the constant $\sfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$ in the upper bound proved by Hayward, Rappaport and Wenger \cite{HRW89} is best possible. We disprove this conjecture by lowering the constant to $\sfrac{3}{14} = 0.214\ldots$. The new bound also disproves a related conjecture by Ramos and Viaña \cite{RaVi09} on finite sets in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Finally, we generalize the latter extremal question to finite sets in possibly non-convex position, for which we prove the first linear lower bound, with constant $\sfrac{(2-\sqrt{2})}{6} = 0.097\ldots$.

papers.title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
papers.abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapstoχ_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.

papers.title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
papers.abstract: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study (arXiv:2511.02864v3), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.

papers.title: Splitting and Mixed Deformations of Toric Generalized Kähler Potentials
papers.abstract: We study splitting phenomena for extremal toric generalized Kähler structures on products of compact toric manifolds. We prove that every extremal symplectic potential splits when the skew-symmetric parameter $B$ is block diagonal, without any restriction on $A$. We also construct two types of non-splitting examples on $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$: an explicit constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structure with a splitting potential but a non-product generalized Kähler structure, and a deformation family of constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structures with genuinely non-splitting potentials.

papers.title: On the false discovery rate of one-sided p-values under Gaussian dependence
papers.abstract: We study the false discovery rate (FDR) of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for $K$ hypotheses at nominal level $q$ under Gaussian dependence of one-sided p-values. We ask whether the global null is least favorable after optimizing over correlation matrices. We show that the global null attains the worst-case FDR for $K\le3$ at every level. In dimension eight, an explicit mixed-null construction has FDR $21q/20$ for $0<q<1/2$. It exceeds the global-null maximum for all sufficiently small $q$, by a uniform extension of the known fixed-matrix small-level Simes bound. For $0<q<1/2$, we identify eight as the first inflation dimension in the monotone rank-one class and prove that $21q/20$ is its exact eight-dimensional maximum. In the same level range, the sharp multiplicative bound over all dimensions in this class is twice the omega constant $w = W(1)$, where $W$ is the Lambert $W$ function. This bound is approached as the dimension increases. We also give scale conditions for stability around the independence benchmark $m_0q/K$, where $m_0$ is the number of true nulls, and obtain a dimension-free upper bound of $q+q^2/2+O(q^3)$ at small levels under the global null with nonpositive correlations.

papers.title: Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Learning the underlying probability distribution from samples is a core problem in statistics and applied mathematics. Generative models based on diffusion and flow matching learn a velocity field whose flow transports a known distribution to the data distribution. They produce novel, realistic samples, although the empirical learning problem is ill posed near the data distribution. Its minimizer transports the samples onto the training data, and small perturbations of the data change the velocity field strongly near the end of the flow. The observed generalization is often attributed to implicit regularization by the network parameterization, early stopping of the training, and the time integration during sampling. Explicit regularization has advanced the theory and computation of many inverse problems and has recently been proposed to prevent memorization in generative models. With a regularizer on the magnitude of the velocity, however, the field approaches the memorizing velocity unless the regularization parameter grows to infinity fast enough, and it then stays bounded by a constant that is small only for large parameters. We show that penalizing the derivatives of order $k$ of the velocity renders the $D$-dimensional empirical problem well posed uniformly in time if $2k > D$ and the training points are in general position. Our experiments in one and two dimensions discretize the velocity with splines and use direct solvers for the regularized least-squares problems to exclude optimization error. Refining the discretization in space and time changes the error of the Hessian-regularized flows only marginally, whereas without the regularizer the error tends to that of memorization. These flows generalize, with errors comparable to or lower than those of well-tuned kernel density estimates.

papers.title: The stable false discovery rate
papers.abstract: When a discovery depends on analysis choices, a list of selected hypotheses that controls the false discovery rate (FDR) gives little indication of how easily the finding could change: the selected set may be very sensitive to a variety of analyst choices, like the target FDR level, which machine learning algorithms are used in the pipeline, the choice of test statistics, and so on. We propose that scientists should measure and control a new metric called the \emph{stable FDR} (sFDR), and give methods to control it, including simple wrappers around existing FDR analysis pipelines. sFDR is a natural continuous extension of the FDR: we assign each hypothesis an allocation between zero and one, and the sFDR equals the expected fraction of null allocation to total allocation. If one runs multiple analyses of the same data by varying different reasonable choices, allocations can be determined by simply dividing each run's selection indicators by its discovery count, then averaging across analyses and rescaling. The resulting sFDR equals the average of the ordinary FDRs of the runs, even though the runs are dependent: thus sFDR control holds under the same assumptions that the original FDR control held. (In contrast, naively reporting just fractions of times each variable was selected need not control the sFDR.) It is interpretable: hypotheses that were always selected are allocated 1 and those never selected are allocated 0. In leukemia expression and neuroimaging analyses, findings with larger allocations were more often supported in separate samples. We also develop procedures that can assign stable allocations directly from p-values, e-values, or knockoff statistics, resulting in stable-BH, stable e-BH and stable knockoff procedures. A representation by e-values describes which allocation rules control the error rate and gives ways to optimize allocations for different follow-up goals.

papers.title: Finite-summability in the noncommutative geometry of crossed products
papers.abstract: We study finite-summability of unbounded representatives of $K$-homology classes for crossed-product $C^*$-algebras associated with actions on compact spaces. Using Kasparov's Dirac--dual-Dirac method, we isolate geometric conditions on the $γ$-element under which elements of $K$-homology can be transferred to a crossed product associated with a proper action and represented by finitely summable unbounded cycles defined from Dirac-type operators with an unbounded potential. We relate finite-summability of these operators to integrability properties of the potential by spectral estimates for Schrödinger operators on manifolds of bounded geometry. In particular, for finitely generated nilpotent groups this leads to finitely summable, unbounded representatives of all $K$-homology classes. We also give examples showing that representability of $K$-homology classes by finitely summable unbounded cycles is not invariant under $KK$-equivalence.

papers.title: Log Hodge-de Rham degeneration beyond the toroidal case
papers.abstract: Let $φ\colon X \to S$ be a flat and proper one-parameter degeneration of algebraic varieties with a single degenerate fiber $X_0$. If $φ\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ is log smooth and saturated, the log Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence is known to degenerate at the page $E_1$. Adding to that some further well-known related properties, we say that the log de Rham complex $Ω^{\bullet,\mathrm{log}}_{X/S}$ is cohomologically flat as a filtered complex, short cffc. Furthermore, if $φ\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ has only toroidal log singularities, it is known that the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. A major motivation to study this property is that in the Calabi-Yau case, $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ being cffc implies that a certain logarithmic deformation functor for $φ_0\colon X_0^\partial \to S_0^\dagger$ is unobstructed. In this article, we develop a computational criterion to determine, under very mild assumptions on $φ\colon X \to S$, whether the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. Applying this criterion, we found many explicit examples of degenerations of surfaces where $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc, even though the log singularities are worse than toroidal. We did not find any new examples of degenerations of threefolds such that $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc.

papers.title: The Contingent HOD Dichotomy
papers.abstract: The axiom V = HOD, referring to the class of hereditarily ordinal-definable sets, is contingently contingent by forcing---it holds contingently in the generic multiverse of some models of set theory but not others. Thus we introduce and investigate the \emph{contingent HOD dichotomy}, according to which either (1) the set-theoretic universe V is close to HOD by forcing---HOD is a ground, V = HOD is forceable, the universe is ordinal-definable from a set parameter $V=\text{HOD}_b$, the blurry HOD hierarchy collapses to kappa-HOD for some cardinal kappa, and furthermore these features are invariant by forcing and hold throughout the generic multiverse; or (2) the universe V is far from HOD by forcing in all those respects, so $V\neq\text{HOD}$, but also HOD is not a ground, V = HOD is not forceable, the set-theoretic universe is not ordinal-definable from a set, the universe is not kappa-HOD for any kappa, and these features hold invariantly throughout the generic multiverse. We investigate the nature of the dichotomy in connection with large cardinals, with set-theoretic geology, with the iterated $\text{HOD}^α$ classes, and with the maximality principles MP and MP(R), showing generally that both prongs of the dichotomy occur with diverse set-theoretic phenomena.

papers.title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

papers.title: Bellman Residual Bracketing: Resolving the Sample Complexity of Discounted and Average-Reward RL
papers.abstract: We study the sample complexity of the empirical planning or plug-in approach for reinforcement learning (RL) with a generative model. We show the discounted plug-in approach finds an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy with $O(SA (1-γ)^{-3} \varepsilon^{-2} \log(SA/δ))$ samples, where $S, A, γ, δ$ are the state and action sizes, discount factor, and failure probability, respectively. In the average-reward setting, we show that discounted plug-in and direct (undiscounted) plug-in achieve $O(SAH\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ and $O(SAD\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ complexities, respectively, where $H$ upper-bounds the optimal bias span and $D$ is the diameter. Combining with our lower bounds for nonadaptive generative models, these results resolve the minimax sample complexity of discounted RL and average-reward RL --- in both the span- and diameter-based classes --- up to constant factors. Our main technical contribution is a novel Bellman residual bracketing technique which improves the efficiency of prior absorbing-MDP-based concentration analyses.

papers.title: Conditional Stochastic User Equilibrium as a Gibbs Distribution: Tractable Flow Laws and Exact Path-Free Sampling
papers.abstract: Treating traffic counts as data calls for the joint distribution of link flows. Stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) gives a single flow vector, and independent route choice at fixed probabilities ignores congestion feedback between travelers. Conditional stochastic user equilibrium (CSUE), in which each traveler of a finite population chooses a route by logit conditional on the routes of all others, contains this feedback but has been hard to compute with at scale. Under separable link costs and a common route-choice precision, the CSUE conditionals are those of a unique Gibbs distribution whose energy is a left-endpoint discrete congestion potential, and for continuous nondecreasing costs the law concentrates on deterministic logit SUE in the large-population limit. When the routes of each origin are the paths of an acyclic bush, retaining origin- or OD-level labels gives an unnormalized layered link-flow law with an explicit product-form multiplicity. On this representation we build a block Metropolis-Hastings sampler whose proposal is an integer version of Dial's loading under frozen costs. It leaves the CSUE law on the bush route sets invariant without enumerating paths or storing individual routes, and at stationarity the mean rejection rate of a block lies between one and two times the total variation distance between its proposal and exact conditional. In experiments, the sampler reproduces reference laws from exact enumeration and traveler-level Gibbs sampling, whereas independent route choice at frozen costs reproduces mean flows but overstates link-flow standard deviations by up to 48% and distorts correlations. On Sioux Falls, the block sampler attains 76.1 times the minimum effective sample size per CPU second of traveler-level Gibbs sampling, and on Chicago Sketch, with over one million travelers, its sampled covariance is used to assess traffic-count locations.

papers.title: An Explicit Version of Serre's Open Image Theorem for Galois Number Fields
papers.abstract: In 1971, Serre showed that the mod $p$ Galois representation associated to a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field is surjective for all but finitely many primes $p$. That is, there exists a constant $c(E,K)$, for $E$ a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field $K$, such that $ρ_{E,p}:\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \mathrm{Aut}(E[p])$ is surjective for all primes $p>c(E,K)$. We give a bound for this constant using an effective version of the Faltings isogeny theorem for specific number fields. We show that, for $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ with $|D|<50$ and $K$ a formally real number field, given a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $K$ we have $c(E,K)\le 2C_1(K)\log N_{K/\mathbb Q}\operatorname{rad}\left( 2\mathcal O_K\mathfrak N_{E}\right )+2 C_2(K)$, where $\mathfrak N_E$ denotes the conductor ideal of $E$, and the constants $C_1(K)$ and $C_2(K)$ can be described explicitly. We also show that for primes greater than this bound, the image cannot be contained in the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup. This works for any Galois number field. Our proof assumes the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).

papers.title: Counterexamples to Strichartz estimates for general irrotational compressible Euler backgrounds and positive estimates for a spherical isotropic background solution
papers.abstract: We consider the free boundary problem for the irrotational compressible Euler equation in a physical vacuum setting. By using the irrotationality condition in the Eulerian formulation of Ifrim and Tataru, we previously showed that the problem can be rephrased in terms of the velocity potential function as an acoustic wave equation that turns out to be widely used in solar seismology. This paper is another step towards understanding what Strichartz estimates are achievable for the aforementioned equation. Our object of study is the corresponding linearized problem. In a previous work, we constructed a class of gallery modes in a model stationary case, which turned out to be counterexamples to Strichartz estimates, forcing a loss of derivatives. By a careful regularization of the domain defining function, we transplant these counterexamples to general Euler backgrounds, and obtain general counterexamples in the same range. On the other hand, we also prove that for the background corresponding to a concrete affine isotropic spherical solution for the irrotational compressible Euler equations, one has Strichartz estimates up to the aforementioned threshold, which shows that they are optimal for at least some explicit Euler backgrounds. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results of this kind for explicit solutions of the irrotational compressible Euler equations in a physical vacuum.

papers.title: Determinateness in a classical theory of nonclassical truth
papers.abstract: Recent theories that take determinateness as primitive are either nonclassical theories of nonclassical truth, like Field's INT, or classical theories of classical truth, like Fujimoto and Halbach's CD and CD^+. This paper develops a third option: a classical theory of nonclassical truth. The theory, KFDcs, extends the Kripke-Feferman theory KFcs with a primitive determinateness predicate. Unlike CD^+, KFDcs keeps the iteration of truth unrestricted and gives up its completeness. With or without a consistency axiom, KFD is proof-theoretically equivalent to the theory \widehat{ID}_2 of twice iterated fixed points, with ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\varepsilon}_0, 0)0), thus stronger than CD^+. It is also shown that replacing full induction with internal induction yields ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}(ω, 0)0), and restricting internal induction to total formulae yields {\varphi}({\varepsilon_0},0), the ordinal of KF.

papers.title: Sharp condition for the existence of wave operators
papers.abstract: We study the wave operators for a Jacobi matrix whose spectral measure satisfies the Szegő condition. We formulate a sufficient condition in terms of the associated Verblunsky parameters and show that it is sharp.

papers.title: Large caps in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$
papers.abstract: We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate. Assigning the $80$-point set to a noncentral $45$-point section gives $5744$, gaining $240$ points over the $5504$ construction obtained from a central $40$-point section.

papers.title: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
papers.abstract: Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. However, neural symbolic mathematics still trains a dedicated sequence-to-sequence model for each task, so that no representation of a function is shared. In this work, we propose the Function Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Func-JEPA, abbreviated f-JEPA): an encoder of mathematical functions, pretrained on their symbolic form, whose latent space imitates the Sobolev space H^1 and in which differentiation is a learned latent operator. The norm of a latent is computed exactly from the function, whereas its direction is learned to match Sobolev angles. The frozen encoder is then reused by lightweight modules for decoding, composition, integration, and regression from samples. The representation and four downstream tasks are evaluated within and outside the pretraining distribution. f-JEPA recovers exact formulas from noisy samples more often than the compared symbolic-regression methods, whereas computer algebra and task-specific models remain stronger on standard integration and differential-equation benchmarks.

papers.title: Second-Order Threshold and Value Asymptotics in Multiple-Stopping Secretary Problems
papers.abstract: We study the classical secretary problem with a fixed number of selection opportunities. We derive explicit corrections to the limiting thresholds and to the optimal success probability. A cancellation identity removes the influence of later threshold rounding from the first correction, while a Poisson representation explains its probabilistic meaning. Every bounded rounding of the limiting thresholds shares the first value correction. We obtain integer rounding laws, eventual threshold identities along continued-fraction convergents, and joint rounding frequencies. Rigorous rational bounds show that the first eleven corrections are positive and the twelfth is negative, producing the first shifted convergent identity.

papers.title: Chang's Omitting Types Theorem in Lukasiewicz Logic
papers.abstract: We prove Chang-style omitting types theorems for standard first-order Lukasiewicz logic. Starting from a prescribed model $M$, we obtain an extension that omits higher-complexity types while preserving lower-level types already realized in $M$. If $T$ is a $Π_{n+2}$-theory, every model of $T$ has an exact extension that preserves its realized $Σ_{n+1}$-types and omits every $Σ_{n+2}$-type not generated by a $Σ_{n+1}$-type. An iterated construction also omits infinity-universal types, whose unbounded quantifier complexity cannot eventually be generated by the corresponding lower-complexity fragments of a single type. The main tool is a refinement of Robinson's infinite forcing sensitive to the quantifier complexity of formulas.

papers.title: Weak-type $(p,p)$ inequalities for Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Geometrically formal Hermitian metrics on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify compact complex surfaces admitting either a geometrically Dolbeault formal or an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric. Furthermore, we prove that on a compact Kähler surface, every ABC-geometrically formal metric is Kähler, whereas, for geometrically Dolbeault formal Hermitian metrics, Gauduchon, LCK, and Kähler conditions are equivalent. On non-Kähler surfaces, an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric is LCK and, except on Inoue surfaces, Vaisman.

papers.title: Edgeworth expansion on sums of Wiener chaos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Edgeworth expansions for random variables belonging to a fixed finite sum of Wiener chaoses. Building on the work of Mansanarez, Poly and Swan (arXiv:2510.14002) for a single Wiener chaos, we investigate the extension of their approach to functionals $F$ living in a finite sum of Wiener chaoses $\mathcal{W}_{\leq d}$. Within the Malliavin--Stein framework, we bound the total variation distance between the law of $F$ and its Edgeworth approximation of order $2dm$ by $(\sum_{p,q}^d \operatorname{Var}Γ(F_p,F_q))^{m/2}(\operatorname{Var}Γ(F,\operatorname{L}^{-1}F))^{1/2}$, where $F_p$ denotes the projection of $F$ onto the $p$-th Wiener chaos. The presence of several chaotic components introduces additional interactions, since these components are orthogonal but generally dependent. Since our proof relies on the integration-by-parts formalism and the spectral properties of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, this result extends naturally to the broader framework of Markov chaoses.

papers.title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
papers.abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

papers.title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. For every symmetric positive definite interaction matrix, we relate the minimizer to a corresponding anisotropic Brownian motion and use the Feynman--Kac formula and elliptic regularity theory to show that it admits a smooth, strictly positive density on the sphere. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. In dimension two, we also propose a numerical scheme for approximating its density based on a Mathieu series expansion.

papers.title: Denoising-Induced Recovery of Effective Dynamics
papers.abstract: Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification. Here, we reveal the effects of filtering, a specific denoising technique, on recovery. Our analysis show that equation discovery performed on filtered data recovers, up to a fixed precision, the normal-form (effective) equations rather than the original system.

papers.title: Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
papers.abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

papers.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

papers.title: Quantum periods and threefold flips
papers.abstract: We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that $$ \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t). $$ The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula. We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.

papers.title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

papers.title: Asymptotic Divergence-Based Monitoring for Data Drift in Production AI Systems: A Discrete Case Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a complete asymptotic theory for monitoring data drift in production artificial intelligence (AI) systems whose inputs take values in a finite set of categories. The framework combines two complementary inferential tools. Under the no-drift hypothesis $H_0$, the two-sample likelihood-ratio statistic $G$ of Wilks follows a universal Chi_{r-1}^2 law, independently of the divergence chosen and of the sample sizes; the calibrated Population Stability Index (PSI) of Yurdakul and Naranjo (2021) shares the same Chi_{r-1}^2 limit and is asymptotically equivalent to the $G$-test under $H_0$. Under the drift hypothesis $H_1$, the plug-in phi-divergence is asymptotically normal with a variance computed in closed form for the one-sample, two-sample and symmetrized configurations, yielding standardized $Z$-statistics, detection boundaries, power functions and sample-size planning rules. We supply a per-category decomposition that localizes the drift on specific categories, a Benjamini--Hochberg procedure for monitoring many features simultaneously, and an explicit comparison with the heuristic PSI cut-offs of industrial practice. Two fully worked simulation examples - one one-sample with the Rényi divergence and multiple testing, one two-sample with the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and sample-size planning - illustrate every notion of the paper on realistic production data.

papers.title: Quaternion Matrix Tuples with Common Invariant Subspaces: Dimension and Nonuniqueness
papers.abstract: Let $M_n(\mathbb{H})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ quaternion matrices. We study common invariant right subspaces of tuples in $M_n(\mathbb{H})^r$ and determine exact real semialgebraic dimensions for two associated sets. If $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ are positive integers, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_s$, and $q=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq s}n_an_b$, the set of tuples preserving at least one nested chain with successive increments $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)q$. For $r\geq2$ and $1\leq k<n$, the set of tuples with at least two distinct common $k$-dimensional right invariant subspaces has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)(k(n-k)+n-1)$. The proofs use finite right-module coordinates and a common local-rank argument.

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.

papers.title: Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
papers.abstract: We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. Unlike previous algorithms which only provide information of wave spectrum, our approach reconstructs the instantaneous phase-resolved wave field. The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. Together with EnKF in the second step, we model the coupled wave-ship dynamics by a high-order spectral (HOS) method for waves and a Cummins equation for ship motion (although higher-fidelity ship model can be applied).
