For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $Λ=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $Λ$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.

papers.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
papers.abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

papers.title: Oriented V-systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap and characterize power against fixed and local alternatives. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates of observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a novel threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule uses the estimated bias to determine whether a reference threshold can be lowered to retain more observations, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables is finite: well-founded refutations in infinitary real-valued logic
papers.abstract: We study the obstructions to noncontextual hidden variables when quantum probability is described in full, by the complete lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space together with its countably additive measures. We give such a description in infinitary real-valued logic, the infinitary extension of Keisler's model theory of general structures; the countable suprema and infima of this logic express the completeness of the lattice and the countable additivity of the measures. The standard models of our axioms represent exactly the density-operator measures of Gleason's theorem. The axioms are closed conditions, non-strict inequalities between the values of sentences and rational numbers. The expressive power afforded by infinitary sentences comes at the price of compactness. The hypothesis that at each hidden state every event receives the value 0 or 1, whatever the context of measurement, contradicts the axioms, yet it is consistent with every finite subset of them. The obstructions nevertheless remain finite. We prove that in this logic a countable set of closed conditions is inconsistent if and only if a well-founded tree whose branches end in finite contradictions refutes it; for the hypothesis above, every such tree has an infinitely branching node. The finiteness theorem is therefore maximal: a hidden-variable hypothesis expressed by countably many closed conditions is inconsistent with the axioms, and thus an obstruction, exactly when such a tree refutes the hypothesis together with the axioms. The same language defines, uniformly across standard models, exactly the $σ$-projective sets of probabilities, and all these results are proved in ZFC.

papers.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning. Empirical evidence suggests that, across a variety of models with and without downstream adaptation, ensembles tend to be more robust to covariate shift than single models. We extend the theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, providing theoretical justification for the empirical trends. We introduce new discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. We then show that with sufficient ensemble size, these models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. Our results suggest that modelers can expect to need larger ensemble sizes for more severe covariate shifts.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Studentized inference in randomized experiments when a few units dominate the outcome variation
papers.abstract: In completely randomized experiments with heavy-tailed outcomes, a few units can carry a share of the residual variation that does not vanish as the number of units grows. In this setting, we study the studentized difference in means and Lin's regression-adjusted estimator under a design-based framework. The studentized statistic has a nonnormal limit in general. Populations with the same marginal distributions of potential outcomes can have different limits, as the limit depends on how the two potential outcomes of each dominant unit are paired. When the outcome errors are drawn from a heavy-tailed law, the limit is random and, outside a degenerate case, varies with the population. Under balanced allocation, the conventional Wald interval has an explicit asymptotic coverage floor. At the nominal level of $0.95$, the floor is about $0.42$ for every population and about $0.84$ when the two potential residuals of each unit are equal. Both floors are close to the best possible, and without balanced allocation, the coverage can fall to the smaller of the proportions of treated and control units.

papers.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an Itô diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and generator evaluations, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs a third matrix, a dictionary with four derivatives, and a fourth-order differential operator evaluated at every sample. Richardson extrapolation of the SDMD-1 step (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. The error bound, for exact and empirical matrices, consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. Relative to the Galerkin semigroup, the limit of the schemes as the time step $\dt\to0$, the time-stepping error is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(Θ_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, with $Θ_N$ the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$, and the first-order term is attained. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a data term of order $K^{d+2}(m^{-1}\log K)^{1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. In experiments with trigonometric dictionaries the errors of SDMD-R and SDMD-2 differ by at most ten percent. For a spline dictionary with two derivatives, SDMD-R remains second-order accurate, whereas SDMD-2 with pointwise evaluations is first-order accurate.

papers.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
papers.abstract: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

papers.title: Indecomposability of derived categories and nef canonical divisors in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, which establishes \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{KO2018} in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of nontrivial admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.abstract: We study wall crossing for ideal classes of rational curves of degrees two through five on the quintic del Pezzo threefold $X=V_5$. Wall exclusion and a uniform bound on the correction length rule out point corrections in degrees two through four on the outer segments of the negative zero-tilt-slope paths. In degree five a correction of length one occurs and gives rise to a second component of the good moduli space. For a rational outer stability parameter, this space is reduced and has exactly two irreducible components. The closure of the smooth rational-quintic locus is a normal tenfold. The other component is the smooth thirteenfold $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Its points represent the polystable objects $I_{E_L}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_p$, where the pencil $L$ cuts out a quintic linear section $E_L$ of arithmetic genus one. The scheme-theoretic intersection is the normal determinantal ninefold parametrizing pairs $(p,L)$ for which $E_L$ is singular at $p$. Along their common reduced singular locus, the principal component and the intersection have transverse models given by the cones of $2\times4$ and $2\times3$ matrices of rank at most one, respectively. We construct a small resolution of the principal component as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota sixfold along its point locus.

papers.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact Kähler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in the companion paper (arXiv:2611.14090).

papers.title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $Λ^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $Λ^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations. The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra, and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions. Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.

papers.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
papers.abstract: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.

papers.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

papers.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
papers.abstract: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.

papers.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{μ_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_σ(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(μ_k)\toβ(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists. We apply these results to matrix cocycles, establishing the existence of invariant measures that realize the joint spectral radius for countable families of matrices.

papers.title: Tilting theory on continuous quivers (I) maximal rigid and tilting subcategories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ be the category of finitely generated persistence modules on the interval $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb R$. We study the maximal rigid subcategories of $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$. Maximal rigid interval consistent subcategories are classified via tilting modules over the corresponding discrete type $A$ quiver. We compare several related notions, (weak) tilting and maximal rigidity, in both the context of hereditary abelian categories with enough projective objects and $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ and prove that every maximal rigid interval consistent subcategory is weak tilting and every maximal rigid consistent below subcategory is tilting. In addition, any maximal rigid subcategory $\mathbf T\subseteq \mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$, not necessarily being interval consistent, satisfies $\mathbf T^{\perp_1}=\mathop {Gen}(\mathbf T)$. We also establish a continuous analogue of Ingalls-Thomas's bijection by showing a bijection between integrally supported maximal rigid consistent below subcategories and integrally generated torsion classes.

papers.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
papers.abstract: For a $Δ$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the localized regime $np^{Δ/2}\gg(\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p\ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices in $H$, and identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this rare event. The degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ changes the Erdős-Rényi picture in two ways. First, the hub construction that competes with a clique in the regime $p \gg n^{-1/Δ}$ is not feasible here. Consequently, for $Δ\geq 3$ throughout the entire localized regime, both the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by a planted almost-clique, of size roughly $δ^{1/v_H}np^{Δ/2}$. Second, as no clique in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ can be of size greater than $(d+1)$, for $Δ=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by $\lfloorδ\rfloor$ many planted almost-cliques of size roughly $d$ and another planted almost-clique of size roughly $\{δ\}^{1/v_H}d$. For cycles of even length, in lieu of pairs of almost-cliques each of size roughly $d$, the conditional structure may possess copies of almost-bicliques with each side roughly of size $d$. In the complementary regime $1\ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H}\ll(\log n)^{α^*_H/(α^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges and $α^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including regular $H$), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

papers.title: Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
papers.abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic surrogate system of PDEs whose solution approximates that of the original stochastic problem. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Rosenblatt, Nataf) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated Gaussian parameters when the basis functionals are multivariate Hermite polynomials (MHPs), where these polynomials are only weakly orthogonal with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs that emerge during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations via tensorization. Namely, an $N$th-order moment has no closed-form expression for $N > 2$ and consequently is estimated numerically. Because the number of such moments grows combinatorially with parameter dimension and polynomial degree, approximating each one individually via sampling or quadrature can quickly become cost-prohibitive. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational properties of MHPs. These results culminate in an explicit formula for evaluating the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) directly without numerical estimation.

papers.title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric descriptions of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we characterise when passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

papers.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
papers.abstract: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both based on the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. For the affine-moment deformation, we establish coefficientwise Hankel total positivity via a continuant criterion and determine Hankel determinants and extremal coefficients of minors. The Askey--Wilson basis deformation yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel whose row polynomials have simple negative zeros, strict interlacing, and $γ$-positivity after palindromic normalization. A $q^2$-Askey--Wilson integral gives a continuous-parameter moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion; an ordinary-power expansion recovers Pan's Touchard identity. For $0<q<1$ and $θ>-1$, we establish total positivity of the kernel triangle and strict total positivity of its associated square, extending Wang--Yang's results simultaneously in $(θ,q)$. We also prove coefficientwise total nonnegativity through order two for endpoint triangles and give an exact triangular change of basis between the deformations. Finally, we identify Tevlin's dual super $q$-Narayana polynomials with a normalized kernel, derive the recurrence for their index-two $q$-$γ$ coefficients via Rogers-functional Pearson--Christoffel identities, and deduce total positivity of the dual triangles and strict total positivity of their squares.

papers.title: Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fréchet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fréchet Means
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the Fréchet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity or semiconvexity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity of the population Fréchet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for its gradient at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On complete connected Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+η)$-moment, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fréchet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fréchet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fréchet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. A flat-torus example exhibits anisotropic scaling, and two examples on the circle illustrate logarithmic smeariness and the failure of any deterministic linear scaling to yield a nondegenerate limit, respectively.

papers.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
papers.abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

papers.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
papers.abstract: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.

papers.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
papers.abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

papers.title: Prescribed-Vertex Rainbow Cycle Spectra in Graph Systems under a Local Ore Condition
papers.abstract: Let $\GraphSys=(G_1,\ldots,G_n)$ be a system of graphs on a common $n$-vertex set, put $δ(v)=\min_i d_{G_i}(v)$ and $E_\cap=\bigcap_i E(G_i)$, and write $d^c$ for rainbow distance. Assume that each $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that $d^c(u,v)\le2$ and $δ(u)+δ(v)<n$ imply $uv\in E_\cap$. We prove that either every prescribed vertex belongs to a rainbow cycle of every length $4,\ldots,n$, or all members coincide with the balanced complete bipartite graph. The non-exceptional systems are also rainbow pancyclic. Under the stronger local cutoff $4n/3-1$, every vertex additionally lies on a rainbow triangle, yielding rainbow vertex-pancyclicity; the cutoff is sharp in the stated congruence class. The proofs use prescribed-color detours, root-preserving neighborhood separation, and a rigidity theorem for missing rooted lengths.

papers.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of planar graphs
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták [Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum colorings of planar graphs with respect to neighborhoods, \emph{Discrete Appl.\ Math.}\ \textbf{324} (2023) 80--92] conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no conflict-free colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a critical planar graph on $25$ vertices and $51$ edges that needs four colours, with a proof that can be checked by hand. Finally, we give an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

papers.title: A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: This article investigates random Dirichlet series within the framework of Hardy and mixed norm spaces of Dirichlet series. For randomization methods by sequences of non-constant independent and identically distributed random variables, we completely characterize when the random symbol space of the Hardy space $\mathscr{H}^p$ (respectively, the mixed norm space $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_α$) coincides with $\mathscr{H}^2$ (respectively, $\mathscr{H}^{2,q}_α$). We also obtain some integrability results when Dirichlet series belong to the corresponding random symbol spaces. The same methods also yield a complete characterization for mixed norm spaces on the unit disk in the range $0<q<4$, closing the gap between previously known necessary and sufficient conditions.

papers.title: Superdecomposable Incidence and Complete Path Algebras
papers.abstract: Generalizing the setting of the second author's work from 2007, we characterize quivers $Q$ for which the dual algebra $R$ of the path coalgebra of $Q$, equivalently the complete path algebra, has no nonzero uniform right ideals: this happens exactly when every vertex of $Q$ can reach a vertex emitting at least two distinct arrows. Equivalently, the injective hull $E(R)$ of the right regular module is superdecomposable. These conditions are also equivalent to the path coalgebra having no nonzero hollow factor modules as a left module over its dual algebra. We also characterize nonempty locally finite posets whose incidence algebras have superdecomposable injective hulls of their right regular modules: this happens exactly when no principal up-set is upward directed.

papers.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
papers.abstract: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

papers.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
papers.abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Schäfer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

papers.title: Tiling 3D Space by (Translates of) a Single Polycube is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. The same result holds if we also allow rotations and/or reflections. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Coefficient arithmetic and Mellin moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction
papers.abstract: We study the signs of logarithmic coefficients associated with the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. An explicit criterion involving a finite product determines whether all coefficients in an arithmetic progression are negative or both signs occur with positive natural density. On the sets $n=5^a m$, $5\nmid m$, negative coefficients occur with positive relative density $δ_a^-$ at every fixed $a$. If $m_a$ is the least such $m$, we prove that both $5^{-a}\log\log(1/δ_a^-)$ and $5^{-a}\log\log m_a$ tend to $5\logφ/(12e^γ)$, where $φ=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and $γ$ is Euler's constant. These are leading double-logarithmic asymptotics, obtained from classical results on additive and multiplicative functions. Coefficient formulas also give irrationality and nonvanishing, determine the poles and residues of generating functions for normalized Mellin moments, and imply that these generating functions are not D-finite. We conclude with applications to integrals involving zeta, Dirichlet $L$, and cusp-form $L$-functions.

papers.title: A Faithful Action of the Mapping Class Group $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ on the $(2g-1)$-Sphere
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ acts faithfully by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on a $(2g-1)$-sphere when $g \geq 3$ using equivariant blow-up and bi-orderability of the Torelli group.

papers.title: Compatible Bases and Actuator Scheduling
papers.abstract: We study a constrained basis-selection problem for an ordered block matrix $B=[ B_1\mid\cdots\mid B_n ].$ The successive tail matrices determine a nested family of column spaces, and we consider bases of representatives which are compatible with this induced flag. Our main linear-algebraic result shows that, among bases of representatives, compatibility with the entire flag is characterized by the intrinsic block quotas $r_k=w_k-w_{k+1}$, where $w_k$ is the rank of the $k$-th tail matrix. We then show that the same structure arises naturally in finite-horizon linear control. For the reachability matrix $[A^{N-1}G\mid \cdots\mid G]$, requiring every actuator to be used exactly once turns an actuator schedule into a representative system. Preservation of the complete reachability profile is then equivalent to compatibility with the tail-space flag. This correspondence leads to an exact depth-first search with a future-rank pruning criterion. For an explicit structured family and a fixed search ordering, the baseline search visits $3\cdot2^m+m-2$ nodes before the first solution, whereas future-rank pruning reduces this number to $3m+1$. Exact-arithmetic experiments reproduce these formulas for all tested instances.

papers.title: Ahlfors--Weill Extension, Asymptotically Conformal Curves and Epstein--Poincaré Surfaces
papers.abstract: The Ahlfors--Weill construction explicitly extends a univalent function $f$ with Schwarzian norm less than $1/2$ to a quasiconformal homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere, an extension that can be understood geometrically through Epstein surfaces. For asymptotically conformal curves, the uniformization map can be extended to a larger disk, and Loewner theory can be used to verify that this extension is quasiconformal. In this paper, we construct a local quasireflection with such an extension. Using this local quasireflection, we modify classical estimates of Ahlfors and show that domains bounded by asymptotically conformal curves have asymptotically similar hyperbolic and quasihyperbolic metrics. Furthermore, by combining these estimates with a geometric reinterpretation of the extension through Epstein surfaces, we show that the Epstein-Poincaré surfaces of the complementary domains are arbitrarily close to one another near the curve.

papers.title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
papers.abstract: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.

papers.title: Regularity of critical immersions for scale-invariant curvature energies in even dimensions
papers.abstract: For immersions of a closed $2h$-dimensional manifold $Σ$ into $\mathbb R^m$, we consider curvature energies that are invariant under ambient isometries and dilations, with the principal term $\int_Σ \big|\nabla^{(h-1)} \vec{\mathrm{I\!I}}\big|_g^2\,d\text{vol}_g$ and lower-order submanifold invariants. Following the four-dimensional approach developed in joint work with Bernard, Martino, and Rivière, we prove that every weak critical immersion in the natural Sobolev class $W^{h+1,2}$, whose induced metric and its inverse have $L^\infty$ coefficients, is real-analytic in harmonic coordinates. The proof combines geometric conservation laws, structural identities, and elliptic estimates with critical Sobolev coefficients to obtain Morrey decay and bootstrap to full regularity.

papers.title: Notions of equivalence among constant Yang--Baxter Operators: To $\infty$-Equivalence and Beyond
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in any higher-representation classification problem is to determine an appropriate notion of equivalence among representations. In ordinary representation theory we have the notion of isomorphism, but in general there may be several coherent choices for morphisms and then the question arises of the relationship between corresponding notions of equivalence. This question is already relevant in the classification of constant Yang--Baxter operators where gauge equivalence (i.e., local basis change) is comfortingly familiar, but is by no means canonical. In this paper we first review the equivalences used in recent advances in this field (through charge-conserving YBOs); we determine the relationships between them; and then develop a toolkit of theorems applicable for testing equivalence in practice. We use $\infty$-equivalence as the reference notion here: for $m\in\N$, $m$-equivalence denotes $n$-strand braid group representation equivalence for all $n \leq m$. This combines naturally with an appropriate variation of the ordinary Artin--Wedderburn Theorem. We show, for example, that for each dimension $N$ there is a finite $m(N)$ so that $m(N)$-equivalence implies $\infty$-equivalence, up to radical (but also show that the function $m(N)$ is unbounded). In principle proving $\infty$-equivalence requires providing an infinite sequence of intertwiners, so this reduces the burden significantly. For another example, we show that in dimension $2$ all bar one local family of solutions are charge-conserving up to radical and $\infty$-equivalence --- a characterisation relatively simple enough that it gives us a framework for addressing the major open classification problem in dimension $3$.

papers.title: A commuting operator self-test for exact entanglement embezzlement
papers.abstract: We show that the optimal commuting operator correlation for a variant of Coladangelo's two-player generalized nonlocal game, based on the embezzlement of entanglement, is a commuting operator self-test. Our result gives the first correlation self-test for an exact entanglement embezzlement protocol in the commuting operator framework. Because the unique optimal correlation necessitates the exact embezzlement of entanglement, the correlation is unrealizable using quantum tensor-product models, even if the local spaces are allowed to be infinite dimensional. Our proof relies on Harris' unique abstract state characterization of exact embezzlement of entanglement involving Cuntz algebras.

papers.title: VC-dimension of distance graphs in finite field geometries
papers.abstract: We study the VC-dimension of distance graphs of large subsets of vector spaces over finite fields. For $3\leq k\leq d$, we prove the distance graph of $E\subset \F_q^d$ has VC-dimension at least $k$ provided that $|E|>Cq^{\min(d-1,\frac{d+k-1}{2})}$. We also show that this exponent is sharp in the $k=d$ case.

papers.title: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
papers.abstract: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $θ= \Pr(N=1) \in (0, θ_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $θ$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.

papers.title: Polynomial Decay in Absorbing Continuous-Time Markov Chains
papers.abstract: Let $P(t)$ be the transition function of an absorbing continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space. We study asymptotic relations of the form $p_{ij}(t)\sim a_{ij} L(t)$, $t\to\infty$, where $L$ is independent of $i$ and $j$. We obtain general conditions under which the coefficient matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ has rank one and describe the resulting consequences for survival probabilities and conditional distributions. The analysis applies to both reducible and irreducible chains. We also construct an irreducible counterexample, based on a killed random walk on a homogeneous tree, for which a common asymptotic scale exists but the coefficient matrix has rank greater than one. This shows that irreducibility alone does not imply rank-one asymptotics. The results identify conditions under which fixed-state transition asymptotics determine the asymptotic behaviour of the entire transition function and clarify the limitations of such conclusions in the absence of additional structure.

papers.title: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
papers.abstract: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.

papers.title: Well-posedness for Wright--Fisher SPDEs with measurable drift
papers.abstract: We prove weak existence and uniqueness in law of $[0,1]$-valued solutions for a class of scalar stochastic heat equations with measurable drifts $b : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, driven by Wright--Fisher noise. The only assumptions we require on the drift are Borel-measurability, and the one-way inequalities $-Cu\leq b(u)\leq C(1-u)$ for some $C<\infty$, compatible with the necessary condition $b(1)\leq 0\leq b(0)$. These are vastly more general conditions than were previously available. Our proof relies on a stochastic duality between the solution of the stochastic heat equation, and a voting scheme running along the graph of a branching-coalescing particle system, generalising the class of drifts for which a dual process is available. Our results and their proof put the regularisation-by-noise result of Barnes, Mytnik and Sun, and its explanation, on a much more general footing.

papers.title: Asymptotic counting of integers with prime factors $p_{r^a s^b}$
papers.abstract: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime, and let $r,s\ge2$ be fixed multiplicatively independent integers. We count the integers up to $x$ whose prime factors all have the form $p_{r^a s^b}$ with integers $a,b\ge0$. Our asymptotic formula for this count has relative error $o(1)$ and is explicit down to the multiplicative constant. For $(r,s)=(2,3)$ these integers are the prime codes of the ordinals below $ω^{ω^2}$, so the formula settles that case of the counting problem of Vernaeve, Vindas and Weiermann.

papers.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
papers.abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-iωI)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

papers.title: An Adaptive Linesearch-free Method for Monotone Variational Inequalities under Local Lipschitz Continuity
papers.abstract: The forward-reflected-backward (FRB) splitting solves monotone inclusions involving the sum of a maximally monotone operator and a monotone Lipschitz continuous operator. Each iteration performs one resolvent step and one evaluation of the Lipschitz operator, together with a reflection term with coefficient equal to one that reuses the operator value from the previous iteration. We consider the setting where the maximally monotone operator is the subdifferential of a proper, closed, convex function. We identify the admissible range of constant reflection coefficients, namely all values larger than one half for a sufficiently small stepsize. We then propose a linesearch-free adaptive variant of FRB for locally Lipschitz continuous operators, in which both the stepsize and the reflection coefficient change across iterations. The stepsize is computed in closed form from a simple local Lipschitz estimate, without knowledge of a global Lipschitz constant, while keeping the iteration cost of FRB. The analysis of both methods relies on a new Lyapunov function that combines the distance to a solution, a residual, and a gap-related term. Alongside nonasymptotic rates, we derive explicit lower bounds on the generated stepsizes, and report numerical experiments on minimax problems, equilibrium models, and regularized regression.

papers.title: Resonant saddles, tangencies with small spheres, and the characteristic flow
papers.abstract: We study resonant Siegel saddles in $\C^2$, with eigenvalue ratio $-p/q$, where $p,q$ are coprime positive integers, through their position relative to small round spheres. An intrinsic invariant $k$, defined through a resonance index that measures approximate first integrals, equals the first resonant obstruction. For $k<\infty$, the maximal contact order with the linear foliation is $m=k(p+q)+1$, and suitably normalized charts give $2k$ tangency circles. We compute their transverse type: resonant terms cancel to first order, and Poincaré--Dulac normalization through degree $2m-1$ makes every contact a saddle, while weaker normalization can produce elliptic arcs and periodic characteristic orbits. For the exact model we describe the whole-sphere flow and the correspondence between its tangency circles and separatrix sectors. In arbitrary charts the characteristic return map near a separatrix circle realizes its holonomy, whose $p$-th iterate has, when $k<\infty$, multiplicity $kp+1$, with $kp$ attracting and $kp$ repelling petals. Classical rigidity of resonant holonomy then recovers the analytic saddle class from $C^1$ orbital equivalence near that circle. We also describe tangency loci for arbitrary nondegenerate germs by the numerical range and the leading orbital form.

papers.title: Open Inextensible Filaments in Planar Stokes Flow: Well-Posedness, Endpoint Asymptotics, and Straightening
papers.abstract: We study an inextensible open filament with free ends in a planar Stokes fluid. The system reduces to a third-order nonlocal curvature equation coupled to an elliptic equation for the tension. We prove local well-posedness for nearly critical initial data in supported Sobolev spaces $\widetilde H^s$, $-1/2<s\le0$, satisfying the arc-chord condition. For positive times, we prove improved Sobolev regularity and derive a $d^{3/2}$-type expansion at each free end using Wiener--Hopf factorization, where $d$ denotes the distance to that endpoint. We further prove global existence and exponential convergence to a straight filament for sufficiently small initial data and for finite-energy initial data satisfying $E(0)<π^2/4$. The finite-energy result follows from an energy identity and a geometric estimate relating the bending energy to the arc-chord constant. More generally, any finite-time breakdown must be accompanied by loss of the arc-chord condition, while every global solution either converges exponentially to a straight filament or has arc-chord constants tending to zero along a sequence of times tending to infinity.

papers.title: Conformal boundary rigidity for simple Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the conformal boundary rigidity problem for Finsler metrics on a bounded domain. We establish stability estimates for determining the conformal factors of simple Finsler metrics in the same conformal class from their boundary distance functions. Our results provide the Finslerian version of the well-known stability estimates for Riemannian metrics.

papers.title: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
papers.abstract: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.

papers.title: Transverse Analytic Envelopes and the Baum--Bott Rationality Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study holomorphic first integrals near singular leaves through transverse analytic envelopes. For diagonal actions these are normal toric quotients, and complete semiglobal integrability along singular orbits with independent support weights is equivalent to maximal resonance rank and finite monodromy. For commuting fields in convergent simultaneous Poincaré--Dulac normal form, induced derivations determine the first-integral algebra. Labelled quotients and logarithmic residues reconstruct weights at maximal rank; Grassmannians describe the ambiguity otherwise. Polynomial examples show losses invisible to prescribed finite jets. For the Baum--Bott rationality conjecture, we prove rationality and an explicit residue formula for smooth compact singular components with product charts and a common invertible semisimple transverse linear part of maximal resonance rank. Equivariant cohomology gives higher-degree vanishing for affine diagonal torus actions, including intersecting singular strata.

papers.title: Exceptional model structures and the induced extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: A Hovey triple $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{W})$ is {\it exceptional}, if $(\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F} \cap \mathcal{W})$ is not a Frobenius pair. One has a disjoint union $\{\text{Hovey triple}\} = \{\text{Hereditary Hovey triple}\} \ \dot\bigcup \ \{\text{Exceptional Hovey triple}\}$ \ $\dot\bigcup \ \{\text{non-hereditary and non-exceptional Hovey triple}\}.$ Exceptional Hovey triples appear widely. For a selfinjective Nakayama algebra $A= kC_n/J^t$, $A\mbox{-}{\rm mod}$ admits exceptional Hovey triples if and only if $\gcd (n, t) \ge 2$ and $t \geq 3$. Their homotopy categories reveal new phenomena. Nakaoka-Palu's Theorem implies that there is a triangulation on $\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}.$ It is proved that a Hovey triple in a weakly idempotent complete extriangulated category $(\mathcal A, \mathbb E, \mathfrak s)$ is exceptional if and only if the induced extriangulated structure $\bigl(\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}, \ \overline{\mathbb E}, \ \overline{\mathfrak s}\bigr)$ is not {\it canonically triangulated}. Between this extriangulated structure and the one arising from the triangulation, the intermediate extriangulated structures are in one-to-one correspondence with Serre subcategories of $\mathrm{fp}((\frac{\mathcal P(\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F)}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Ab})$.

papers.title: The $α$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $α>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(Ω)$. In the limit $α\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(Ω)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $Ω_2\subset Ω$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_α$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $Γ$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(Ω)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_α$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_α\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(Ω)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(α)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(α)$ upper bound is sharp.

papers.title: Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold
papers.abstract: We establish local existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system posed on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$ and initial conditions given by a nonzero constant magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ and arbitrary divergence-free velocity $v_0\in H^s$, in the range $(n+1)/2<s\le n/2+1$. The proof uses a Lagrangian wave--Hodge reformulation and exploits an Alfvén null--structure hidden in the pressure forcing. This work builds on Zhang \cite{Zhang2026} and provides a bridge from the Lagrangian theory to the Eulerian Cauchy problem. In particular, the constructed solutions are induced by a bi-Lipschitz and volume-preserving map.

papers.title: On the gonality of Kneser graphs
papers.abstract: The Kneser graphs $\text{KG}(n,k)$ are a classically studied family of graphs. One known invariant of graphs is gonality (also called divisorial gonality), which is the minimum degree of a rank 1 divisor on the graph. Using known bounds on gonality of simple, connected graphs, one may obtain that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is bounded above by $\binom{n-1}{k}$. In 2014, Harvey and Wood showed that the treewidth (a lower bound on gonality) for $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is $\binom{n-1}{k}-1$ for $n\geq 4k^2-3k+2$. In this paper, using scramble number, another lower bound on gonality, we improve this polynomial bound and show that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is exactly $\binom{n-1}{k}$ for $n\geq \frac{3k^2+k+2}{2}$, and conjecture an even stricter polynomial bound using the uniform edge scramble. We then extend our argument to the family of generalized Kneser Graphs, computing the scramble number and gonality using the same polynomial bound.

papers.title: A Structural Theory of Admissible Transitions in Biological Reaction Networks
papers.abstract: Biological reaction networks exhibit transient changes that cannot be understood from steady states or long-term persistence alone. We extend Chemical Organization Theory to transitions between species subsets, using stoichiometry and feasible reaction fluxes to characterize structurally admissible changes without specifying kinetic parameters. The framework distinguishes algebraic admissibility from feasibility constrained by reactant availability. We relate these transitions to reaction-based ordinary differential equations and identify an asymmetry: closure-building transitions are determined by network structure, whereas subsequent reductions can depend on the realized trajectory. Transitions to terminal organizations are characterized when the relevant species sets occur along that trajectory. An HIV-immune response model illustrates how a shared closure-building phase can precede different long-term outcomes. The framework connects continuous dynamics with discrete changes in species composition and supports structural analysis of transient pathways and organization formation in systems biology, while distinguishing structural admissibility from realization under particular kinetics.

papers.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linearly elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.title: On Samuels' Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $0\leqμ_1\leq\cdots\leqμ_n$ and let $λ>\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=μ_i$, and write $D_i := λ-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}μ_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<λ\right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{μ_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

papers.title: The Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem for odd wheels: Resolving a conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem, which asks for the maximum adjacency spectral radius over graphs with a fixed number of edges that forbid a prescribed subgraph. We settle an open conjecture due to Yu, Li and Peng for odd wheel graphs $W_{2k+1}$. A striking dichotomy appears in the extremal configurations: the forbidden-$W_5$ case and the general case $k\ge 3$ rely on identical stability and dense-core reductions but produce completely different extremal graphs. For sufficiently large size $m$, we derive sharp spectral inequalities and give complete characterizations for graphs achieving equality. Our approach combines the edge-spectral stability theorem with the dense-core method and residual-function analysis. Beyond solving the target conjecture, the developed framework provides a systematic approach for edge-spectral Turán problems and implies several known results for odd cycles, friendship graphs and odd fans. Directions for future research on edge-spectral supersaturation are also discussed.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices: Non-convexity and Geometry
papers.abstract: A real symmetric matrix is called $d$-locally positive semidefinite if all of its $d \times d$ principal submatrices are positive semidefinite. We investigate the spectral geometry of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices. The set of vectors of eigenvalues of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $n \times n$ is fully understood and known to be convex when $d \in \{1,n-1,n\}$ \cite{blekherman2022hyperbolic}.
